Overview
Designers of complex chips find many reasons to modify the netlist. Often these changes
come late in the design process where errors are very costly. Netlist changes are errorprone because the netlist is large, complex, unfamiliar, and hard to understand. Errors
such as changing the wrong gate or making a typo are common. The nECO module is
designed to solve this problem. It helps you to isolate the logic that needs to change in an
ECO window so you can easily modify the design. After the modification, you can commit
this change and nTrace and nSchema reflects the changes immediately. When you export
the changes to new HDL source files, comments are automatically added to the new HDL
files to keep the ECO history.

Overview

The nECO module provides the following capability:
* Dedicated ECO window to isolate logic that needs to be changed.

* Modify the connection between logic gates.
* Add/Delete logic gates.
* Undo/Redo.
* Commit the modification to reflect the change to source code and schematic.
* Write the modified netlist to new HDL files.
* Automatically add comments to the source code to keep the ECO change history.
* ECO utilities to create ports, change cell type, clone module, and move instances to a
different scope.

* Support freeze silicon mode and non-freeze silicon mode.

non-Freeze Silicon Mode

* Support Novas ECO script in Tcl and Avant! ECO script format for the change.

* Add/Delete buffers.
* Rename nets or instances.
* Manage the spare cells by cell number or instance name.

Terminology
ECO Window
This is the dedicated window for you to modify your netlist.
Library Cell
This is the most basic module in gate level netlist and is defined in the Verdi platform as a
symbol library.
Cell and Component
Instances of library cell.
Instance Pin
The pins of a component.

Dedicated ECO Window

Dedicated ECO Window
The ECO window is the main window of the nECO module. This window displays the
circuit in a flattened schematic style to isolate logic from other non-related circuits. You
can modify the design in this window. Any modification made in this window does not
take effect until the Commit Change command is invoked. After the Commit Change
command, the internal database of the Verdi platform is updated and the content in nTrace
and nSchema reflects the change immediately. You can verify whether the changes meet
the requirement.

1. You can select the components you want to modify in any nSchema window and
invoke the Tools -> New Schematic -> ECO Window command. The ECO window
opens and displays the selected components exactly the same as the display style in
the flattened window.

2. You can collect all the interesting components in a flattened window first and then

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
The ECO window acts like scratch paper. Any changes made in the ECO window does not
affect the real design until you commit the modification. Hence it is safe and local. Also if
you miss any components when you created the ECO window, you can incrementally drag
and drop them from other Verdi windows.

To avoid confusion, only one ECO window is allowed in the Verdi platform. If the ECO
window is opened, the commands to invoke ECO window are disabled.

Modify Connection in ECO Window
The instance pin is the basic unit to make changes in the ECO window. All the connection
modification actions are related to the instance pin. Also the connection status of the
instance pin is very important. You cannot connect a connected instance pin to another
net. An Xmark is displayed next to the instance pin if this instance pin is floating (not
connected). Also the View -> Fan In/Out Number command turns on the display of the
fan in/out number to provide more detailed connection information.

pin

instance

Cell Modification

ECO provides the following ways to modify the connection:

This command is used to make a connection between two objects. The connection can be
between:

* instance pin - instance pin

* instance pin - net

In both cases, at least one of the instance pins must be floating.

This command is very flexible, you can:
* Select two objects and invoke this command.
* Select one object, invoke this command, and then select another object.

Connect to Net
This command is used to connect the selected instance pin to the specified net. This is a
short cut to the make connection command.

Delete Connection
The delete connection command can be applied to an instance pin or a net. If applied to a
net, all the instance pins are disconnected from this net. If applied to an instance pin, the
instance pin are disconnected from the net it is connected.
Delete Connection

pin

instance

Cell Modification
In the ECO window, you can add cells to the design, delete cells from the design, or
replace a cell with a different type. The following commands facilitate cell modification.

Add Instance
This command allows you to add an instance from the cell library to this design. While
adding an instance, you must specify the scope you want to add the instance into. This
command lists all the scopes currently referenced in the ECO window for you to choose
from or you can type in another scope.

Delete Instance
This command deletes the selected instances from the design.

This command allows you to replace the selected instance with another cell type. The form
lists the possible candidates according to the pin name match result. You can choose to
list those cells with exactly the same pin name and pin count or those cells that have pins
that cover the selected cell.
If the Freeze Silicon Mode is turned on, the behavior of these commands are different. It
deals with the cells in the spare cell list.

Undo/Redo
Multiple levels of Undo/Redo are provided for you to undo/redo the action in the ECO
window.

All the editing you do in the ECO window does not take effect until you invoke the Commit
Change command. This command checks the connection and cell status in the current
ECO window and gives you a report to verify. Also it displays the default comment that is
added to the source code with date (by default) for this change. You can change it to your
preferred comment. Once you commit the form, it updates the changes to Verdi internal
knowledge database and you see the changes in other windows such as nTrace and
nSchema.

ECO

window

The nECO module provides Freeze Silicon Mode for the post layout ECO stage. In this
mode, the cells in the design are fixed. All the changes only impact the connection.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
To set this mode, you need to turn on the Freeze Silicon option on the Tools ->
Preferences -> Schematics page-> ECOpage -> Freeze Silicon page. When this option
is turned on, you can set the other options for the spare cell rules in the design.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
In Freeze Silicon Mode, all the cell modification commands deal with the cells in the
spare cell list. The Edit -> Spare Cell command in the ECO window is for you to create
the spare cell list. You can load the spare cell list from a file that may be prepared by you
or saved from a previous nECO session. You can also use naming rule matching to search

cell

spare

ECO Utilities

the spare cells. The content in the spare cell list varies with the modifications in the ECO
session. Also, you can save the final spare cell list to a file for future retrieval.

The biggest difference in Freeze Silicon Mode is that the cell modification commands
does not modify the cells in the design. Instead, they are dealing with the spare cell list.

Add Instance
This command lists all the instances available in the spare list for you to add. When an
instance is added from the spare list, this instance is deleted from the spare list.

Delete Instance
This command adds the deleted instance to the spare cell list.

This command only lists the cells in the spare cell list with the matched pin status. When
you replace the selected cell with another cell in the spare cell list, the replaced instance is
added to the spare cell list and the chosen cell is removed from the spare cell list.

The spare cell rule is applied to the new added spare cells.

ECO Utilities
In addition to the ECO window, the nECO module also provides some ECO utilities for you
to change your design hierarchy. Following are two utilities available:

Clone Module
A module may have several instantiations in the design. In some scenarios, you only want
to make a change to one or some instances of this module. For this case, you need to
clone these instances into different modules to make them distinct. Giving the module
name, this command lists all the instances for this module in this design and then you can
clone these instances according to your need.

title: Verification ContinuumTM

This command is for you to move an instance from one scope to another scope. You
select an instance in the schematic first then invoke Tools -> ECO Utility -> Change
Instance Scope command. While moving this instance to the specified scope, this

command automatically handles the connection and hierarchical port modification from

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Write the New Netlist to New HDL Files
When you have finished all the modifications by using the ECO window or an ECO utility,
you can write the new netlist to HDL files by choosing the File -> ECO -> Save ECO
Netlist command in the nTrace window. You can choose to save only those HDL files that
are changed in this ECO process or you can save all the HDL files starting from a scope.
This command does not override your original HDL files. Instead, it writes all the new HDL
files under the specified directory and keeps the original file names.

The content in the saved HDL files is the same as your original HDL files except for what
is modified. The comment specified when committing the change is added to the modified
part in the new HDL files. Also, you can use the File -> ECO -> ECO Report command to
generate a report for all the changes you made during this ECO session.
ECO Report

This feature supports both Freeze Silicon Mode and non-Freeze Silicon Mode.

Perform the following steps to use the nECO module:
1. Check whether your Verdi library is prepared and whether the NOVAS_LIBS and
NOVAS_LIBPATHS environment variables are set correctly.

The -ssz, -ssy and -ssv options of vericom or verdi must NOT be used
when compiling the gate-level design in nECO.
2. Invoke the Verdi platform to import your design.
3. Invoke nSchema to display the schematic.
4. If the design is in freeze silicon status:

title: Verification ContinuumTM

Enable the Freeze Silicon option on the Tools -> Preferences -> Schematics
page-> ECO page -> Freeze Silicon page.

Invoke the Tools -> ECO Utility -> Spare Cell command in nSchema to prepare
your spare cell list.

title: Verification ContinuumTM

5. Select the components you want to change in the schematic window and invoke the
nECO command to bring up the ECO window.

Steps to Use the nECO Module

8. After you have made all the changes, invoke the Commit Change command. You find

ECO Window

illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 1

nECO Frame

Frame Banner
The banner at the top of each nECO frame identifies the application and frame number
(such as <nECO:4>) and the operation mode (Non-Freeze Mode or Freeze Mode).

Chapter 2: User Interface
ECO Window

Pull-down Menu
A pull-down menu bar is located just below the frame banner. Each menu item contains
several commands that display when the menu is selected. The nECO module supports
the tear-off menu convention. This allows you to pull aside a frequently used menu on Unix
platforms and leave it open.

Mnemonic Key
The pull-down menus support Meta key invocation using mnemonics. The mnemonic for
each item is indicated by an underline. For example, to display the File -> Open menu
(meta -fo), click and hold the <Meta> key on the keyboard (the diamond key/<Alt> key on
Sun keyboards or the <Alt> key on Windows keyboards) and click the "f" key, then release
the <Meta> key and click the letter "o" key.

Bind Key
You can bind a command to either a keystroke or a mouse button. Once you have defined
bind keys, you can easily invoke commands with a keystroke or mouse click. For example,
the Source -> Active Annotation command can be invoked using the "x" key (the defined
bind key is the letter after the command in the menu).

Toolbar
A row of icons appears below the pull-down menu bar. These icons give you access to
frequently used commands for the current window.

Mouse Operation
The mouse is most often used to select objects by clicking the left mouse button. You can
select ranges of objects by dragging with the left button over the objects. You can also
select a range by using the <Shift> key along with clicking-left. To add or remove individual
objects to or from the selection, use the <Ctrl> key along with click-left.
The nECO module also makes use of drag-and-drop operation to move information from
one frame to another. You normally perform drag-and-drop by pressing the middle mouse
button to select the object, holding the button as you move the mouse to a new location,
then releasing the button to "drop" the object into a new location.

Chapter 2: User Interface
nECO Toolbar Commands

nECO Toolbar Commands
A row of icons appears below the pull-down menu bar. These icons provide access to
frequently used commands for the current window.
The available toolbar icons may be modified using one of the following methods:
* Enable/disable the icon category using the right-click menu option on the main window.
* Left-click to select the separator bar and then drag left or right to decrease or increase
the associated space. When the space is decreased such that some icons are no
longer visible, a double arrow (>>) symbol is displayed to the right of the category. Click
this symbol to display the hidden icons.
* Left-click and select the gray bar, then drag up or down to undock the category and
then move to a new location on the toolbar or the left/right/below of the window.
Available slots are highlighted with a blue dashed line.
* Define/modify/add toolbar icons and categories using the Tools -> Customize Menu/
Toolbar command.
Refer to the nECO chapter of the Verdi and Siloti Command Reference manual for details
on the available toolbar icons.

This chapter describes the basic functionality of the nECO module. As an example, the
tutorial uses a microprogrammed CPU design with gate-level source.

Before You Begin
Before you begin the tutorials, you (or your system manager) must have installed the
Verdi and Siloti systems as described in the accompanying Installation and System
Administration Guide.
The optional Novas-2008??-demo.tar.gz package must be installed (where
2008 corresponds to the year and ?? corresponds to the month).

Installation and Setup

Installation and Setup
You must also complete the following actions in order to set up the Verdi environment and
the files required for this tutorial:
1. Add the Verdi application (binary) to the search path and specify the search path to the
license file:
Refer to the Setting Up the Environment and Running the Software section in the
Installation and System Administration Guide for details.
2. Create a working directory:
% mkdir <working_dir>

3. All of the tutorial data resides in the$VERDI_HOME/demo directory. Make a copy of
these demo files in your working directory:
% cp -r $VERDI_HOME/demo <working_dir>

The tutorial uses the case in the $VERDI_HOME/demo/nECO directory. Make sure the
demo/nECO directory exists under your working directory.

This tutorial illustrates the nECO operations in non-freeze silicon mode. In this mode, you
have all the freedom to modify your design. This tutorial demonstrates how to insert a cell
in original design, and edit connections.
non-Freeze Silicon Mode

Import a Verilog Gate Design
1. Change the directory to <working_dir>/nECO/tutorial/gate. Then set the environment
variables for symbol libraries and execute the Verdi platform to import the sample CPU
design:
> setenv NOVAS_LIBPATHSNOVAS_LIBPATHS $VERDI_HOME/share/symlib/xx

where xx stands for the bit of your machine. It is either 32 or 64.
> setenv NOVAS_LIBSNOVAS_LIBS default_u

2. Invoke the Verdi platform:
> verdi -f run.f &

The Verdi platform opens and the gate level design is imported.

Appendix A: Novas ECO Script
To perform repetitive Engineering Change Order (ECO) changes in an easy and efficient
way, the nECO module provides a set of Novas ECO script commands, which are
programmed in the Tcl format. The ECO changes may be performed using both Novas
ECO script commands and all other standard Tcl functions.

This appendix consists of the following topics:
* Commands and Key Components
* Script File Format
* Loading the ECO Script Through Batch Mode
* Example

Commands and Key Components
This section describes two kinds of Novas ECO script commands and explains how to use
these script commands for the ECOs.

Novas ECO script commands are categorized as two types and are presented with
different prefixes. These two types are as follows:

* Commands with prefix _eco
prefix _eco

* Commands with prefix ECO
prefix ECO

The commands with prefix _eco must be included within the ECOBeginSession and
ECOEndSession commands. Each ECO session begins with the ECOBeginSession
command and ends with the ECOEndSession command. The ECOEndSession
command not only means an ECO session is ended; it also implies a commit action. The
nECOmodule does not commit the changes for the commands with the prefix _eco until it
encounters the ECOEndSession command. Multiple ECO sessions can exist in a script file;
however, nested ECO sessions are not allowed - an ECO session cannot be included in
another ECO session.
The commands with prefix ECO must not be included within the above ECO session.
These ECO commands perform the related ECO changes and imply an ECO commit
action at the same time.

Prior to using the Novas ECO script commands for ECOs, a script file in the Tcl format,
may be written with the provided Novas ECO commands. Since the Tcl format is adopted,
all other standard Tcl commands may also be used in this script file.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
After the script file is ready, an ECO may be performed by loading the file into the nECO
window using the File -> ECO -> Load ECO Script command from nTrace. After loading
the script file, use the Verdi standard functionality to verify the output of the ECO changes.
If the output result is correct, use the File -> ECO -> Save ECO Netlist command in
nTrace to save the ECO changed HDL files onto disk.

text:

scripts. The first line is the command syntax and the following lines in italics are examples
of the command.

These are not the nECO Tcl commands. Refer to the nECO chapter in the Verdi
and Siloti Tcl Reference for the complete list of Tcl commands.

"system.i_cpu1.i_ALUB.\\IXR_reg\[5\] "

[-delim delim]

Loading the ECO Script Through Batch Mode

Loading the ECO Script Through Batch Mode
If you already have an ECO script file, that is, novas.eco, you can load the ECO script file
in the batch mode using the following command:
verdi -f run.f -ecoScript novas.eco

A warning message is issued if the Verdi import design fails.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Example
The following example shows how to use Verdi provided Novas ECO script to perform
ECO changes.
# The original net list is
#
gate U282 is driving gate U253 via net n742
#
gate U284 is driving gate U254 via net n744
#
gate U286 is driving gate U255 via net n746
#
# The following Novas eco script will first perform an
# eco change for putting an inverter between above gates
# After eco, the net list will become
#
# U282 is driving eco_i_1 via net n742 and
#
eco_i_1 is driving U253 via net eco_n_1
# U284 is driving eco_i_2 via net n744 and
#
eco_i_2 is driving U254 via net eco_n_2
# U286 is driving eco_i_3 via net n746 and
#
eco_i_3 is driving U255 via net eco_n_3
#
# Then replace the gate U236 with cell type YCBUFP
#
ECOSessionBegin -comment "1st updated by Novas eco script"
for {set i 1} {$i < 4} {incr i 1} {
set net_id [expr 740 + $i * 2]
set inst_id [expr 252 + $i]
# add the inverter instance first
_ecoAddInst -master "IV" -inst "system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.eco_i_$i"
# connect the input pin of inverter
_ecoMakeConnection \
-instport "system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.eco_i_$i" "A" \
-signal "system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.n$net_id"
# delete the input connection of U25X
_ecoDeleteConnection -instport "system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.U$inst_id" "A"
# connect the output pin of inverter
_ecoMakeConnection -map " eco_n_$i" \
-instport "system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.eco_i_$i" "Z" \
"system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.U$inst_id" "A"

Example

}
# to replace the gate U236 with cell type YCBUFP
_ecoReplaceInst -master "YCBUFP" \
-inst "system.i_cpu.i_CCU.U236"
ECOSessionEnd
#
# The following Novas eco script will perform an eco change for
# moving gate U258 from scope system.i_cpu.i_CCU to scope
# system.i_cpu.i_ALU
#
ECOChangeInstScope -scope "system.i_cpu.i_ALUB" \
-inst "system.i_cpu.i_CCU.U258" \
-comment "2nd updated by Novas eco script"

Performance Analyzer Overview
The Verdi Performance Analyzer is an interactive graphical application that provides
graphical performance, and statistical and transaction analysis of protocol related data. It
provides a convenient way to measure the performance of protocols using protocol-related
transaction information that has been recorded in an FSDB (for example, from Synopsys
Verification IP, Custom Verification IP, or from emulation).
Performance Analyzer is based on Protocol Analyzer. It works as a feature of Protocol
Analyzer and provides protocol-oriented analysis, compliance checking, report generation,
and report comparison. In addition to accelerating the investigation of protocol behavior,
Performance Analyzer also defines several extendable interfaces and commands that can
be used to integrate Performance Analyzer to the regression system or other VIP tools.
Performance Analyzer is a protocol-aware platform that supports different protocols with
different versions. It also provides extendable interfaces to support new protocols. By
default, Performance Analyzer provides common performance metrics and report layouts.
VIP developers and end users can also define their own performance metrics and report
layouts for different protocols.
The following are the key features of Performance Analyzer:
* Protocol-aware platform: Performance Analyzer is a general protocol-aware
platform that supports different protocols with different versions. It provides extendable
interfaces to support new protocols.
* Performance metric customization: You can customize the performance metrics
for different protocols. In addition to the metric definition, Performance Analyzer also
provides convenient ways for you to manage and configure performance metrics.
* Performance report customization: Performance Analyzer uses WYSIWYG visual
designer and layout tools to create performance reports. You can easily add metrics
and UI controls using the drag-and-drop feature, change various properties of visual
component using a property editor, and apply compliance check rules.
* Graphical view: Performance Analyzer provides different types of charts and controls,
such as bar chart, pie chart, and line chart to display the performance data. Related
charts and controls can be grouped into the section control.

Chapter 1: Performance Analyzer Overview

* Multi format report: Performance reports can be exported in different formats, such as
PDF, HTML, and Excel file. You can also export the simulation performance data to a
CVS file, so that you can perform data analysis using Microsoft Excel.
* Batch mode capability: Most functions in Performance Analyzer can be run in the
non-GUI mode. You can call functions by typing the commands in the Console view.
Full batch mode capability can also be used in regression tests.
Figure 1

Performance Analyzer Use Model

Performance metric calculations are performed using the same transaction data that is
recorded during simulation for viewing in Verdi Transaction and Protocol Analyzer. Thus,
in order to calculate performance metrics for one or more VIP instances in the design,
FSDB dumping must be enabled for those instances using the same process that is used
to enable viewing and analysis of protocol-related data in Protocol Analyzer. Pre-defined
performance metrics are provided for select Synopsys VIP titles (AXI/ACE, AHB, DDR,
USB, Ethernet, and so on). Refer to the individual VIP documentation for details about
Verdi Performance Analyzer support.

Invoking Verdi Performance Analyzer
The Performance Analyzer application in the Verdi platform is used to measure the
performance of protocols and provides performance, statistical, and transaction analysis of
protocols.
To use Verdi Performance Analyzer, make sure that the
VerdiPerformanceAnalyzer license feature is available in the license server.
Verdi Performance Analyzer is invoked with the Tools -> Transaction Debug ->
Performance Analyzer command in the nTrace window as illustrated in the following
figure:
Figure 2

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Invoking Performance Analyzer From nTrace

The default layout of the Performance Analyzer window is illustrated in the Performance
Analyzer Default Layout. The Performance Analyzer window is divided into the following
panes:
* The left region contains the Hierarchy Tree pane that displays the instance hierarchy,
protocol metrics, and performance results.
* The middle region contains the Performance Report pane that displays the
performance report.
* The right region contains the Details pane that displays the details associated with the
selected metric result.
Figure 3

Performance Analyzer Default Layout

If there is a primary FSDB file, any newly-opened Performance Analyzer window
automatically opens the primary FSDB file; otherwise, the newly-opened Performance
Analyzer pane is empty. You can then open an FSDB file with the File -> Open command
icon.
or the Open FSDB File
The selection is synchronized between Performance Report pane, the Metrics tab, and the
Results tab. The Details tab shows metric results and constraint violations for the selected
metric.

Hierarchy Tree Pane
The Hierarchy Tree pane contains Hierarchy Tree Tab, Metrics Tab, and Results Tab.

Hierarchy Tree Tab
The Hierarchy Tree tab is used to display all VIP instances in the design. The hierarchy
is extracted from the FSDB file and is the same hierarchy that is displayed for the Protocol
Analyzer. However, only the instances are checkable. The hierarchy view is used to select
the instances for which performance metrics are to be calculated.
Figure 4

The Hierarchy Tree Tab

The following right-click commands are available in the Hierarchy Tree tab:
* Expand All: Expands all items.
* Collapse All: Collapses all items.
* Show in Result View: Shows the selected instance in the result view.

* Show Report: Evaluates the enabled performance metrics for the selected instances.
This displays the Performance Report.
* Show Report in New Window: Evaluates the enabled performance metrics for the
selected instances. This displays the Performance Report in a new Performance
Analyzer pane.
Only one Performance Report is displayed in the new Performance Analyzer pane. You
can open the Performance Report in a new window using the Show Report in New
Window command.
If instances from multiple protocols are selected for performance evaluation, only the
instances from the first protocol are used. A warning message appears to enable you to
view performance reports for other instances in the new Performance Analyzer pane.

Metrics Tab
The Metrics tab displays metrics and its associated constraints for all protocols in the
design. If there are multiple instances of the same protocol in the design, there is still only
one root node for that protocol. This tab allows you to enable/disable metrics, define/edit
custom metrics and constraints, or add/ change/remove metric constraints.
Figure 5

The Metrics Tab

For each protocol, the tree of performance metrics has the following two sub-nodes:
* One node for the instance performance metrics
* Another node for the multi-instance performance metrics.
The corresponding metrics appear as leaf-level tree nodes within each of these subnodes. Performance metrics can be enabled or disabled by clicking the check boxes in
the hierarchy tree. The check box for the instance folder and the protocol folder is used
to enable or disable all metrics in the folder.
Predefined metrics are differentiated from custom metrics by the icon of the metric name.
You cannot delete or edit predefined metrics.
Figure 6

Enable Performance Metrics by Clicking Check Box

The following right-click commands are available in the Metrics tab:
* Expand All: Expands all items.
* Collapse All: Collapses all items.
* Add Metric: Displays a dialog box for adding a custom metric.
* View Metric: Shows the details of the selected metric in the Metric dialog box.
* Edit Metric: Opens the Add/Edit Metric form in which you can edit a custom metric.
Only custom metrics can be edited. Predefined metrics cannot be edited, but they can
be copied with the Copy Metric command.
* Copy Metric: Displays a dialog box for copying the selected metric. All fields remain
the same with the selected metric except the metric name.
* Delete Metric: Deletes the selected metric.

* Set Chart: Displays a dialog box to set the chart option for the selected metric.
* Set Column Datatype: Sets the original data type and data unit for a selected column
of the metric.
* Save Configuration: Saves the current metric/constraint configuration into a Tcl file.
* Load Configuration: Loads a metric/constraint configuration from a Tcl file.
* Reset Constraint: Resets the constraints for the protocol of the selected metric. You
are prompted with a dialog box to confirm the operation.
* Reset Configuration: Resets both metrics and constraints for the protocol of the
selected metric. You are prompted with a dialog box to confirm the operation.
If the metric definition contains any syntax error, a warning message appears when you
attempt to create or modify the metric.
Any runtime errors associated with the metric definition, such as an incorrect table name
or column name, can only be detected when the metric is evaluated. This class of errors
are annotated in the Results tab.
Custom performance metrics can be defined with New Metric and Edit Metric right-click
commands. If one of these commands are invoked, the Add/Edit Metric form is opened.
As illustrated in the following figure, you can specify or modify the performance metric
definition:
Figure 7

The Add/Edit Metric Form

In the Metrics tab, double-click Min and Max columns of the metric to set minimum and
maximum constraint for that metric.

Figure 8

Set the Minimum/Maximum Constraint for a Metric

The Set Chart command is used to set the metric display chart option as illustrated in the
following figure:
Figure 9

Set Chart Type Form

The Set Chart command is used to set the metric display chart option as illustrated in the
following figure:
Figure 9

Set Chart Type Form

The following settings are used for each chart type:
* Chart Type
Bar chart: Shows the bar chart using the first column as the y-axis. The second
column as the x-axis.
Line chart: Shows the line chart using the first column as the y-axis. The second
column as the x-axis.

Pie chart: Shows the pie chart using the first column as the percentage of slice and
the second column as the slice tag (name).
Step chart: Shows the count changes on the x axis in the form of steps. This chart
uses the data from x and y axis to compute and form a range.
* Data
Use the same column as both x axis and y axis in the Data field to specify the
frequency.
* Customize Range
Customize the range, such as specify start, end, step, and function in the Customize
Range field.

Results Tab
The Results tab is a tree view that displays performance analysis results. The root folder
for the tree is the protocol name. This folder contains a sub-item that contains the results
of evaluating all multi-instance metrics and separate sub-items for each instance that was
evaluated.
The Results tab also shows the grouping information of the metrics. Groups are created
only in the Metrics tab. After you evaluate the report, the same grouping is applied to the
Results tab.
In addition,check boxes are present in the Results tab, These check boxes enable you to
select the metrics that you want to view. By default, all the metrics selected in the Metrics
tab are selected inside the Results tab. You need to de-select the metrics for the instances
for which you do not want to view the reports.

The following figure illustrates the Results tab:
Figure 10

The Results Tab

The next level in the tree hierarchy displays the individual metrics (instance or multiinstance) that are evaluated. Constraint violations are indicated with an alternate
background color for the violating metrics.
The Count column shows the number of results generated for the metric. If a runtime error
occurs when evaluating the metric, NA is shown. The tip tag provides details of the error.
Any metric that has constraint violations is highlighted in a following different color:
* purple for maximum constraint violations
* yellow for minimum constraint violations
* Red for both maximum and minimum constraint violations
Selections in the Results tab are synchronized automatically with the corresponding item
in the Results tab of the Performance Report pane. For example, if the trans_write_latency
metric is selected for instance2, the Results tab of the Performance Report pane scrolls
to the section for instance2. This highlights the chart for the trans_write_latency metric
automatically.

There are multiple scenarios to consider while displaying the information in the Results
tab and the results inside the Chart Section. Following are the different use cases with
examples:

The Results tab shows instance grouping. However, the Metrics tab shows
generic grouping. There is no option available to group metrics based on the
instance. The generic metrics grouping is applied inside each instance.
The following right-click commands are available in the Results tab:
* Expand All: Expands all items.
* Collapse All: Collapses all items.
* Show in Hier. Tree: Shows the selected instance in the Hierarchy Tree tab.
* Show in Metrics View: Shows the selected metric in the Metrics tab.
* Show Metric: It displays the metric definition as illustrated in the following figure:

* Save Configuration: Saves the current metric/constraint configuration into a Tcl file.
* Load Configuration: Loads a metric/constraint configuration from a Tcl file.
* Reset Configuration: Resets the configuration settings to default settings.
* Clear Instance Constraints: Clears the constraints for all the instances.
You can save or load configurations from the Metrics tab or the Results tab.
If there are errors while saving or loading the configuration file, these errors
are reported and the process is aborted.

Performance Report Pane
The Performance Report pane displays the performance report of the specified protocol.

Performance Report Pane
The Performance Report pane displays the performance report of the specified protocol.
After the performance evaluation is completed for the selected instances, a metric report is
generated and displayed in the Performance Report pane.
The multi-instance metrics are evaluated only once on all input instances. The instance
metrics are evaluated on every input instance. The performance report includes a
separate section for each input instance and a summary section for all input instances.
The instance section includes performance results for all instance performance metrics.
The summary section only includes performance results for multi-instance performance
metrics.
A performance metric can generate a result that has only one record or contains multiple
records. The result can also have only one column or can include multiple columns.

If a performance result has multiple columns, the first column is taken as the
value of the metric.
Figure 11

Performance Report

For a metric result with only one record, the result is shown as a label.
Figure 12

Result as Label

If there is a constraint violation for the metric, the result is shown in a different color.
Figure 13

Result in Different Color in Label

For a metric result with multiple records, the result is shown as either a bar chart or a line
chart. If there are constraints associated with the metric, the constraint values are also
displayed.
Use the middle button of mouse to scroll up/down to zoom in/out the chart. Drag left and
right to move the chart left and right. The scroll bar below the chart is also used to move
the chart left/right and zoom in and out.
For line and bar charts, some of the details may be lost if there are too many items in the
visible range. Since some of the date items may overlap, zoom in the chart for several
times makes all items in the desired sub-range visible.

Figure 14

Line Chart of the Performance Report

Figure 15

Bar Chart of the Performance Report

For pie charts, only the top ten items are shown in separate slices. Other items are
grouped as one item with the name "others".
The selection of the pie chart does not synchronize to Details and Results pane.
This is because the pie chart shows the ratio of various performance analysis
results. This does not have one-to-one mapping with the results displayed in
Details and Results pane.

Figure 16

Pie Chart of the Performance Report

Points to Note for Step Chart
* The chart configuration is applied to the specified metrics. In other words, if a metric
configuration is changed, then it is applied to all instances of the same metric. The
chart configurations are saved when the session is saved. These are restored when
the session is loaded.
When the CSV format report is saved, the raw data is saved into the CSV file.
When the HTML format report is saved, the same chart setting is used that is
present when the report is displayed.

* Constraint violation highlighting is not supported for charts with split range.
* Constraints are always applied to the y axis. If you change the y axis column, the
current constraint is removed.

The Performance Report pane includes a section for every input instance and a summary

The following right-click commands are available in the Performance Report pane:

Details Pane
For any metric result selected in the Performance Report pane, result data and any other
data specified in the SQL metric expression is shown in the Details pane. Metric constraint
violations are also annotated in this pane.

Details Tab
The Details tab displays the result data for any metric result selected in the Performance
Report pane. This includes all the data selected in the SQL metric expression as illustrated
in the following figure:
Figure 21

The Details Tab

The first column of the table displays the metric result. Any vector result that has multiple
records is shown as a bar chart in the HTML report .The values from the first column as
the data for the y-axis. The values from the second column as the data for the x-axis.
If the table includes a column of transaction IDs, that information is used in the debugging
process. For example, the transaction IDs are used to trace the ultimate cause for
constraint violations. They are also used to synchronize selections with Performance
Analyzer, Transaction and Protocol Analyzer, and Transaction Table View panes. In
addition, the records that include transaction IDs are dragged and dropped to another
pane to be viewed.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Usage Summary
To execute performance analysis using Verdi Performance Analyzer, perform the following
steps:
1. Open the Performance Analyzer pane.
2. Open an FSDB file. Alternatively, use the primary FSDB file if it is loaded automatically.
3. Select instances from the Hierarchy Tree pane.
4. Set performance metrics and constraints (disable or enable metrics; set constraint
values).
5. Perform the metric evaluation with New Metric and Edit Metric commands.
6. Open the performance report.
7. Check the performance report and debug any constraint violations.
8. Save the performance report in the HTML or the CSV format.
9. Open the HTML report in a web browser and review the report. Open the CSV report in
Excel or OpenOffice, show charts for the data and review the report.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Shortcut Keys
The following table shows the available shortcut keys for the mentioned actions:
Action

Shortcut Key

File -> Save Report

Shift+S

Shift+L

Loading Metrics From Multiple Directories
The Performance Analyzer allows you to load the metrics from both PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH
and DESIGNWARE_HOME directories. You can define few metrics inside the
PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH directory and remaining metrics in the DESIGNWARE_HOME directory.

Sorting and Filtering

Use Cases
* Case1 - Only the PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH environment variable is set..
In this case, there are no changes and the tool processes metric files from the
PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH directory.
* Case2 - Only theDESIGNWARE_HOME environment variable is set.
In this case, there are no changes and the tool processes metric files from the
DESIGNWARE_HOME directory.
* Case:3 Both PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH and DESIGNWARE_HOME environment variables
are set.
In this case, the tool firstly loads metric files from the DESIGNWARE_HOME directory. The
tool then scans the PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH directory and overrides the metrics that exist
in both paths.
The PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH environment variable allows you to specify multiple
paths. However, the multiple paths must define metrics for different protocols;
the specification of multiple protocols is not supported. If multiple occurrences
of the same protocol are encountered, the first path in the list takes precedence.

Sorting and Filtering
You can sort metric result values present in the Details tab, the Results tab, and the
Metrics tab in ascending or descending order. Click the head of a column to sort the metric
result by that column in ascending or descending order.

By default, sorting is not applied to the results displayed in the columns.
You can also filter metric result values present in the Details tab using the filtering
mechanism that works on the specified metric result on the specified instance. For
example, if the Details view displays results for metrics "M" for instance "I", the filtering
mechanism is applied only to the current result (metrics "M" on instance "I"); it is not
applied to the results of metric "M" on other instances.
To apply the filtering mechanism, right-click the head of a column in the Details tab, as
illustrated in the following figure:

Sorting and Filtering

The following right-click options are available:
* Show All Values
Clears all the filters applied on a column.
* Filter by Value
Applies filter based on the values present in a column. A list of values is displayed,
which can be selected as per your preference.

Note that a maximum of ten values are displayed in the list menu for a column. If more
than ten different values exist for a column, the Filter by Value option is disabled for
that column.
* Filter By Range
Applies a filter for a range of values. A range filter is applied only for numeric value
columns.

* Customize

Sorting and Filtering

For a customized filter, you can specify the operator and the value of the filter, as
illustrated in the following figure:

The following operators are supported for string and numeric values:
>= greater and equal
<= less and equal
== equal
!= not equal
~= wildcard match, for example *abc*
You can apply filters on both the Details view and the Performance Report view. After
the filter is applied, only the data items which pass the filter criteria are displayed in the
Details view and the Performance Report view.
For single row metric results, all filters are disabled.
* Clear all Filters
Clears all the applied filters.
If you save a session for the current report, sorting, filtering, and color
settings are saved in the session and are restored when you reload the
session. However, if a new performance report is generated, all the filter
settings are cleared for the new report.

Search Field for Hier. Tree, Metrics, and Results Tabs

Search Field for Hier. Tree, Metrics, and Results Tabs
To easily find data in Performance Analyzer, a search field is available in the Hier. Tree
tab, the Metrics tab, and the Results tab. The search field is hidden by default, however,
you can enable the search field using one of the following methods:

Spliting the Data for the x Axis Into Ranges
You can split the data for the x axis into fixed length ranges/intervals and display only a
statistical result item for every range in the report.
This feature is supported only for numeric x values.
Use the following options to specify how the x axis must be split:
* The range width (required).
* The start of the range (optional; by default the minimal x value).

* The end of the range (optional; by default the maximal x value).
* Out-of-range data: ignore or take as one interval (optional; by default out-of-range data
is ignored).

Aggregate Functions for Range
If the x axis is split into intervals, for every interval there may be multiple data items;
however, only one data item is displayed for every interval. This value is a statistical result
of all the data items in the interval that can be specified by the users.
The following aggregate functions are supported:
* cnt
It is used to show the count of data items in an interval.
* max
It is used to show the maximum value of the data items in an interval.
* min
It is used to show the minimum value of the data items in an interval.
* sum
It is used to show the sum of all the data items in an interval.
* avg
It is used to show the average value of all the data items in an interval.

Tcl Command
To set the chart configuration for metrics, use the following Tcl command:
perfSetChart -protocol <protocol_name>
-x <column_for_x_axis>
-y <column_for_y_axis>
-start <start_of_range>
-end <end_of_range>
-step <width_of_interval>
-aggr <aggregate_function>
-other <ignore_or_include_data_out_of_range>
-type <chart_type>

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Defining Groups for Metrics

Points to Note
* The chart configuration is applied to the specified metrics. In other words, if a metric
configuration is changed, then it is applied to all instances of the same metric. The
chart configurations are saved when the session is saved and are restored when the
session is loaded.
When the CSV format report is saved, the raw data is saved into the CSV file.
When the HTML format report is saved, the same chart setting is used that is
present when the report is displayed.
* Constraint violation highlighting is not supported for charts with split range.
* Constraints are always applied to the y axis. If you change the y axis column, the
current constraint is removed.

Defining Groups for Metrics
The Metrics tab in the Hierarchy Tree pane of Performance Analyzer displays the metrics
for all protocols in the design. It allows you to enable and disable metrics. Each protocol
node has two sub-nodes: Instance and Multiple Instances. The corresponding metrics
appear as leaf-level tree nodes within each of these sub-nodes. However, as the number
of metrics increases, it becomes difficult to enable or disable each metric individually.
Performance Analyzer provides you the capability to group together the metrics with
specific meaning (with some rules). This allows you to enable or disable metrics based on
groups.

Defining Groups
There are no explicit rules for metrics that can automatically separate metrics into several
groups.
You need to add or define groups manually using the perfGroup Tcl command. The
syntax of the perfGroup command is as follows:
perfGroup -protocol <protocol_name>
-create <group_name>
//support hierarchical group
name

To delete a group, use the following Tcl command:
perfGroup -protocol <protocol_name>
-delete <group_name>
//support hierarchical group
name

Defining Groups for Metrics

Points to Note
* A group only acts on metrics level. Instance and Multiple Instances sub-nodes have
their own metric groups for each protocol.
* Once the groups are created, they cannot be modified.
* A group has a hierarchical structure. All the commands related to groups must use the
full hierarchical name.
* The name of a group in each level only supports a-z, A-Z, and 0-9 characters. The dot
'.' character is used to separate the group hierarchy.
* You can either create a simple group, such as bandwidth, or a hierarchical group, such
as latency.read.

Adding Metrics to Groups
After the groups are created, you can adjust the hierarchy of the metrics by moving the
metrics to related groups. You can move any metric (whether in another groups or not)
to a specific group, or move the metric out of a group to related Instance and Multiple
Instances sub-nodes.
To add a metric to a group, use the following Tcl command:
perfGroup -protocol protocol_name
-group group_name
-add metric_name

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
To remove a metric from a group, use the following tcl command:
perfGroup -protocol protocol_name
-group group_name
-remove metric_name

Enabling and Disabling Groups
You can enable/disable multiple metrics by enabling/disabling the group containing the
specific metrics. You can use either of the following methods to enable/disable a group:

Using Tcl Commands
To enable a group, use the following command:
perfEnableMetric -protocol <protocol_name>
-group <group_name>
-enable

To disable a group, use the following command:
perfEnableMetric -protocol <protocol_name>
-group <group_name>
-disable

Using the GUI Mode
The Verdi GUI mode supports enabling and disabling groups through the check-box
displayed next to the group's folder in the Metrics tab of Performance Analyzer. To enable
a group, select the check box next to the respective group folder and to disable a group,
deselect the check box next to the group folder. This is illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 25

Enabling/Disabling Groups

If the group folder is empty, the enable operation cannot be performed.

The columns in metric results display data type and data unit.
The following types of data types are supported:
* Time
The time unit includes fsdb (time unit specified in the FSDB file), fs, ps, ns, us, ms, and
s.

The default time unit is fsdb. The time unit is global for the Performance Analyzer view.
All the columns of the FSDB time datatype share the unit in the same Performance
Analyzer view.
* Data
The data unit includes Byte, KB, MB, GB, and TB. There is no default data unit and you
must specify an original unit for data type. You can set the display unit for data type in
the Details view.
* Bandwidth
The bandwidth data type is a compound type and its unit is <data unit>/ <time
unit>. There is no default bandwidth unit and you must specify an original unit for the
bandwidth type. You can set the display unit for the bandwidth type in the Details view.
* User-Defined Type
The user-defined data types do not support unit translation. You need to specify a unit
string for user-defined types.

Setting the Original Data Type and Data Unit
You can set the original data type and data unit for a column before the performance
report is generated by either using the perfSetColumnType Tcl command or using the
GUI mode. This setting cannot be changed after the report generation.

Tcl Command
Use the following Tcl command to set the original data type and data unit for metric
columns:
perfSetColumnType -protocol <protocol_name>
-column <column_to_be_set>
-type <type_string> // column type
-unit <unit_string> // column unit

title: Verification ContinuumTM

GUI Mode
To set the original data type and data unit for a column in the GUI mode, perform the
following steps:
1. In the Metrics tab, select an instance and click the Set Column Datatype right-click
option to open the Set Column Type and Unit dialog box.

2. In this dialog box, select the column for which you want to specify data type and data
unit in the Column field. Select Type and Unit in the respective fields and click Apply.

The specified data type and data unit for the column is displayed in the Details view and
Report view after you regenerate the report.
In the Details view, the data unit is displayed in the header section of the list view, as
illustrated in the following figure:

In the Reports view, the data unit is displayed in the axis label as illustrated in the following
figure:

Data type and unit settings are associated with a metric. In other words, if the
data type is set for the column of a metric, that setting is applied to all instances
of the same metric and column. If the original data type or unit is changed for a
metric, the change takes effect when the next performance report is generated.
Data type and unit configurations are saved during session saving. These
configurations can be restored during session loading.

Setting the Display Unit
You can set the display unit for a performance report by either using the perfColumnUnit
Tcl command or using the GUI mode. The display unit setting only changes the display
unit of a column. The datatype of the column does not change. This setting is applied to
the performance report immediately.

Tcl Command
Use the following Tcl command to set the display unit for metric columns:
perfColumnUnit -protocol <protocol_name>
-column <column_to_be_set>
-type <type_string> // column type
-unit <unit_string> // set the column display unit as the
given unit string
-instance <instance_to_be_set> // optional, to apply the
setting to the specified instance, all instances are not specified

GUI Mode
To set the display unit for a column (data or bandwidth columns) in the GUI mode, perform
the following steps:
1. Select a column in the Details view. Right-click Set Display Unit option to open the Set
Display Unit dialog box.

2. The Set Display Unit form opens. In this form. Select the unit to be displayed for the
column and click Apply.

If the display unit is changed for a column, the change takes effect immediately on the
current performance report, however, the display unit setting is not retained when the
report is generated again. Additionally, the filter on that column is removed.
If the display unit is changed for the y axis column, the constraint value remains the same
and is compared with the value in the original unit. In the chart, the constraint line is
adjusted according to the new display unit.
For both CSV and HTML format reports, the display unit setting is not used; the
original type and unit is used in the saved report.

Synchronization Between Performance Analyzer and nWave Windows

Once you enable synchronization (as explained above), markers are added inside the
nWave window at the location that corresponds to the value of the time that is associated
with the item selected inside the Details tab of Performance Analyzer.
Synchronization can only be performed for metrics whose results include time columns.
Note that some metrics include only a single time in their results, while other metrics might
contain two or more time columns.
* If there is only one time column, then only one marker is drawn inside the nWave
window. For example, if the time of the selected row is 1000, then a marker is drawn at
time 1000 inside the waveform viewer using a marker whose name is the same as the
time column name.
* If the metrics contains two time columns, then two markers are drawn inside the
waveform viewer with the two values matching those of the two time columns.
For example, if the metric has two time columns (called request_time and
response_time), and the value of request_time is 1000 and the value of
response_time is 3500, then the request_time marker is drawn at time 1000 and the
response_time marker is drawn at time 3500 inside the waveform viewer.
The Details tab does not allow multiple selections manually. Certain metrics that use the
rate function contain values that are calculated using multiple events. For these values,
all the events are highlighted when you select the value in the chart. In this case, the tool
shows two markers inside the waveform viewer, which indicates the time of the first event
as the start prefix column name and the end prefix column name as the last event in the
list. The tool auto-detects the time column(s) to facilitate synchronization. If a metric does
not contain any time columns, then there is no synchronization between Performance
Analyzer and nWave windows for those metrics. The selection synchronization icon
does not have any impact on nWave and Performance Analyzer when enabled or
disabled.
If there are more than two time columns, the values of the first two columns
whose name ends with time are used to add markers in the nWave window.

Limitations
The following limitations apply to the synchronization functionality in Performance
Analyzer:
* You cannot enable Performance Analyzer and nWave windows synchronization and
TNPA and nWave window synchronization at the same time. If you have enabled any
one of these synchronizations and attempt to synchronize the other window, then a
dialog box appears asking if you want to switch between the two synchronization types.

Cross-Instance Relationship

If you select the Yes option, the synchronization is switched from one to another.
If you select the No option, then the current synchronization remains.
For example, if you have already enabled synchronization between Performance
Analyzer and nWave, and then attempts to synchronize from TNPA to the same
nWave window, the Question dialog box appears that shows the message - Do you
want switch synchronization from Performance Analyzer and Waveform to TNPA and
Waveform?. Based on your choice, the synchronization is enabled accordingly.

Cross-Instance Relationship
Some performance analysis needs to be measured from transactions across multiple VIP
instances. For example, the analysis may cover Initiator (master) - Target (slave) pairs.
This requires a way to associate the master transaction(s) with the corresponding slave
transaction(s).
As the parent-child relationship can be used to associate transactions within one VIP
instance, the predecessor-successor relationship is used to associate transactions across
different VIP instances.
In addition, the master/slave cross-instance performance analysis metrics is built based on
predecessor-successor relations. The predecessor-successor relation is added by the VIP.
It is assumed that for the same master-slave pair, there are three different scenarios of the
predecessor-successor relations:
* One predecessor to one successor
* One predecessor to many successors
* Many predecessors to one successor
When the performance analysis metrics are written, the SQL query statement only
references the predecessor or successor when it is single and unique.
In other words, for the following three scenarios,

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
successors
* Many predecessors to one successor
When the performance analysis metrics are written, the SQL query statement only
references the predecessor or successor when it is single and unique.
In other words, for the following three scenarios,
* One Predecessor to one successor - The SQL statement can query either predecessor
or successor.
* One predecessor to many successors - The SQL statement can only query the
predecessor.
* Many predecessors to one successor - The SQL statement can only query the
successor.

Cross-Instance Relationship

Many predecessors to many successors scenario is not supported.
When translating the FSDB file streams into SQL tables, Verdi Performance Analyzer
provides the following two extra columns:
* The pred_event column - Records the single unique predecessor.
* The succ_event column - Records the single unique successor.
When a transaction has 0 or more than 1 predecessors, its pred_event entry is null.
When a transaction has 0 or more than 1 successors, its succ_event entry is null.
This is illustrated in the following figure:

In a SQL query statement, pred_event and succ_event can be used to link two
transactions.
If transaction A is the single unique predecessor of transaction B, B.pred_event =
A.event are used.
If transaction B is the single unique successor of transaction A, A.succ_event = B.event
is used.
Following is an example of a metric:
perfCreateMetric -protocol "AMBA_SVT AXI_SVT"
-name "cinst_concurrent_write_response_count"
-type "multi_instance"
-definition {SELECT COUNT(*) AS
concurrent_write_response_count
FROM $inst__Bus_Activity AS activity_resp,
$inst__Transaction AS axi_transaction
WHERE axi_transaction.type_path =
'Transaction.Write'
AND activity_resp.type_path =
'WRESP.WRESP'
AND activity_resp.pred_event =
axi_transaction.event }
-description "Multiple slaves are trying to send BRESP
to the same master in B channel."

Support for Instance-Based Constraints
The Performance Analyzer allows you to set constraints for each performance metric on
an instance-by-instance basis. You can define minimum and maximum constraints for the
instances of the selected metrics in Min and Max columns of Results tab. This allows you
to set the constraints before the results are shown in the Results tab.
Note that,
* If you set the Min/Max constraint in the Metrics tab, it is applied to all the selected
instances.
* If you set the Min/Max constraint in the Results tab for a single instance (or multiple
instances) for a metric (or multiple metrics), the constraint settings in the Metrics tab
are overridden by the value(s) specified in the Results tab.

and moves the window down if there is availability of space in the window to arrange it
down. If there is no space, then Verdi tabs to the current window.

summary related metrics are controlled by the Tcl command in the metric definition file.

space.

perfColumnFiltering -protocol "protocol_name" -name \

Specify the protocol name.

Specify the metric name.
-instance

Specify the instance name.

Specify the column that needs to be hidden in the detail tree.

Specify to get back the hidden column.

perfConfigDetails -protocol "AMBA_SVT AXI_SVT" -name
axi_trans_read_latency -instance "env.axi_system_env.master_0" \

Improving Debug Messages for SQL Flow

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Improving Debug Messages for SQL Flow
It is difficult to debug the SQL flow in the tool. To solve this problem, tool debug messaging
has been enhanced for all the SQL/NO SQL errors written out in a separate log file and
this log file is stored with other Verdi logs.
The errors are captured and categorized with the unique code.
The following is the log path:
./verdiLog/verdi_perf_err.log

The following are the error examples:
* [SQL_ATTR_NOT_FOUND_ERROR] -> This error is flagged in the log file under this
category if any attribute is missing in SQL schema. This error can be resolved by hitting
"Resolved Attribute action".
For example, [SQL_ATTR_NOT_FOUND_ERROR] has no such column:
ace_transaction.total_byte_count in SQL
* [SQL_GEN_ERROR]-> Any generic SQL error is flagged in the log file under this
category. This error can be resolved as per the description given for the error.
For example, [SQL_GEN_ERROR] has no such table:
env.axi_passive_system_env.master_0_ace_trans_read_latency in SQL
This log contains all the errors occurred during the analysis.

Following is the use model for this feature:

Use Model
The red error icon, as shown in the following figure, is added to the metric node if the error
is of type No Attribute Found (NAF). You can right click on metric to get the RMB menu
and click on the action Resolve missing Attribute Errors. After regenerating the report
errors are resolved.
If the error is not resolvable then those attributes are the dumped part of ./verdiLog/
verdi_perf_err.log under macro (PERF_FSDB_MISSING_ATTR_LIST) file for user

Invalid attributes are not resolvable.

Resolving Missing Attributes

You need to create a json file for all the resolved attributes. Json file can be copied to
the path $PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH/performance/metrics/. This path is used for future
reference.

Batch Mode Operation
This chapter discusses about the batch mode support available for Verdi Performance
Analyzer in the following sections:
* Batch Mode Use Model
* Batch Mode Tool
* Batch Mode Commands

Batch Mode Use Model
The Performance Analyzer application in Verdi offers the functionality to calculate
performance metrics as a batch operation. This allows you to include performance
measurement and validation in a regression (or a similar automated validation)
environment. You can calculate performance metrics and check those metrics against
desired minimum or maximum constraint values.
Considering the highest level, the batch mode use model comprises of the following three
steps:
1. Write the command files [optional].
2. Execute the verdi_perf command to process the command files and generate one or
more performance reports.
3. Review the reports in a web browser or in Microsoft Excel.
The structure of the command file enables the evaluation of multiple performance metrics
for different sets of instances with only a single invocation of the Performance Analyzer.
This can increase the overall efficiency of the flow, as illustrated in the following figure:

Batch Mode Tool

Batch Mode Tool
Performance Analyzer in Verdi comprises of an in-built wrapper that encapsulates the
required capabilities into an easy-to-use batch mode tool. The basic environment in which
this tool can be used is illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 41

Batch Mode Tool Environment

The wrapper has three types of input data and one type of output data.
It can be invoked using the following command:
verdi_perf -fsdb/-f
-instance/-i
[ -start/-s <start_time> ]
[ -end/-s <end_time> ]

Batch Mode Tool
[
[
[
[

-cmd/-c <list_of_command_files> ]
-output/-o <ouput_file_name> ]
-format/-m <output_file_format> ]
-session/-n <session_saving_option> ]

-fsdb/-f

The -fsdb or the -f option specifies the FSDB file to be processed. The FSDB file is
the output of a simulation that contains all the protocol-related simulation data that is
required to perform the desired performance metric calculations. This means that FSDB
dumping must have been enabled for all VIP instances of interest. The FSDB file needs to
be specified either through the -fsdb option or in the command file specified by the -cmd
option.
-instance/-i

The -instance or the -i option specifies the instances on which the performance
evaluation is done. The instance needs to be specified either through the -instance
option or in the command file specified by the -cmd option.
-start/-s

The -start or the -s option specifies the start time for performance evaluation.
-end/-e

The -end or the -e option specifies the end time for performance evaluation.
-cmd/-c

The -cmd or the -c option specifies a list of one or more command files to be processed.
These command files can contain Tcl commands. You can use these commands to define
custom performance metrics. They can also enable or disable performance metrics. You
can set or clear constraint values, perform metric calculations, and specify the location and
type of results to produce.
-output/-o

The -output or the -o option specifies the name of the output file.
-format/-m

The -format or the -m option specifies the format of the output file: html for HTML format,
and csv for CSV format.
-session/-n

Batch Mode Tool

The -session or the -n option specifies the condition/option to save the current session.
The saved session can later be opened in the Performance Analyzer GUI.
The various options to save a session are as follows:
* on - Save the session always.
* off - Never save the session.
* fail - Save the session if there is any constraint violation.
The default option to save a session is fail.

Protocol Extensions
The Protocol Extensions defined for the Verdi Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
also apply to the Verdi Performance Analyzer. They are present at the same location
as pre-defined performance metrics. In addition to the Synopsys VIPs that are
located in the DESIGNWARE_HOME directory, any directories that are specified using the
PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH environment variable are also analyzed for protocol definitions and
any associated pre-defined performance metric definitions.

Batch Mode Processing Flow
The following two flows exist for batch mode processing:
1. Write the operations in a TCL command file, and specify the TCL command through
the -cmd/-c option.
2. Use other command line options to specify the FSDB file, instances, and so on.
The -cmd/-c command line option is mutually exclusive with other
command line options. You need to choose to use either the command file
or the command line options, but not both.
If no command files are specified, the Verdi Performance Analyzer applies the pre-defined
performance metrics to the VIP instances found in the design. It produces a report using
the default output format, which is CSV.
If the command file is specified, the command file can contain one or more of the TCL
commands mentioned in Batch Mode Commands section.

file:

text:
Aggregate Performance Analysis
Verdi Performance Analyzer can also generate an aggregate performance analysis report
for all the FSDB files generated from multiple simulation runs for the same design. For
multiple FSDB files, the performance analysis report includes results for the merged
data from all the FSDB files and results for data from every single FSDB file. Therefore,
you can get a summary of performance results for all runs and also the statistical result
distribution/difference among every FSDB file.
This chapter explains about how to generate and view an aggregate performance analyzer
report in the following sections:
* Prerequisites
* Generating Aggregate Performance Analysis Report
* verdi_perf Utility
* Viewing Aggregate Performance Analysis Report in GUI
* Examples to Demonstrate Merged Results for Multiple FSDB Files

Prerequisites
The following are the prerequisites for aggregate performance analysis:
* Each FSDB file generated by a regression or by multiple runs must have a unique
identifier. This can be used by Verdi to organize, indicate, add or remove the test
results associated with a specific test. The FSDB full path (generated from the tests) is
used as the unique identifier.
* The FSDB files generated from different tests must have similar VIP instantiation
hierarchies. This merges the performance analysis results.
Some FSDB files may contain more instance hierarchies, while some may have
fewer instance hierarchies. However, only the results from the same VIP instantiation
hierarchy path are merged.

Generating Aggregate Performance Analysis Report

Generating Aggregate Performance Analysis Report
To generate an aggregate performance analysis report, perform the following steps:
1. Generate the result database (in Batch Mode)
Execute the verdi_perf command to initialize a result database (that is. a directory)
to save the performance results, and configure the metrics and constraints for the
performance analysis on multiple results.
Performance analysis on multiple test results share the same metrics and
constraints configuration.
2. Add or remove FSDB files to/from the database (in Batch Mode)
Run simulations for multiple tests, with Protocol Analyzer dumping enabled to dump the
FSDB file with protocol data. After each test, execute the verdi_perf command to run
performance analysis on the generated FSDB file.
The result is saved in the result database directory.
If there are constraints violations, the verdi_perf command issues error messages.
The FSDB file can be deleted after the file has been added to the result database;
aggregate results will not be affected.
In many regression systems, multiple tests are run at the same time. The verdi_perf
command can also run in parallel to analyze the dynamically generated FSDB files and
write the results to the result database.
You can also execute the verdi_perf command to override or remove an existing
analysis result from the result database.
3. Generate and view the aggregate performance analysis report (in Batch Mode)
a. Execute the verdi_perf command with -db/-d, -format/m, and -output/-o
options to generate HTML or CSV format analysis results.
b. View the report in a web browser (HTML format) or in an excel sheet (CSV format).
You can also view the aggregate performance report in Verdi GUI mode.
For details, see Viewing Aggregate Performance Analysis Report in GUI.

The following is an example to generate an aggregate performance analysis report using a
configuration file:
1. In the first phase, an empty database directory needs to be created with the specified
protocol, instances, and configurations. This is an example to generate multiple FSDB
file result database for the svt_axi protocol with the preceding configuration file as
follows:
verdi_perf -protocol "amba_svt axi_svt" -cmd axi.cfg -db axi.dbdir

2. In the second phase, with the created empty result database directory (axi.dbdir),
execute the verdi_perf command multiple times (in parallel, if desired) to analyze the
performance of the FSDB files (generated from each test) into the result database.
verdi_perf -add axi01.fsdb -db axi.dbdir
verdi_perf -add axi02.fsdb -db axi.dbdir

You can remove an FSDB file from the database as follows:
verdi_perf -remove axi02.fsdb -db axi.dbdir

verdi_perf Utility

3. In the third phase, with the created result database directory, and FSDB files added
into the database, use the verdi_perf command to generate an HTML or a CSV
format report.
verdi_perf -db axi.dbdir -format html -output axi_html
verdi_perf -db axi.dbdir -format csv -output axi.csv

verdi_perf Utility
Verdi Performance Analyzer comprises of an in-built wrapper which encapsulates the
required capabilities into an easy-to-use batch mode tool. It can be invoked using the
verdi_perf utility to generate an aggregate performance analysis report.
Following is the list of valid options for generating an aggregate performance report:
verdi_perf
[

[

-instance/-i
-protocol/-p <protocol> ]
-cmd/-c <config_file_name> ]
-db/-d <database_name>]
-add/-a <fsdb_name> ]
-remove/-r <fsdb_name> ]
-force/-w <fsdb_name> ]
-output/-o <ouput_file_name> ]
-format/-m <output_file_format> ]

-instance/-i

The -instance or the -i option specifies the instances and scopes on which the
performance evaluation is done. The instance needs to be specified either through the
-instance option or in the command file specified by the -cmd option. The value of an
instance is a list of nodes where a node could be an instance or a scope.
-protocol/-p <protocol>

The -protocol or the -p option specifies the protocol to be processed for performance
evaluation. All the instances for the specified protocol are evaluated. This option is
required for database initialization.
-cmd/-c

The -cmd or the -c option specifies the metrics/constraints configuration file. The
configuration file syntax and format is the same as the one used for single FSDB file
processing. For example, the Tcl command for adding or changing metrics or setting
constraints could be added into the configuration file.
-db/-d <database_name>

verdi_perf Utility

The -db or the -d option specifies the name of the result database directory. This option
is mandatory for generating an aggregate performance report. If this option is not added,
Performance Analyzer enters the single FSDB mode.
-info

The -info option shows information about the specified aggregate database. The
information includes a global environment, which contains the FSDB file list, protocol, and
instance names. If the number of FSDB files is more than sixteen, only the first sixteen file
paths are displayed in the output. The output format is as follows:
General information for dbdir: <dbdir>
Protocol: "<protocol>"
Instance: <instance>
Number of instances: n
<instance1>
<instance2>
Number of fsdb files: n
<fil1>
<file2>
-add/-a <fsdb_name>

The -add or the -a option adds the specified FSDB file into the database.
-remove/-r <fsdb_name>

The -remove or the -r option removes the specified FSDB file from the database.
If neither -add nor -remove option is added, and either -instance or -cmd
option is specified, the verdi_perf command performs database initialization.
The -add and the -remove options can not be added at the same time in the
command.
-force/-w <fsdb_name>

The -force or the -w option overwrites the FSDB file with the same name in the database.
-output/-o

The -output or the -o option specifies the name of the output file. This is an optional
parameter.
-format/-m

The -format or the -m option specifies the format of the output file: html for HTML format,
and csv for CSV format. This is an optional parameter.
