For UVM-1.1d, compile with the vlogan utility and elaborate the design using the following
commands:
%> vlogan -sverilog -timescale=1ns/1ns -ntb_opts uvm
%> vlogan -sverilog -ntb_opts uvm +incdir+../sv ubus_tb_top.sv
%> vcs -debug_access+all -ntb_opts uvm ubus_tb_top

See README.txt and Makefile.vcs files in the following directory for the 1.1d example
details:
$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm/lib/examples/integrated/ubus_evdp_ntb_u
um/examples

For UVM-1.2, compile with the vlogan utility and elaborate the design using the following
commands:
%>vlogan -sverilog -timescale=1ns/1ns -ntb_opts uvm-1.2
%>vlogan -sverilog -ntb_opts uvm-1.2 +incdir+../sv ubus_tb_top.sv
%>vcs -debug_access+all -ntb_opts uvm-1.2 ubus_tb_top

Transaction begin_time
You are allowed to specify the transaction begin_time. If the begin_time is not specified,
simulator will set the begin_time equal to current simulation time while creating the
transaction..
If the VCS compile option +define+UVM_VERDI_FORCE_BEGIN_TR_TIME is added,
simulator will ignore user specified begin_time and will use current simulation time as the
begin_time of the transaction while creating all transactions.
It is suggested to use Verdi T-2022.06, 21.09-SP2-2 or later versions, for the feature of
Transaction begin_time.
If you are using Verdi T-21.09-SP2-1 version, the default behavior is different and is
described as follows:
The begin_tr () function is used to indicate that the transaction is started. When Verdi
recorder is enabled in the UVM, the begin_time argument of begin_tr () is forced to
use the simulator time.
The transaction begin_time specified by the user is accepted only when the following two
conditions are met:
1. Add compiler directive, +define+UVM_VERDI_NOT_FORCE_BEGIN_TR_TIME
2. When you do not use the UVM Verdi recorder.
Otherwise, you will be forced to use the current simulator time as the begin_time for the
transaction.
If the Verdi recorder is used and enabled, the specified begin_time in the
begin_tr() function call will not work.
If you are using Verdi S-2021.09-SP2 and before versions, the default behavior is different
and is described as follows:
* UVM 1.1d or IEEE libraries: If begin_time is specified, the specified begin_time is
used. Otherwise, current simulation time is used.
* UVM 1.2 library: In this case, begin_time is forced to use current simulation time.

For advanced users, a PLI task-based API (application programming interface) with a
SystemVerilog wrapper is provided. These users require recording different or more data
than the Verdi-modified libraries provide. The API dumps transactions to an FSDB file

through the FSDB dumper. In addition, a C5 function-based API dumps transactions to an
FSDB file through the FSDB writer. SystemC6 and SCV function-based APIs (SC-API and
SCV-API) are also provided to dump transactions to an FSDB file.
Verdi also provides corresponding C and Tcl APIs to dump the transaction data into FSDB.
For details, see VC APPS Native Programming Interface (NPI) User Guide.
The following sections describe the PLI task-based API usage and provide examples for
reference:
* Stream Tasks
* Transaction Tasks
* Transaction/Relation Tasks
* Miscellaneous Tasks
* Simple API Example
* Rules
* Coding Style for API
You can configure the dumper to dump all the transaction data into a specified FSDB that
is separate from the signal based FSDB.
The FSDB dumper provides the following two ways to specify the transaction FSDB:
* Set the environment variable: FSDB_TRANS_FILE. For example, the command setenv
FSDB_TRANS_FILE xxx creates xxx.fsdb.
* Specify the option in the simulator command line: +fsdb_trans_file+. For example,
the command simv +fsdb_trans_file+yyy creates yyy.fsdb.
You can use this environment variable or command line option when you want to dump
transaction and signal data into separate FSDB files.
* Transaction based FDSB does not support $fsdbAutoSwitchDumpFile.
* Use the Transaction Debug features described in the subsequent chapters.
They help you recognize the transactions and messages in the novas.fsdb
transaction-based FSDB file.
The PLI system tasks include the following categories: Stream, Transaction, Transaction/
Relation, and miscellaneous tasks. For details, see Stream Tasks, Transaction Tasks,
Transaction/Relation Tasks, and Miscellaneous Tasks. To get better performance
in the Verdi platform with version 2014.12, refer to the Coding Style section for the
recommended coding style.

The data type of stream id and transaction id are both longint types.

Stream Tasks
The following tables describe the Stream Task API usage and provide examples for
reference.
stream_id $fsdbTrans_create_stream_begin

$fsdbTrans_create_stream_begin(string stream_fullname[,
string option]);

Creates a stream and returns stream_id with the longint type. If the
returned value is 0, it indicates that something is wrong and the stream
cannot be created.

stream_fullname Specifies the full hierarchy name of a stream. Use the . character as a
delimiter. For example, top.sub.s is placed into the top/sub hierarchy
and named s.

["+fsdbfile+filename"]

Specifies the output FSDB file name.
If this option and the +fsdbfile+filename runtime option are used
simultaneously, the FSDB file is overwritten by the file specified in
the +fsdbfile+filename runtime option.

void $fsdbTrans_define_attribute

$fsdbTrans_define_attribute(stream_id sid, attribute_var[,
string option]);

Use this task to define the dense attribute. This task must be called
after the $fsdbTrans_create_stream_begin task and before the
$fsdbTrans_create_stream_end task, and can be called multiple times.

sid

Specifies the stream id it belongs to.

attribute_var

The attribute template. The name and data type of attribute_var
is used as the name and the data type of the predefined attribute.
For example, if addr is declared as int addr, and is used as
attribute_var, the attribute name would be addr and the data type
would be int.

For example, if addr is declared as int addr, and is used as

["+name+attrname"]

["+radix+bin"] ["+radix+oct"] ["+radix+dec"] ["+radix+hex"]

["+default_value"]

Specifies a new attribute name to replace the name of attribute_var
as the attribute name.
Specifies the default radix.

Specifies a default value to store for the default attribute.

void $fsdbTrans_add_stream_attribute

$fsdbTrans_add_stream_attribute(stream_id sid,
attribute_var[, string option]);

Use this task to add attribute for the specified stream. This task must be
called after the $fsdbTrans_create_stream_begin task and before the
$fsdbTrans_create_stream_end task, and can be called multiple times.

sid

Specifies the stream ID it belongs to.

attribute_var

The attribute template. Name, data type, and value of attribute_var
is used as the name, data type, and value of the added attribute. For
example, if addr is declared as int addr = 'h1234, and is used as
attribute_var, the attribute name would be addr, the data type would
be "int", and the attribute value would be 'h1234.

["+name+attrname"]

Specifies a new attribute name to replace the name of attribute_var
as the attribute name.

void $fsdbTrans_create_stream_end

$fsdbTrans_create_stream_end(stream_id sid);

Ends the stream creation. Only after this task is called, the stream is
completely created and ready to add transactions.

sid

Specifies the stream ID.

Transaction Tasks
The following tables describe the Transaction Task API usage and provide examples for
reference.
trans_id $fsdbTrans_begin

$fsdbTrans_begin(stream_id sid, string trans_type);

Creates a transaction and returns a transaction ID with longint type.
Use transaction_id to create transaction details or add relationship
between transactions. If the returned value is 0, it indicates that
something is wrong and the transaction cannot be created.

sid

Specifies the stream ID it belongs to.

trans_type

Specifies the transaction type. The Transaction Debug windows use
different representations (GUI symbols) for each type. trans_type :=
["+type+message"] ["+type+action"] ["+type+group"]
["+type+transaction"]

void $fsdbTrans_set_label

$fsdbTrans_set_label(trans_id tid, string label);

Sets the label name of a transaction. This task is only applicable before
invoking the $fsdbTrans_end task.

tid

Specifies the transaction.

label

Specifies a new label.

void $fsdbTrans_add_attribute

$fsdbTrans_add_attribute(trans_id tid, attribute_var[,
string option]);

Adds an attribute into the tid transaction. If you predefined the attribute
name and data type when creating streams, a dense attribute is added.
Otherwise, a sparse attribute is added. This task is only applicable
before invoking the $fsdbTrans_end task.

tid

Specifies the transaction.

attribute_var

The attribute template. Name, data type, and value of attribute_var
is used as name, data type, and value of the added attribute. For
example, if addr is declared as int addr = 'h1234, and is used as
attribute_var, the attribute name would be addr, the data type would
be int, and the attribute value would be 'h1234
.

["+name+attrname"]

["+radix+bin"] ["+radix+oct"] ["+radix+dec"] ["+radix+hex"]

["+expect", expect_value]

Specifies a new attribute name.
Specifies the default radix.

Specifies an expected value for this attribute. The type of the expected
value must be the same as the type of attribute_var. Otherwise, a
warning is reported.

void $fsdbTrans_add_tag

$fsdbTrans_add_tag(trans_id tid, string tag);

Add a tag to a transaction. Multiple tags can be added to a transaction.
This task is only applicable before invoking the $fsdbTrans_end task.

tid

Specifies the transaction ID.

tag

Specifies a new tag

void $fsdbTrans_end

$fsdbTrans_end(trans_id tid);

Ends a transaction.

tid

Specifies the transaction.

Transaction/Relation Tasks
The following tables describe the Transaction/Relation Task API usage and provide
examples for reference.
void $fsdbTrans_add_relation

$fsdbTrans_add_relation(string rel_name, trans_id master,
trans_id slave);

Adds the relationship between two transactions. This task can be called
either before or after the transaction is ended.

rel_name

Specifies the relationship name. The Transaction Debug windows use
different representations for each predefined relation.
rel_name := ["parent_child"] ["belong_to"] ["succ_pred"]
["annotate_to"] or user-defined

master, slave

Based on the relation being added, master and slave should be as
mentioned in the table below.

rel_name

master

slave

parent_child

parent

child

belong_to

group

member

succ_pred

predecessor

successor

annotate_to

annotator

annotatee

Miscellaneous Tasks
The following tables describe the Miscellaneous Task API usage and provide examples for
reference.
void $fsdbTrans_add_scope_attribute

$fsdbTrans_add_scope_attribute(string scope_fullname,
attribute_var[, string option]);

Adds an attribute for a scope of transactions. If the specified scope does
not exist, the scope is created.

scope_fullname

Specifies the scope with the full hierarchy name. Use the . character as
the delimiter.

attribute_var

Specifies the attribute.

["+fsdbfile+filename"]

["+name+attrname"]

Specifies a file name.

Specifies a new attribute name.

error_state $fsdbTrans_get_error_code

$fsdbTrans_get_error_code();

Returns the error (execution) state of the task with the prefix
$fsdbTrans_ occurring right before it.

error_state

The data type of return value is an integer type:
0: when the task is successful
1: when the task completes with some warning messages
2: when the task fails with some errors

text:
For additional information or documentation on VC APPS Protocol Analyzer, see VC Apps
Protocol Analyzer User Guide.
Verdi also provides corresponding C and Tcl APIs to dump the protocol related transaction
data from custom VIP into FSDB. For details, see VC APPS Native Programming Interface
(NPI) User Guide.

Using Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer lets you view different types of simulation data in a
single application window. These include VIP transactions, protocol transactions, and
UVM transactions or messages. This helps you debug testbench simulation data more
efficiently.
The Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window provides a software-oriented waveformlike view (compared to the hardware hierarchical view in the nTrace window) for testbench
debugging. The waveform view supports new transaction types and the virtual streams
that are recognized transactions from different streams. The Transaction and Protocol
Analyzer window can be used to debug and analyze transactions and their temporal
activity by the time and stream axes.
The Unified Transaction Browser Mode is applicable for using Verdi Transaction and
Protocol Analyzer, which helps you to view different types of simulation data including
VIP transactions, protocol transactions, and UVM transactions or messages in a single
application window. The following sections describe the usage of Transaction and Protocol
Analyzer in Unified Transaction Browser Mode:
* Invoking Transaction Debug ModeI
* Invoking Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
* Importing an FSDB to the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window
* Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window Overview
* Preference Options
* Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Operations
* Interlinking Between Transactions and Signals
* Connecting nWave and Transaction and Protocol Analyzer

Invoking Transaction Debug ModeI

Invoking Transaction Debug ModeI
The recommended flow to browse the abstract data with the Transaction Debug solution
is:
1. Start the Verdi platform with the whole system, including the design and testbench.
%> verdi <options> &

2. Click the Work Modes icon in the Welcome Page, select the Transaction Debug
Mode option, and then press the Go to Work button.
Figure 2

Selecting Transaction Debug Work Mode

Or use the -workMode command line option directly to invoke Verdi in Transaction
Debug mode:
%> verdi -workMode transactionDebug <options> &

The Transaction Debug mode opens the original nTrace windows and all the necessary
Transaction Debug windows for you to debug the Verilog/SystemVerilog system at a
higher level of abstraction. Alternatively, each of the Transaction Debug windows can
be manually opened using the Tools menu in the nTrace main window.
The Transaction Debug panes are displayed in the main window by default. As with other
panes in the Verdi platform, the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer, the Transaction Table
View, and the Transaction Relation Navigator panes can also be docked or undocked, or

Invoking Transaction and Protocol Analyzer

dragged and dropped to other parts of the main window. The main window is shown in the
following figure:
Figure 3

Invoking Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
You can invoke Transaction and Protocol Analyzer using the Tools -> Transaction Debug
-> Transaction and Protocol Analyzer menu command in nTrace.
You can also invoke Transaction and Protocol Analyzer using the following menu
commands:
* Tools -> Transaction Debug -> Transaction and Protocol Analyzer command in the
Verdi main window.
* Tools -> New Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window command in the
Transaction Table View window.
* Tools -> New Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window command in the tRelation
Window.
* Window -> Connect Transaction and Protocol Analyzer and nWave command in
the nWave Window.

One Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window can only open one FSDB file.

The Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window can display all the supported transaction
data types (For details, see Chapter Using Data Types in Transaction Debug).
The default layout of the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window is as follows:
* The left region contains the Hierarchy Tree pane
* The middle region contains Stream pane and Transaction pane
* The right region contains the Value pane

Hierarchy Tree Pane
The Hierarchy Tree pane contains three tabs: Hier. Tree, Quick Filter, and Protocols tab.
You can switch between the tabs by clicking the tab labels. After importing an FSDB file, if
the Hierarchy Tree pane is not visible, invoke the Show/Hide Hier. Tree Area command
by clicking the

button to view the Hierarchy Tree pane.

Hier. Tree Tab Behavior for Non-VIP (UVM) Transactions
If the FSDB file contains Non-VIP (UVM) transactions related data, the Hier. Tree tab in
the Hierarchy Tree pane shows the hierarchy tree as illustrated in the following figure:

Adding Non-VIP Streams and Scopes to the Transaction Pane
To add non-VIP (UVM) streams to the Transaction pane, double-click the required stream
in the Hier. Tree tab, or click the Add Stream to Display right-click option (for streams), or
click the Add All Streams to Display
icon in the toolbar.

To add non-VIP (UVM) scopes (with all the streams under the scope) to the Transaction
pane, click the Add All Streams To Display right-click option.
Newly-added streams are displayed at the bottom of the Transaction pane based on the
insertion order.
Adding Duplicate Streams
To add duplicate streams into the Transaction pane, double click the required non-VIP
stream or click Add All Streams To Display or Add Stream to Display right-click options.
Duplicate streams are added at the end of the Transaction pane based on the insertion
order.
Drag and Drop
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer provides the capability to drag and drop a stream from
the project Hier. Tree to other widgets or from other widgets to the project Hier. Tree.
Dragging and dropping duplicate streams is not supported and dragging and dropping a
stream/scope into the same hierarchy tree in the same frame is not supported.

Hier. Tree Tab Behavior for VIP Transactions
If the FSDB file contains VIP transactions related data, the Hier. Tree tab in the Hierarchy
Tree pane looks as illustrated in the following figure:

Adding VIP Streams and Scopes to the Transaction Pane
The Hier. Tree pane in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer displays a check box next
to the VIP streams and scopes. If the loaded FSDB file has only VIP streams, then the
$trans_root top scope would also have a check box.
To add the VIP streams and scopes to the Transaction pane, select the check box
respective to the VIP stream and scope in the Hier. Tree pane.

To remove the VIP streams and scopes from the Transaction pane, uncheck the check box
respective to the VIP stream and scope in the Hier. Tree pane.
Alternatively, you can also select the Add Stream to Display or Add All Streams to
Display right-click options, or click the Add All Streams to Display
icon in the toolbar.
Adding Duplicate Streams
Adding duplicate streams is not supported for VIP streams.
Drag and Drop
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer provides the capability to drag and drop a stream from
the project Hier. Tree to other widgets or from other widgets to the project Hier. Tree.
To add a VIP stream/scope to the Transaction pane, drag and drop the stream/scope from
the project Hier. Tree to the Transaction pane. The check box next to the stream/scope in
the Hier. Tree tab changes to a checked state.
Deleting the Selected Transaction Type
To remove the unwanted transactions of a similar type from the Transaction pane, rightclick a transaction and click Remove all 'xxx' objects right-click option ('xxx' signifies the
display text of the object). This option removes all the objects of the selected stream and
its associated streams.
This feature is applicable only for the selected object of the type VIP stream.

Error Indications in Hier. Tree
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer marks erroneous transactions/messages in the Hier
Tree to enable you to view only those transactions /messages that are causing errors.
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer displays the streams having error(s) with red-colored

exclamatory icon on top of the original icon in the Hier. Tree. The ToolTip also displays the
error type for the selected scope/stream. This is illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 7

Error Indications in Hier. Tree

If a stream has an error, then the stream and its parent scope gets marked with an
exclamatory error icon. This helps you to identify a stream when the corresponding stream
or scope is in a collapsed state.
The transaction display also highlights the transactions/messages having error with the
red-color
icon.
You can also select the has_errors() function as the search expression in the Search
dialog in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer to search all the transactions having expected
field value mismatch errors or error messages and display those in the Search Results
view.

Save Streams
The configured streams can be saved using the File -> Save Stream command with the
file_name.rc naming. The content of the saved file contains the data path of the FSDB file,
zoom ratio, time range, and stream/group list, but it does not include virtual streams and
runtime signals. You can restore the save file using the File -> Restore Stream command
without opening the FSDB file first.

command in the right-click command menu to trace the class definition in the source code
frame of the transaction.

platform, and

Stream Pane Behavior for VIP Streams and Scopes
The FSDB file generated by the VIP contains streams grouped with channels, columns,
and instances. The Stream pane in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer displays
connections between channels, columns, and instances name. This makes it easier to
identify channels, columns, and instances that belong to each other.
The following figure illustrates the dev_agent instance name connecting to Transfer,
Transaction, Packet, Link_Item, LFPS_Signalling, and LTSSM Packet columns. Here,
Link_Item and LFPS_Signalling column names are connecting to Rx and Tx channels.

Points to Note
* For instances whose first stream row and column have channels - the stream row
heights are increased automatically to display the newly added instance and column
names.
* The height of the above stream rows automatically increase only if the application
default height is not changed. In case you have already executed vertical zoom in/out
actions, the stream uses the application default height and displays the name.
* If you change the Stream pane width by dragging on the splitter using a mouse action,
then newly added VIP instance or column names are displayed horizontally as compact
as possible; otherwise, a scrollbar is added if available.
* If any of the newly added instance names or column name having channels cannot
be displayed on top of the channel name, then the maximum width required to draw a
column/instance is used for all other columns/instances as well.
* On selecting the Full Stream Name option in the View menu command, the instance
name in the Stream pane displays the full path of the instance; there is no change in
the display text for other columns or channels.

Stream Pane Behavior for Non-VIP Streams and Scopes
The FSDB file containing Non-VIP (UVM) transactions does not display groupings for
channels, columns, or instances in the Stream pane.
You can move the streams up/down in the Stream pane by dragging and dropping the
stream to the required position.
You can also create virtual streams for FSDB file containing UVM transactions. For details,
see Creating Virtual Streams.

Transaction Pane Behavior for VIP Transactions
If the FSDB file contains VIP transactions, the Transaction pane in Transaction and
Protocol Analyzer displays the transactions based on the default colors defined in the
protocol definition files of VIPs. Additionally, it displays common text and additional text
(predefined by the VIP) next to each of the transactions.
The common text is displayed only if the Detail Transaction Information
option in the View menu is not selected.
As illustrated in the following figure, in the Stream pane, all the RADDR stream
transactions have the common text as Read_Addr and SNOOP_Transaction stream
transactions have a common display text as SNOOP (highlighted in green color in the
figure).

As illustrated in the figure,
* For RADDR stream type transactions, coherent_xact_type:"MAKEUNIQUE" is the
additional text displayed below the common text. Here, coherent_xact_type is the
attribute name and MAKEUNIQUE is the value of the attribute for that transaction.
* For SNOOP_Transaction stream type transactions, snoop_xact_type:"READONCE" is
the additional text displayed below the common text. Here, snoop_xact_type is the
attribute name and READONCE is the value of the attribute for that transaction.

Points to Note
* By default, the attribute value is displayed in the Transaction pane. If the View ->
Display Attribute Name menu command is selected, then the attribute name is
displayed along with its value.
* If the newly added stream in the Transaction pane has predefined fields defined by
the VIP, then height of the stream is increased automatically to display the additional
text of a transaction. So, you can see both common text and additional text for all such
transactions.
* When adding a stream to the Transaction pane, the height of the stream automatically
increases only if the application default height is not changed. In case you have already
executed vertical zoom in/out actions, the stream uses the application default height.
Common text and additional text are displayed according to the available height.
* In case of adding virtual streams having both VIP/UVM type transactions to the
Transaction pane,
VIP type transactions contain common text and additional text.
UVM type transactions display text continues to show the value of a top attribute
present in the Details tab.

* Changes in the order of the configuration dialog attribute makes display text changes
only for UVM type transactions.
* When collapsing the channels/columns using the icon for the first time, the height of
the new stream is the same as the first stream row height. However, on collapsing a
channel/column from second time onwards, the stream uses the previous stream row
height which is available at the time of previous expand.
* When expanding the channels/columns using the icon, the height of the new
channel/column rows are the same as the channel/columns rows which were available
at the time of collapse.

Points to Note
* The names and the values of the checked attributes are displayed below the common
text based on the order shown in the Details tab.
* On checking an attribute in the Details tab, height of the stream row increases or
decreases automatically (if required) to display the checked attributes' values as
additional text. Checking too many attributes in the Details tab may consume the
maximum height of the available Transaction pane, hence, you must be careful when
checking the attributes in the Details tab.
* If you add a stream and check/un-check the required attributes' name and remove the
stream from the Transaction pane and then add the same stream again, Transaction
and Protocol Analyzer still retains the last state of the checked/un-checked attributes
and displays only those attribute values as additional text.
* The check-box in the Details tab is not displayed if the View -> Detail Transaction
Information menu command is selected or the Detail Transaction Information option
is selected in the Preferences -> Transaction Debug -> Transaction and Protocol
Analyzer page.

You can view multiple transaction details using the tooltip. The tooltip is visible on mouse

Preference Options
You can change the default setting for showing/hiding the display of the panes or
information in the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window. The height of the stream and
initial zoom ratio are also configurable.
To access the preference options, use the Tools -> Preferences menu command and
select the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer page under the Transaction Debug folder
in the left pane.
The following Debug Mode options are available in the Transaction and Protocol
Analyzer page of the Preferences form:
* Unified Transaction Browser - Select this mode to access preference settings for
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer (that is, for both Protocol Analyzer and Transaction
Browser).
It is recommended to use the Unified Transaction Browser mode, which
is the default mode. This chapter only talks about Unified Transaction
Browser mode. For details on the VIP Protocol Analyzer mode, see
Appendix A: Using Transaction and Protocol Analyzer (Protocol Debug
Mode).

Preference Options

The Transaction and Protocol Analyzer page of the Preferences form is illustrated in the
following figure:

The following is the list of available Transaction and Protocol Analyzer preference options:
* Show Message Type for New Stream
If enabled, Transaction and Protocol Analyzer displays the message types for a new
stream.
* Unfold Mode
This option automatically expands all the child streams and then splits overlapping
parent/child streams when you add a stream (assuming the transactions of this stream
have children) in the Unfold Mode. It is enabled by default.
If you add a stream with the Unfold Mode disabled, the stream is added without any
expansion. In this case, if the stream has a child, you can double-click the stream to
expand to a new stream or double-click a transaction to expand to the original stream.
* Full Stream Name
If enabled, this option displays the full stream name of all streams in Stream pane.
* Detail Transaction Information
If enabled, this option allows you to choose the number of transaction fields to be
viewed in the transaction display by entering the count in the Fields Count field. By
default, the Fields Count value is 0 and Transaction and Protocol Analyzer displays all
the available fields of transactions in the Transaction display pane.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
For example, if 5 is specified in the Fields Count field, Transaction and Protocol
Analyzer displays only the first five fields based on the order in the Details tab.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
* Display Attribute Name
If enabled, this option displays attribute names in the Transaction pane.
Stream Height
The default value is 30.
Tool Tip Attribute Count
The default Value is 10 but can be changed up to 20.
* Apply Filter/Colorization for All Streams
If enabled, this option applies filter/colorization settings to all the streams or channels
present in the Transaction pane. For newly added streams, previously specified filter/
colorization settings are applied and displayed in the Transaction pane.
To apply different filter/colorization settings for different sets of streams, you must
disable/un-check the Apply Filter/Colorization for All Streams option in the
Preferences page of Transaction and Protocol Analyzer.
When the Apply Filter/Colorization for All Streams option is in the selected
state, you can clear all the filtered settings applied in all the streams loaded in the
Transaction pane by using the Stream -> Clear Filtered Results menu command.
This option enables Transaction and Protocol Analyzer to stop applying filter settings
to newly added streams until any other filter settings are applied. Similar behavior is
applicable for the Stream -> Clear Colored Results menu command as well.
If no filter/colorization setting is specified, then newly added streams do not have any
filter or colorization; if required, click the Stream -> Filter/Colorize Transaction and
Protocol Analyzer menu command.

Displaying Attribute Name and Value as Additional Text in
Transaction Pane
To add or display the attribute name as additional text for a transaction in the Transaction
pane, select or enable the View -> Display Attribute Name menu command. The names
of all the checked attributes are displayed along with their values.
To add or display the attribute value as additional text for a transaction in the Transaction
pane, check the check-box next to the required attribute.
The checked state of an attribute is retained across all other transactions of the same
stream. When you select another transaction of the same stream, the attribute value for
that transaction is also displayed as additional text in the Transaction pane. This is also
illustrated in the following figure:

To remove an attribute value displayed as additional text for a transaction in the
Transaction pane, uncheck the check-box next to the required attribute.
If the selected transaction supports default attributes for its stream, those attributes are
checked in the Details tab.
Their values are also displayed as additional text below the common text for the selected
transaction. The attribute values are displayed in a separate row for each checked
attribute.

Highlighting by Relation
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer lets you highlight the relation between two transactions.
You can highlight the related parent/children/siblings of the selected transaction. Use the
Highlight Relation right-click option and toggle on the related sub-options. This option is
illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 23

Highlight Relation Right-Click Option

children of the selected transaction gets highlighted in red color (as illustrated in Parent/
Child Relationship).

Adding Streams by Relation From the Selected Transaction
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer lets you add a parent/child stream to a selected stream.
Use the following right-click options in the Transaction pane:
* Add Parent Stream(s) by Relation
This option adds parent streams to the selected streams and highlights the parent
streams. The parent streams are displayed in front of the selected streams.
* Add Child Stream(s) by Relation
This option adds the child streams to the selected streams and highlights the child
streams. The child streams are displayed next to the selected stream.
* Add Predecessor Stream(s) by Relation
This option loads the predecessor streams of the selected transactions (if not loaded)
and highlights the predecessor streams. The predecessor streams are displayed next
to the selected stream.
* Add Successor Stream(s) by Relation
This option loads the successor streams of the selected transactions (if not loaded)
and highlights the successor streams. The successor streams are displayed next to the
selected stream.
On selecting these options, the corresponding relation type sub-options in the
Highlight Relation option are also toggled ON. For example, on selecting Add
Child Stream(s) by Relation option, the immediate child stream gets added.
The Children sub-option of the Highlight Relation right-click option is also
toggled ON.
For non-VIP streams, if you select a stream that is already on the stream panel, a pop-up
appears. The message shows how many streams are already on the panel. It asks you to
go ahead or move the existing stream(s).

Click Yes to move the existing parent/child streams. Choose Cancel to stop the operation.
The message is illustrated in the following figure:

the project Hier. Tree tab. You can enter the search string in the text field displayed at the
top of the project Hier. Tree; the matching scope or stream gets selected and displayed, as
illustrated in the following figure:

To display or hide the Navigation text field, select the Show navigation text field rightclick option in the project Hier. Tree tab.

* Transaction and Protocol Analyzer checks occurrences in the Project Hierarchy tree.

Search or Filter Capability in Details Tab
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer provides search and filter capabilities. You can search
for required fields in protocol recorded transactions in the Details tab.
Enter the search string in the text field at the top of the details tab. Matching scopes/
streams are displayed as illustrated in the following figure.
Figure 26

Search Capability in Details Pane

To search multiple fields, enter multiple strings in the search text field with
space as a delimiter.
The search text field supports wildcards with "?" and "*" characters.

Search Capability for Transactions
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer provides the capability to search the transactions that
have a particular attribute or search the transactions that match a specified expression.

Configuring Display
You can use the View -> Configure Display command to hide/show some attributes in all
streams in the current window. This command will open the Configure Display form (see
figure Configure Display). The string entered in the Find field will find the partial matched
attributes in both lists and be highlighted. Use the arrow buttons to decide the Hide and
Show Attributes.
You can also change the attributes display order of all the panes in this Transaction and
Protocol Analyzer window using the Up and the Down buttons.
Figure 28

Configure Display

You can save or restore the configuration by clicking the Save or Restore buttons.

Filter/Colorize the Transactions
The transactions may be filtered based on more complex expressions. Select the streams
and display the Filter/Colorize form by selecting the Stream -> Filter/Colorize command.
The usage of entering the expression is the same as the usage of creating the virtual
stream. See section Creating Virtual Streams for details.
After entering the desired expression, click the Apply button. The filtering result is applied
to the selected streams in the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window.
You also can select an expression from the history field. Click the Add button and apply it
to the selected streams.
You can save or append the list of created virtual streams to a list file. Click the Save or
Append buttons.

to see transactions/streams that match certain conditions.
After entering the desired expression, click the Add button.

Creating Virtual Streams
The Transaction Debug solution provides users a way to combine a set of transactions
into one stream and view them together through virtual streams. You can write a flexible
expression to select the matching transactions, create a stream which contains only the
matching transactions, and view them together. This helps the users to create their own
stream dynamically with a meaningful name having certain transactions and/or messages
and segregate the transactions into several streams for better debugging.
This feature/functionality is not supported for VIP transactions.

You can create a virtual stream by using any of the following commands:
* The Stream -> Create Virtual Stream menu command.
This command opens the Create Virtual Stream form. The All FSDB Transactions
option is selected by default as the Search Mode. This is illustrated in the figure below.
The Create Virtual Stream option is enabled only if an FSDB file is loaded
into Verdi.

In the Create Virtual Stream form, enter the selection criteria for transactions in the
Expression field and enter a unique stream name in the Stream Name field. Then
click the Create button to create a virtual stream with all the transactions matching the
criteria.
* Create Virtual Stream RMB option in the Stream display view.
This command is enabled only if a row is selected in the stream display.
This command opens the Create Virtual Stream form and Selected Streams option is
selected by default in the search mode.
* Create Virtual Stream RMB option in the Search results view.

You can create a virtual stream by grouping all selected transactions in the Search
Results view. The Create Virtual Stream RMB option is enabled only if a row is
selected in the Search results view, as illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 32

Create Virtual Stream RMB Option

The Create Virtual Stream RMB option opens the Virtual Stream Name form as
illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 33

Virtual Stream Name Form

In the Virtual Stream Name Form, enter the stream name in the Virtual Stream Name
field and click OK. Transaction and Protocol Analyzer groups all selected transactions and
creates a virtual stream with the specified name.

The following figure illustrates a virtual stream in the Hier. Tree tab:
Figure 34

Virtual Stream in the Hier. Tree Tab

The Function field in the Create Virtual Stream form provides three predefined functions
for use as an operand: has_attribute(), has_relation() and has_tag(). You can enter
the attribute/relation/tag you want to match in the parentheses after clicking the function.
Keeping the parameter blank in the expression will result in TRUE value if transactions
have any attribute/relation/tag(s). For example:
has_attribute("att1") && has_relation("child") && has_tag()

For the has_relation function, the expression support:
* has_relation("relation_name"), for example, has_relation("ud1") will be true for
both the Master and Slave sides if there is a ud1 relationship between them.
* has_relation("relation_name_fr"), for example, has_relation("ud1_fr") will be true if
the ud1 transaction occurs in the Slave side.
* has_relation("relation_name_to"), for example, has_relation("ud1_to") will be true
if the ud1 transaction occurs in the Master side.
The Expression field also provides a $R operand. $R represents the selected transaction.

You also can get the expression from the Quick Filter pane using following steps (see
figure Create Virtual Stream through Quick Filter):
1. Check the desired attributes in the Quick Filter pane.
2. The expression of the combined attributes is automatically shown in the Expression
field.
3. Click the Import button in the Create Virtual Stream form.
4. As shown in figure Get Expression from Quick Filter, the expression in the Quick Filter
pane is imported to the Expression field in the Create Virtual Stream form.
Figure 35

Create Virtual Stream through Quick Filter

Figure 36

Get Expression from Quick Filter

After setting up the expression, click the Add button to add the stream into the history
(lower) field. The Name column is editable for keeping more meaningful details in the
history list. After you click the Create button, the created virtual stream will be added
into the stream pane. The stream name is shown in the Stream Name field which is also
editable. You can save or append the list of created virtual streams to a list file by clicking
the Save or Append buttons. The Clear button is provided to clear the strings in the
Expression field for the next new expression input.

Search Modes
Virtual stream supports the following search modes:
* Selected Streams
This mode allows you to create a virtual stream by considering only the matching
transactions available in the selected streams in the Stream display view.
To create a virtual stream from the selected streams,
1. Select the streams in the Stream display view.
2. Click the Stream -> Create Virtual Stream menu command or click the Create
Virtual Stream RMB command.
3. In the Create Virtual Stream form, select Selected Streams in the Search Mode
field as illustrated in the following figure:

* All FSDB Transactions
This mode allows you to create a virtual stream by considering only the matching
transactions available in the FSDB file. This search mode is selected by default in the
Create Virtual Stream form.

Transaction and Protocol Analyzer is tightly integrated with nWave, which is helpful in
debugging testbench simulation using transactions and waveform signals. You can open
the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application from nWave, load the corresponding
stream, and view the selected associated streams and transactions of a signal in
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer. You can also load the signals from Transaction and
Protocol Analyzer to the nWave window.
This section consists of the following sub-sections:
* Loading UVM Interface Signals From the Selected Transaction
* Loading Protocol Interface Signals to Selected nWave Application
* Loading Transactions to Selected Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Application
* Synchronization With nWave
* Points to Note

Only some VIPs support the features: Loading Protocol Interface Signals
to Selected nWave Application and Loading Transactions to Selected
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Application. For details on which VIPs
support these features, contact Synopsys support.

Loading UVM Interface Signals From the Selected Transaction
After the simulation, the generated default novas.fsdb FSDB file includes virtual interface
information.
To load the UVM interface signals from the selected transaction, perform the following
steps:
1. Open the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application in Verdi and load the FSDB
file.
2. In the Hier. Tree tab in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer, select a stream and select
the Add Signals to nWave right-click option. This option is enabled only if an FSDB
file has an interface signal path for the selected object instance.
Figure 40

Add Signals to nWave Right-Click Option

3. The Get Signals form opens, select the virtual interface signals, and click OK to view
the signals in nWave, as illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 41

Get Signals Form

4. The selected signals get added to nWave, as illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 42

Signals Added to nWave

If you also invoke the Resource View frame of UVM Debug, you can see the virtual
interface resource in the Resource View frame and use the Show Source for Virtual
Interface right-click command to check the definition code in the Source Code pane.

To enable dumping virtual interface with IUS, make sure to specify the following
file and options during compilation:
$VERDI_HOME/etc/uvm-1.1/verdi/dpi/uvm_verdi_dpi.cpp
+define+UVM_VERDI_VIF_RECORD
+define+UVM_VERDI_DPI
-DINCA

Points to Note
The following points must be noted for the synchronization functionality behavior between
nWave and Transaction and Protocol Analyzer:
* All Transaction and Protocol Analyzer applications synchronize only with the primary
nWave window.
* Each Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application remembers the loaded signals in
nWave. It ensures the same signals are not loaded again from the same Transaction
and Protocol Analyzer application.
* If any Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application is enabled with Sync. View
Range or Sync. All option, view range changes sync between the primary nWave and
the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application.
* If any Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application is enabled with Sync. nWave
Cursor Time or Sync. All option, cursor time selection between the primary nWave
and the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application is synchronized.
* If any Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application is enabled with Mark Transaction
or Sync. All option, then selecting the transaction from Transaction pane marks
pa_begin and pa_end markers in the primary nWave application.
* View range or cursor marker changes in other nWave (non-primary) applications do not
affect the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application.
This is true even when those applications are created or signals are loaded from the
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer application.

Using Cache and Memory Protocol Analyzer
(Memory Mode)
Synopsys Memory VIPs are based on Synopsys SystemVerilog Technology (SVT)
infrastructure that includes SystemVerilog classes and Memory Server. The Memory
Server is one of the key elements of SVT Memory VIP infrastructure because the actual
memory values are stored in the Memory Server instead of a SystemVerilog array. The
primary advantage of using this approach is that the performance of the Memory VIP does
not rely on the quality of the implementation of the equivalent sparse array server of each
simulator. For multi-GB memories, the simulation typically accesses only a small portion
of the overall address space. In addition, this approach supports virtual patterns which
enable memory initialization without incurring any significant memory or performance
overhead.
In a Memory VIP, protocol-level transactions and memory actions are stored in an FSDB
file. The Memory Server can be configured to record all memory actions to the same
FSDB file to view the memory-related data in the Verdi Cache and Memory Protocol
Analyzer. With the information recorded by the Memory Server, you can determine the
value of any memory address at any time during simulation.
The SVT Memory Server has been enhanced to store the memory actions associated
with the server in an FSDB file as transactions. The streams of these transactions are
tagged with the hidden attributes so that the memory instances can be recognized by the
Verdi environment and viewed in the new Memory Array browser. In addition, you can view
the memory actions of the Memory Server in Transaction Table View or Transaction and
Protocol Analyzer windows.
For performance considerations, each instance of a Synopsys Memory VIP must be
configured to dump data to the FSDB file. By default, this capability is not enabled.
Synopsys Memory VIPs provide controls for dumping protocol-level transactions, the
status of internal state machines, and the memory actions performed by the Memory
Server.

The following figure illustrates the high-level flow for Cache and Memory Protocol
Analyzer:
Figure 52

High-Level Flow for Cache and Memory Protocol Analyzer

Verdi, it is mandatory to specify the -lca option during compilation. For usage

Cache and Memory Protocol Analyzer Overview

Cache and Memory Protocol Analyzer Overview
Cache and Memory Protocol Analyzer provides the following features:
* Viewing the values and most recent memory actions for a specified address range. You
can view them at a specified time in a 2-D array format.
* Viewing the attributes associated with a specific address at a specific time.
* Viewing a list of memory actions associated with a specific address up to a specific
time.
* Viewing a list of all memory actions and the associated attributes.
* You can correlate a Memory VIP protocol-level transaction with one or more addresses
at a specific time. You can also correlate it with one or more specific memory actions in
the list view of memory actions.
The Cache and Memory Protocol Analyzer feature is dependent on the Verdi
FSDB SystemVerilog Writer API.

Reverse Debug Capability in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer also provides reverse debug capabilities to rewind and
go back to the simulation point from where the transaction started/ended/from where the
field value is assigned and use trace and simulation debug actions. You can also enable
tracing of value assignments from the Details pane in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer.
These capabilities are helpful to debug transactions that have issues or if a transaction
field value is not correct or needs to be traced to check its assigned value.

Reverse Debug Capability in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer

Tracing the Simulation to the Beginning or End Point
To trace the simulation back to where the transaction begins or ends, you must use the
-debug_access+reverse argument as a part of VCS compile switches to dump the
transaction step counter details.
By default, transaction begin step counter is recorded. You can control the required details
by using the following simulation time switches:
Beginning of Transaction:
+fsdb+event_begin_step_count=on
+fsdb+event_begin_step_count=off

/

Transaction end:
+fsdb+event_end_step_count=on
+fsdb+event_end_step_count=off

/

In interactive mode, load the UVM streams having transactions into Transaction and
Protocol Analyzer and
* Click the Go To Transaction Start right-click option to move the simulation backward
to the source from where the transaction is started (not by time).
* Click the Go To Transaction End right-click option to move the simulation backward to
the source from where the transaction is ended (not by time).

Trace Field Value Assignment
In interactive mode, load the UVM streams with transactions into Transaction and Protocol
Analyzer. The values for the selected transaction fields are displayed in the Details tab.
Select the required field in the Details tab and click the Go To Next Assignment rightclick option to trace the field value assignment. On clicking this option for the first time,
simulation goes forward to the point where the value assignment happened for the first
time. On clicking this option for the second time for the same transaction, the simulation
is forwarded to the next assignment. On clicking this option every time, the simulation is
forwarded to the next assignment.
Select the required field in the Details tab and click the Go To Previous Assignment
right-click option to trace the field value assignment. On clicking the Go To Previous
Assignment right-click option for the first time on the selected field, simulation goes
backward to the point where the value assignment happened for the last time for that
particular field. On clicking this option for the second time for the same transaction, the
simulation goes backward to the previous assignment. On clicking this option every time,
the simulation goes backward to the previous assignment.

Practice
This chapter demonstrates how to compile a design with a UVM environment,
automatically record transaction data during simulation, and use the applications to
observe and debug the transaction data in the Verdi platform.
This practice uses the UVM test_read_modify_write example with the Verdi modified
libraries. Perform the following steps to complete this practice for different stages.

Compiling and Simulating Design With UVM Environment
1. Change directory to the example at the following location:
%> cd
$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm/lib/examples/integrated/ubus_evdp_n
tb/examples

2. Set the environment variables as follows:
# Set VCS environment
%> setenv FSDB_ENV_DUMP_SEQ_NUM 1
%> setenv FSDB_ENV_MAX_GLITCH_NUM 0
un
# Set FSDB dumping environment
%> setenv VERDI_HOME <NOVAS_INST_DIR>
%> setenv LD_LIBRARY_PATH
$VERDI_HOME/share/PLI/VCS/LINUXAMD64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

3. Specify the VCS_UVM_HOME environment variable before compilation. It identifies the
path to the UVM 1.1d library for the VCS simulator.
%> setenv VCS_UVM_HOME $VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm-1.1d/lib/src

4. Use the following command to compile the design:
%> vcs -full64 -debug_access+all -sverilog -timescale=1ns/1ns
-ntb_opts uvm +incdir+../sv ubus_tb_top.sv

5. Use the following command to run the simulation:
%> ./simv +UVM_TESTNAME=test_read_modify_write +UVM_VERDI_TRACE
+UVM_LOG_RECORD +UVM_TR_RECORD +UVM_VERBOSITY=UVM_LOW

Viewing Transactions in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window

command:
%> make -f Makefile.vcs BITS=64

UVM_HOME = ../../../..
include ../../../Makefile.vcs_ntb

$(VCS) +incdir+../sv \
ubus_tb_top.sv

$(SIMV) +UVM_TESTNAME=test_read_modify_write +UVM_TR_RECORD
+UVM_LOG_RECORD +UVM_VERDI_TRACE
$(CHECK)

You can review other VCS options in the Makefile.vcs_ntb file of the $VERDI_HOME/
share/vmlib/uvm/uvm-1.1d/lib/examples path.

Viewing Transactions in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
Window
1. Expand the $event_root -> uvm_test_top -> ubus_example_tb0 -> ubus0 ->
masters[0] and slaves[0] directories in the Hier. Tree tab. Double-click the tree
nodes to add streams to the Transaction pane. As shown in Figure: Add Streams, the
sequencers of masters[0], slaves[0], and bus_monitor streams are added. You can
check transaction details in the Value pane by selecting a transaction in the Waveform
pane.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Viewing Transactions in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window

Figure 83

Add Streams

2. Select a transaction and use the Highlight Relation -> Parent command in the rightclick command menu. As shown in Figure: Highlight Relation, you can see the parent
transaction of the selected req transaction is highlighted in red.
Figure 84

Highlight Relation

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
3. Observe the bus_monitor stream.
a. Select the first transaction of the bus_monitor stream. It is a READ transaction with
address 16'hc304 and read data 8'h7a.
b. Select the second transaction of the bus_monitor stream. It is a READ transaction
with address 16'hb5fc and read data 8'h1f.
c. Select the third transaction of the bus_monitor stream. It is a WRITE transaction
with address 16'hc304. Now, the data is 8'h7b.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Viewing Transactions in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window

Figure 85

Write/Read Transactions

4. Select the second req transaction of the first sequencer stream. Switch to the Quick
Filter tab and you can see all attributes of the selected transaction are automatically
shown in the Quick Filter tab.
Figure 86

Using Quick Filter

5. Select beginTime and endTime attributes in the Quick Filter tab. The expression of
these two attributes is automatically completed. You can then use the Filter button to

Viewing Transactions in Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
filter out the transactions in the Waveform pane. You can also use this expression to
create a virtual stream, as described in the next step.
6. Use the Stream -> Create Virtual Stream command to open the Create Virtual Stream
form (as shown in Figure: Create Virtual Stream).
a. Use the Import button to import the expression from the Quick Filter tab.
The $beginTime==120ns && $endTime==210ns expression is shown in the
Expression field.
b. Modify the expression as shown in Figure: Create Virtual Stream.
c. Click the Add button to add the expression to the expression history.
d. In the Stream Name field, type VS_TIME1 to specify the name of the new virtual
stream.
e. Finally, click the Create button to create the VS_TIME1 virtual stream
Figure 87

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Create Virtual Stream

As shown in Figure: VirtualStream1-Virtual Stream, the VirtualStream1 stream is created
with the transactions between 120ns to 210ns.

Viewing Transactions in the Transaction Table View Window

Figure 88

VirtualStream1-Virtual Stream

Viewing Transactions in the Transaction Table View Window
To observe transactions whose begin times are larger than 100ns and with the req label
name, do the following:
1. Click the
icon and then select the By Conditions tab in the Add Transaction form
to add transaction by condition. Double-click $beginTime and $label attributes to add
them into the Expression field.
2. Complete the expression with $beginTime>100ns&&$label=="req" condition.
3. Click the Add button to add the expression to the expression history.
4. In the Stream Name field, type VSTIME2 to specify the name of the editable tab.
5. Finally, click the Create button to create the VSTime2 tab in the Transaction Table
View window (refer to Figure: Add Transactions by Condition).

Viewing Transactions in the Transaction Table View Window

Figure 89

Add Transactions by Condition

6. Transactions that match the expression are added in the VSTime2 tab in the
Transaction Table View window. Drag the second transaction of the bus_monitor from
the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window and drop to the Transaction Table View
Figure 90

Add a Transaction from Transaction and Protocol Analyzer

Viewing Transactions in the Transaction Table View Window

7. Click the first transaction and middle-click the second transaction to check the relative
time between two transaction recordings from master and bus_monitor. The cursor
time shows the time of the first transaction that was selected by left-clicking and
the row is highlighted with yellow. The marker time shows the time of the second
transaction that was selected by middle-clicking and the row is highlighted with red.
Figure 91

Relative Time between Transactions

8. Use the View -> Configure Columns command to combine $beginTime and
$endTime columns for easier observation. Select $beginTime and $endTime attributes
and click the Pack Selected button in the Configure Columns form. The names of
packed attributes are added with a (Pack1) suffix. Click the Apply button and the
columns are combined to one column with the $beginTime;$endTime name.
Figure 92

Configuring Columns

You can also unpack the packed attributes as follows:
Invoke the View -> Configure Columns command.
Select the packed attribute.
Click the Unpack Selected button.
Click the OK button to apply the setting.
9. To observe the transactions in the sequencer stream of Master, add the sequencer
stream by dragging and dropping from the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window.
Drag the first sequencer from the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window and drop
to the Transaction Table View window to create a non-editable tab.

Viewing Transactions in the Transaction Table View Window

Figure 93

Adding Sequencer Stream

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
10. Use the View -> Highlight Relation -> Child command and select the first transaction.
You can see the children of the selected transaction are highlighted. Also use the View
-> Show Relationship command to show the $Relationship column in the Transaction
Table View window.
Figure 94

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Viewing Children of Transactions

Transaction Relation Navigator window through the Transaction Table View window,

command in the right-click command menu.

Transaction Relation Navigator

in the upper-right corner of these windows. Then select the fourth transaction in the

Installing VIP Examples
You can install any of the VIP public examples and the instructions on how to install
an example is present in the README file located at $DESIGNWARE_HOME/vip/svt/
<suite_name>/latest/examples/sverilog/<test_bench>/README

Configuring VIP to Generate Transaction FSDB File
Most of the Synopsys VIPs have port level configuration control for recording the
transaction information into an FSDB file. After installing the examples, you can search for
enable_xml_gen and pa_format_type configuration attributes which are probably inside
the *cust_*configuration.sv file. The fields need to be set with the following values:
enable_*_xml_gen=1;
pa_format_type = svt_xml_writer::FSDB;

Along with the configuration, use the following additional compilation switch to enable the
transaction recording:
+define+SVT_FSDB_ENABLE

Appendix A: Using Transaction and Protocol
Analyzer (Protocol Debug Mode)
The Transaction Debug platform in Verdi is designed from the ground-up for capture,
display, debug, and analysis of abstract data, such as, transactions, messages, or any
other information that users want to access at high-level.
Transaction and Protocol Analyzer is integrated into Verdi as an extension to Verdi's
Transaction Debug platform. The Verdi Transaction and Protocol Analyzer is a protocolaware transaction debug solution in Verdi that allows viewing and debugging high level
protocol and transaction/memory information along with signal-level waveform, using one
FSDB file for all the mentioned data. To enhance usability, this single-process solution
provides a user-friendly platform to debug waveforms, transaction data, logs, and source
code, with different views that can be synchronized. The protocol data in the FSDB file is
dumped directly from Synopsys VIP. VC APPs APIs are also provided for users to enable
their own custom VIP to dump the protocol data into the FSDB file.
This Appendix discusses the VIP Protocol Analyzer mode (Protocol Debug mode) in the
following sections:
* Invoking Protocol Debug
* Invoking Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
* Prerequisites
* Transaction and Protocol Analyzer Window Overview

Invoking Protocol Debug
The recommended flow to browse the protocol data is as follows:
1. Invoke the Verdi platform with the whole system, including design, testbench, and
FSDB file. For example,
verdi -ssf <file_name>.fsdb

2. Click the Work Modes icon in the Welcome Page. Select the Protocol Debug Mode
option. Then press the Go to Work button.

Invoking Protocol Debug

Figure 101

Selecting Protocol Debug Work Mode

Or use the -workMode protocolDebug option directly to invoke Verdi in Protocol
Debug mode. For example:
%> verdi -workMode protocolDebug <verdi options> &

Use the Tools -> Transaction Debug -> Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
command in the main window.
The Protocol Debug mode also opens the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer pane to
debug the Verilog/SystemVerilog system at a higher level. As with other panes in the Verdi
platform, the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer pane can be docked or undocked. You
can also drag and drop it to other parts of the main window. In the following figure, "TNPA"
means Transaction and Protocol Analyzer.
Figure 102

Prerequisites
Before using the Verdi Transaction and Protocol Analyzer to perform protocol-level
debugging, use the VC VIP and execute the simulation to dump the protocol information
into the FSDB file (refer to the VIP manual for the supported VIPs and the detailed usage).
The HDL signals and the protocol data can be dumped into the same FSDB file.
Then, Transaction and Protocol Analyzer can be used to observe the VIP transaction data
and protocol information in Verdi.
Also, the extension.xml file, that is, the protocol definition is required to show the layered
structure for the protocol in the tree or the display.
You must also specify the following environment variables before invoking the Verdi
platform to enable VIP-related Transaction and Protocol Analyzer features:
%> setenv DESIGNWARE_HOME <DesignWare install path>
%> setenv PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH <Protocol Definition Files path>

If proprietary protocol VIPs need to be analyzed, you can specify the location of
proprietary protocol definitions using the PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH environment variable.

The Transaction and Protocol Analyzer pane provides a software-oriented waveformlike view (compared to the hardware hierarchical view in the nTrace window) for protocol/
transaction level debug. The Protocol Browser window can be used to debug and analyze
transactions and their activity by the time and transaction type.
The default pane layout of the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer window is shown in
the following figure. The left region contains the Hierarchy Tree pane; the middle region
contains the Protocol Transaction pane; the right region contains the Details pane.

Protocol Browser Default Layout

including the selected transaction, parent-children relationships of the selected
transaction, and detailed attributes for the selected transaction. Refer to the Figure:

button or select the File ->

Transaction and Protocol Analyzer is integrated with nWave, Smart Log, and Source

Protocol Analyzer Toolbar or Menu Bar Overview
You can use commands in the menu on the top of the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
pane to invoke forms or execute operations. The categories of the command menu
include: File, View, Transaction, Tools, and Window. Also, you can click the toolbar
icons to execute the corresponding commands. If the command has corresponding toolbar
icon, the figure of the icon displays to the left of the command name in the command
menu.
For example, you can use the File -> Save Streams / Restore Stream commands to
save or restore the protocol analyzer session; you can use the View -> Configure Display
command to invoke the Configure Display form to set to hide or show attributes in the
Details tab; you can use the commands under the Transaction menu to leverage the
features of the Transaction pane.
Figure 107

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Menu Bar Overview

Figure 108

Toolbar Overview

The following command actions can be realized with icons and fields in the toolbar:
* Show/hide objects: Click the toggle icons to switch between showing and hiding
panes or tabs, including Hierarchy Tree pane, Details tab, and global draw area.
* Highlight all Ancestors/Descendants: Click the toggle icon to highlight all the
ancestors/descendants of the selected object.
* Mark time and set time unit: Click the Marker Action icon to mark the specified time
in the Transaction pane. To specify the time unit, you can either enter it manually in
the time unit field, or click the Time Unit icon to invoke the Set Window Time Unit form
where you can select the time unit from the pull-down menu.
* Adjust the view in the Transaction pane: Click the icons to zoom in/out selected
transaction vertically and horizontally, or show all vertical/horizontal transactions.
* Synchronize with nWave and Smart Log: Click the icons to synchronize the Protocol
Analyzer pane with nWave pane and Smart Log pane.
* Configure Display: Click the icon to invoke the Configure Display form to specify the
attributes to be shown or hidden in the Details tab.
* Search Transaction: Click the icon to invoke the Set Search Attribute form to specify
the search criteria to search matching attributes.
* View selected objects: Click the View selected objects icon to show only the
selected objects and check the related parent-children objects. Other objects are
hidden.

Color Preferences
Menu Bar:

Tools -> Preferences

This command opens the Preferences page where the color settings of the selected
protocol can be configured.
Figure 109

Preferences Form

Figure 110

Color Preference Dialog

Figure 111

Select Color Form

The following field and buttons are available:
* Protocol: Select the protocol from the Protocol selection field.
* Hierarchy Tree: Select the object to configure the color settings from the hierarchy tree
section.
* Back Ground Color: This field displays the background color of the selected object.
If other background color is specified from the Select Color form, the specified color is
displayed in this field.
* Font Color: This field displays the font color of the selected object. If other font color is
specified from the Select Color form, the specified color is displayed in this field.
* Modify: Click this button to open the Select Color form where the color of background
or font can be specified for the selected object. The following fields and buttons are
available:
Basic colors: Specify the desired color for the background or font of the object
from this plate of basic colors.
Custom colors: Specify the customized colors from the Basic colors plate or the
color spectrum.
Add to Custom Colors: Click this button to add the specified color to the Custom
colors plate.
Color Spectrum: Specify the desired color for the background or font of the object
by clicking the color in the color spectrum or specifying the color values in the
selection fields below the color spectrum.
OK: Applies the settings and closes the Color Preference form.
Cancel: Cancels the settings and closes the Color Preference form.
* Preview: This field displays the specified colors of background and font of the object
for preview.
* Reset All To Default Colors: Click this button to reset the color settings of all objects
of the selected protocol to default.
* Reset Default: Click this button to reset the color settings of the selected objects to
default.
* Apply: Click this button to apply all of the changes in the Select Color form and leave
the Color Preference form open.

* OK: Click this button to save all of the changes in the Select Color form and close the
Color Preference form.
* Cancel: Click this button to cancel all of the changes in the Select Color form and close
the Color Preference form.

Tree pane
The Tree pane consists of three tabs: Hierarchy Tree, Quick Filter, and Protocols.

Hierarchy Tree
The Hierarchy Tree tab displays the protocol hierarchy that is present in the loaded FSDB
file. In the protocol-aware pane, the tree displays groups of streams that are based on
different layers that have been defined for the protocol.
For example, in the following figure, the tree for the USB protocol groups all streams
into one of the following layers: "Transfer", "Transaction", "Packets", "Link Items", and
"LTSSM". All these are different layers within the USB protocol.

These groupings are helpful to decide which layer to open to debug. Double-click on each
layer to open the content inside.

Add Signals to nWave
The Add Signals To nWave right-click command is provided to add signals from the
loaded FSDB file to the nWave pane. Specify signal interfaces in the invoked Add Signal
Interfaces to Waveform form and click the OK button.
Figure 112

Add Signal Interface to Waveform

The Sync Protocol Analyzer and nWave option is automatically enabled, which syncs
Protocol Analyzer and nWave as illustrated in the following figure:

The Protocol Analyzer synchronizes with nWave and marks the corresponding start time
and end time of the selected object with cursors in the nWave pane. The nWave pane can
then be used to analyze the signal activity between these two cursors.

Figure 113

Protocol Analyzer Synchronized with nWave Pane

View Source
The View Source right-click command can be used to load the source code for the
selected object into nTrace. Protocol Analyzer synchronizes with the source code from the
hierarchy tree. You can see the corresponding class definition in the Source Code pane.
If the source code has been loaded into Verdi, the corresponding class source code is
displayed in the Source Code pane.
Figure 114

Protocol Analyzer Synchronized With Source Code Pane

The Count column displays the object count instance, layer, or stream, adding up from
bottom to top.

Quick Filter
The Quick Filter tab provides the filtering feature for the protocol transaction content
shown in the Transaction pane.
Select one transaction in the Transaction pane (for example, in the following figure, the
selected transaction is a Control transfer); the attributes of this transaction are shown on
the Quick Filter tab. These attributes and their corresponding values that can be modified
can be used to perform quick filtering.

To set the filter criteria, select or de-select the attributes by checking or un-checking the
corresponding boxes. Click the Filter button to hide the transactions that do not match the
filter criteria. Only transactions that match the filter criteria are displayed in the Transaction
pane. Filtering transactions based on attribute values simplify the debug process by
narrowing down an issue to a smaller debug area.
For example, click the device_address field (refer to the figure below), the
device_address==0 expression is automatically displayed in the Expression field.
Click the Filter button. The results of filtering are shown in the Transaction pane. Only
transactions whose device_address attribute is equal to 0 is displayed.

Figure 115

Specify the Filter Condition

Protocols
The protocols tab displays all of the protocol definitions that have been read by the
Protocol Analyzer. This tree is constructed hierarchy by reading the protocol definitions
files from VIP installed in the path specified with the DESIGNWARE_HOME environment
variable and protocol definition files for custom or proprietary protocols. The location of
proprietary protocol definitions is specified using the PA_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH environment
variable.
To view a document, double click on the document link in the Protocols tab. The document
is opened in a new window.
