The Assertion Evaluation Engine of the Verdi Automated Debug Platform provides a
runtime assertion mechanism to add assertions during runtime without compiling and
loading the design again.
In general, assertions are added in the design, compiled with the design, and then the
results are checked by the Assertion Debug functions after they are loaded and undergo
simulation. The Assertion Evaluation Engine also checks assertions against a signal level
FSDB trace file for the design.
If there is change in assertion demands, the design, including the newly added assertion
code, must be compiled, loaded, and simulated again. The Verdi platform now provides an
interface to insert assertions without modifying the original design and check the failure or
success of the assertion. There is no need to recompile, reload, and resimulate.

Import Designs and Assertions
The design and SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) can be imported into the Verdi platform.
See the Language Support and Compile/Import Methods chapter in the Verdi and Siloti
Command Reference Manual for details.

Before you begin this application, follow the instructions in the Before You Begin chapter.
Transactions are an important piece of abstraction in system design and debug. System
design is in an early stage of the whole design process. Therefore, a powerful viewing
mechanism for transactions is mandatory for system designers.
transaction

For testbench verification, transaction-level checking is efficient when verifying the entire
system. It makes it easy to compare system behavior against the system specification.
When an error is found at the transaction level, you then investigate at the signal level.
This section covers the following topics:
* What is a Transaction?
* Generating Transaction Data
* View Transactions in nWave
* View Transactions in Transaction Table View Window

What is a Transaction?
Transactions are higher-level abstractions of signal-level activity. They are organized into
streams. Transaction streams can be dumped into FSDB format using dumping libraries
from Synopsys and its partners. You can also use the Open Transaction Interface (OTI)
extension of the FSDB Writer API.
stream

FSDB

Open Transaction Interface

OTI

API

Streams hold transactions. Each transaction consists of a set of attributes and is
independent of the others. There is no concept of "transaction type", as in SCV, even
when two transactions have the same set of attributes.
attribute

When you create a transaction, you must follow these steps :
1. Create a stream.
2. Create attributes.
3. Create a transaction.
4. Create relationships between existing transaction.

Generating Transaction Data
The transaction data can be obtained from the following sources.

Provided FSDB Dumpers
Dump transaction data from languages directly with native FSDB dumpers.
* SystemC/SCV -- supported OSCI and NCSC simulators.
* Specman/e
* SystemVerilog testbench in conjunction with simulator support (VCS, ModelSim)
* Vera
Refer to the SystemC Linking chapter in the Linking Novas Files with Simulators and
Enabling FSDB Dumping manual. It describes how to link native FSDB dumpers, SystemC
SCV, and HVL simulators.

Transaction IP Partners
Contact Denali (PCI-Express) or Spiratech (AMBA AXI, AHB) directly for details on
dumping FSDB format from their available intellectual property (IP).
FSDB

SVA Extraction
You can add SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) constructs to your design code to represent
transactions. The transactions can then be extracted from a signal level FSDB. Refer
to the Extracting Transactions Using SVA section in Appendix D: Additional Transaction
Example for more details.

FSDB Writer API and the Open Transaction Interface (OTI)
If you cannot generate transaction data in FSDB format using any of the previously
mentioned methods, use the Open Transaction Interface (OTI) extension of the FSDB
writer API to dump transaction data.
Open Transaction Interface

OTI

API

SVTB Automatic Logging of OVM/UVM Component and Port
Transactions
SVTB-based testbench environments are typically built on an SVTB verification library/
methodology like OVM/UVM. Synopsys has leveraged the OVM/UVM infrastructure to
record component and port transactions flowing up and down the testbench into the FSDB
file. The Synopsys mechanism uses OVM/UVM transaction recording to capture testbench
transactions in the FSDB file for debug and analysis in the Verdi platform.

View Transactions in Transaction Table View Window
This tutorial familiarizes you with transaction viewing and search operations in a
spreadsheet-like view.
transaction

1. Change the directory to <working_dir>/demo/transaction.
% cd <working_dir>/demo/transaction

2. Execute Verdi to import the FSDB file:
> verdi -ssf ahb32.bus.fsdb -workMode hardwareDebug &

The nTrace main window and nWave frame open and the FSDB file is loaded.
This tutorial only has an FSDB file that contains transactions and there is not
a related design.
3. In the nWave frame, choose the Signal -> Get Signals command to open the Get
Signals form.
Get Signals

The transaction FSDB is loaded displaying BusTop as the top hierarchy and
MyAHB_1(_AHB_) as the first hierarchical level which is for different protocols.
4. Click MyAHB_1 to show the streams under this hierarchy.
5. Select AhbTransfer and AhbTransaction and then click OK.

Add/Remove Transaction Streams
After loading a FSDB file with transaction data, you can view and manipulate the results in

Loading Information in Verdi
To invoke PPA (Power, Performance, and Area) through Verdi, use the following
% verdi -apex -ppa

You can invoke PPA and load design using the following command where, simv.daidir is

example,

The canvas view support enables visualizing, analyzing, and querying RTL objects in the

User Interface
You can open the canvas view in the following three ways:

Tcl Command
You can enable the canvas view and open its user interface using the following Tcl
schCreateCanvasWindow

You must specify the canvasType and scope arguments in the following command:
schCreateCanvasWindow -canvasType $type -valueType $valueType -scenario
$scenarioName -scope $scopeName

The command consists of the following arguments:
* -canvasType: Specify it as congestion or power.
* -valueType: The valueType argument depends on the canvasType. If the valueType
argument is not specified, by default metrics_cong_num_in_hot_spot is set for
congestion and total_power is set for power.
For congestion, you can specify the following arguments:
metrics_cong_num_in_hot_spot(default),
metrics_cong_cell_padding,
metrics_cong_logic_cong,
metrics_cong_overflow
For power, you can specify the following arguments:
total_power(default),
internal_power,
switching_power,
leakage_power,
glitch_power
* -scenario: You can use this argument only when the canvasType is Power. If it is not
specified, it uses the first scenario as the default value.
* -scope: Specify the scope module that you want to open.
schCreateCanvasWindow -canvasType power -scope top.cpu -valueType
total_power -scenario func.ss0p95v125c
schCreateCanvasWindow -canvasType congestion -scope top.cpu -valueType

Simprofile
The Simprofile feature in Verdi is used for profiling simulation performance. It allows you
to measure where the program spent its runtime and provides insights into the functions
called during execution. This profiling data is generated by VCS commands and stored
in a simprofile database. The profileView window in Verdi shows the CPU time of the
module, instance, and assertion.
This chapter contains the following sections:
* Loading the Simprofile Database (W-2024.09 and Earlier Releases)
* Loading the Simprofile Database (X-2025.06 Release Onward)
* Opening profileView
* profileView Window Panes
* Menus and Commands of the profileView Window
* Source View Indicator
* SVA Distribution Mode
* Merged Simprofile Report
* DUT/TB Proportion Display
* Limitations

Loading the Simprofile Database (W-2024.09 and Earlier Releases)

Loading the Simprofile Database (W-2024.09 and Earlier
Releases)
The profileView window uses the simprofile database generated by the VCS command
line. To load the database from the VCS command line, perform the following steps:
1. Run the following compile-time option in VCS:
%vcs -simprofile

2. Run the following runtime option in VCS:
%simv -simprofile time+json_dbg_field

3. Set the following environment variable:
setenv VERDI_SIMPROFILE_VIEW 1

4. Launch Verdi using the following command:
%verdi -apex -lca -profilePath <profile_database_path> -profileFilter
<percentage>

Where,
-profilePath <profile_database_path>: Specifies the path of the profile
database.
-profileFilter <percentage>: (Optional) Specifies the threshold percentage of
CPU time. The default value is 0.5 percent.
-lca: Enables the LCA feature.
-apex: Opens Verdi in Apex mode.

Loading the Simprofile Database (X-2025.06 Release Onward)
The profileView window uses the simprofile database generated by the VCS command
line. To load the database from the VCS command line, perform the following steps:
1. Run the following compile-time option in VCS:
%vcs -simprofile

2. Run the following runtime option in VCS:
%simv -simprofile time+json_dbg_field

Opening profileView

3. Launch Verdi using the following command:
%verdi -apex -profilePath <profile_database_path> -profileFilter
<percentage>

Where,
-profilePath <profile_database_path>: Specifies the path of the profile
database.
-profileFilter <percentage>: (Optional) Specifies the threshold percentage of
CPU time. The default value is 0.5 percent.
-apex: Opens Verdi in Apex mode.

Limitations of the Source View Indicator
The source view indicator has the following limitations:

The Simprofile feature in Verdi has the following limitations:
* Does not support save session and restore session.
* Does not support cross-platforms. For example, Verdi_linux_64bit can correctly
load the profile database only from VCS_linux_64bit.
* Supports only time profiling. Memory profiling and performance analysis are not
supported.
* Supports only concurrent assertions; other assertion types are not supported.
* Supports only the post-simulation mode.
* Supports loading the profile database only from the consistent version and sub-version
of VCS. For example, Verdi_2016.06-1 can correctly load the profile database only
from VCS_2016.06-1.
* The functions or tasks in the Caller Callee tab are related only to the constructs in the
Construct tab.
* Supports only Verilog as the component filter.
* Supports showing only the top-N instance list.
* Does not support RMB context menus in the Summary and Filter panes of the
profileView window.
* Cannot identify if an object is addable in the RMB context menu.

* Does not support the Show in Detail RMB context menu in the Top N Usage pane.
You can double-click the pane instead to view the details.
* Does not support the Show in Source Code RMB context menu in the Detail pane.
You can double-click the pane instead to view the source code.

Recommended Coding Style
The following coding styles are recommended for optimum transaction extraction results:
* Only "assert" directive is supported.
* Most SVA constructs are supported. For details, see Unsupported Coding Style.
* Using constructs, the sequence layer is recommended for modeling transactions.
Deep nesting range repetition and unbound range delay, for example ##[0:$], are not
recommended as it impacts performance.
* SVA local variables, including those declared in the sub-sequence of a specific
assertion, are recorded as attributes of transactions. Therefore, it is not recommended
to declare local variables with the same name across different sequences or properties.
Example 1:
sequence single_read;
logic [31:0] addr;
logic [31-1:0] data;
int ws;
@(posedge hclk)
(true,ws = 0) ## 0
(hready) ##1
(!hready && hsel) [*0:$] ##1
((hready && hsel && SR_CTRL), addr = haddr) ##1
((!hready && hsel), ws = ws + 1) [*0:$] ##1
(hready, data = hrdata);
SINGLE_READ: assert property(single_read);

The addr, data, and ws local variables of the single_read sequence are recognized as
the attributes of the assertion statement, SINGLE_READ.
Example 2:
sequence s1;
int localvar;

title: 0.5 percent, unless overridden through the
0.5 percent, unless overridden through the
text:
a_trans1: assert property(@(posedge clk) s1 and s2);

* You can specify the transaction label name of a specific sequence by declaring a string
type local variable named label_nTX, and assigning a label name to it. For example,
if you specify the following for a sequence/property, the transaction label name is
my_single_read:
sequence single_read;
string label_nTX;
(, label_nTX = "my_single_read",) ;

If you specify the following for an assertion statement, the label_nTX variable (if exists) of
the sub-sequence/property is used as its transaction label:
sequence s1;
string label_nTX;
(, label_nTX = "my_s1",) ;
sequence s2;
string label_nTX;
(, label_nTX = "my_s2",) ;
a_s1 : assert property((@posedge clk) s1 ##1 s2);

In this case, the label is either my_s1 or my_s2.

Unsupported Coding Style
The following coding styles are not supported for transaction extraction:
* Multiple clocking is not supported.
* Immediate assertion is not supported.
* cover and assume directives of SVA are not supported. Only the assert directive is
supported.
* Three types of assertion successes are not recognized as a transaction:
The vacuous success of the implication is not recognized as a transaction.
The abort success of disable iff is not recognized as a transaction.
Empty matches, for example seq1[*0];, are not recognized as a transaction.

Code Example
Consider the following SVA code example:
bind test assert_checker bind_transaction_evaluator(
.EN (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.ram_2kx32.mem.EN),
.WE (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.ram_2kx32.mem.WE),
.ADDR (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.ram_2kx32.mem.ADDR),
.DI (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.ram_2kx32.mem.DI),
.DO (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.ram_2kx32.mem.DO),
.CLK (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.ram_2kx32.mem.CLK),
.RST (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.ram_2kx32.mem.RST),
.RDInvalid (test.uFL_AMBA_SRAM.uSMI.iXOEN_d)
);
module assert_checker (
input EN,
input WE,
input [10:0] ADDR,
input [31:0] DI,
output [31:0] DO,
input CLK,
input RST,
input RDInvalid
);
sequence core_memory_write;
logic [10:0] Addr;
logic [31:0] Data;
(1) ## 0
(EN == 1'b1 && WE == 1'b1, Addr = ADDR, Data = DI) ##1
(!(EN == 1'b1 && WE == 1'b1));
sequence core_memory_read;
logic [10:0] Addr;
logic [31:0] Data;
(1) ## 0
(WE==1'b0 && RST==1'b0 && RDInvalid==1'b0, Addr = ADDR) ##1
(RDInvalid == 1'b0) ##1
(1, Data = DO);
CORE_MEM_WRITE : assert property(@(posedge CLK) core_memory_write);
CORE_MEM_READ : assert property(@(posedge CLK) core_memory_read);

Introduction
The UCLI dump command is enhanced to dump the Fast Signal Database (FSDB) file in
addition to the VPD and EVCD file dumping.
Now, you can use the UCLI dump command to dump the FSDB file by default, instead of
calling the FSDB system tasks or using FSDB commands on the UCLI command prompt.

Native Integration of Verdi and VCS

You can also perform the following operations using the dump command:
* Simultaneously open single VPD, EVCD, and FSDB dump files and manage them
individually.
* Simultaneously open multiple FSDB dump files and manage them individually.

The following steps describe the use model:
1. The default dump type of VCS is VPD. You can use the following environment variable
to set the default GUI as Verdi and the default dump type as FSDB
% setenv SNPS_SIM_DEFAULT_GUI verdi

title: 0.5 percent, unless overridden through the
text:
2. Set VERDI_HOME as provided in the following command line:
% setenv VERDI_HOME <novas_path>

title: 0.5 percent, unless overridden through the
text:
3. Compile your designs with the -debug_access+cbk option, as provided in the following
command line:
% vcs -debug_access+cbk <file_name>

Key Points to Note
* If a single dump file is open, it is not required to specify the -fid argument with the
dump commands that follow the dump -file command. If multiple dump files are
open, you must specify the -fid argument with the dump commands that follow the
second dump -file command.
* During simulation, if the number of open dump files return to one, you can exclude the
-fid argument. VCS issues an error message, if a dump command is specified without
the -fid argument when multiple dump files are open

Enhanced and New UCLI Dump Options
Several UCLI dump options are enhanced and new added for dumping FSDB file. For

Native Integration of Verdi and VCS

Optimized Performance of Gate-Level Designs Using Native FSDB
Gate
This section consists of the following subsections:
* Introduction
* Prerequisites
* Using the FSDB Gate Feature
* Limitations

Introduction
Verdi provides the Fast Signal Database (FSDB)-Gate feature for gate-level designs
without Standard Delay Format (SDF) information. You can invoke the FSDB-Gate feature
using VCS, which supports optimized FSDB gate-level dumping.
To enable this feature, use the VCS +fsdb+gate runtime option. It directs VCS to analyze
essential signals and the netlist information including the signature, function table, and
partition mapping, and uses the FSDB Dumper to record this information in an FSDB file.
Applications, such as Waveform Viewer and FSDB Reader, retrieve the mapping data
stored in the FSDB file. The retrieved data is further used by the VCS computation engine
to generate the complete signal data during debugging.
Additionally, if you enable the VCS force capability along with the -debug_access+f
+fwn compilation option, the VCS dynamic de-aliasing capability is also enabled while
dumping forced signals into the FSDB file. The FSDB Reader then interprets the event
and generates the related waveform in Verdi.
The FSDB Gate and dynamic de-aliasing acceleration features reduce the FSDB file
dumping size and optimize the VCS simulation time for specific coding styles and forced
signal flows.

Prerequisites
These features are available starting with the following versions:
* VCS simulator 2014.12
* Verdi 2014.12
* FSDB Reader 5.2 (for user of FSDB reader API)
* If the API libraries of the FSDB Reader are used to read the FSDB file with new format,
a Verdi license is required.

Native Integration of Verdi and VCS

Using the FSDB Gate Feature
Use the +fsdb+gate runtime option in the VCS simulation command line to enable these
features.
%> ./simv +fsdb+gate

Alternatively, set the following environment variable before starting the simulation:
%> setenv FSDB_GATE 1

Key Points to Note
* After simulation, a new format of the FSDB file is generated.
* FSDB cannot be read by previous Verdi version, for example 2014.03.
* Expect to see a higher simulation speed in the SystemVerilog Gate-Level design
without SDF.
* FSDB reading performance (CPU or memory) when using Verdi debug might be
impacted.

The following are the limitations for the FSDB-Gate feature:
* The +fsdb+gate option is disabled with a warning message, if you add any of the
following FSDB Dumper options in the simulation command line or if you specify them
using the setenv command:
- +fsdb+glitch=<num> (its corresponding environment variable is
NOVAS_FSDB_ENV_MAX_GLITCH_NUM or FSDB_GLITCH): If the <num> argument is not
equal to 1, the +fsdb+gate option is disabled.
- +fsdb+dumpon_glitch+time and +fsdb+dumpoff_glitch+time
- +fsdb+region (its corresponding environment variable is FSDB_REGION)
- +fsdb+sequential (its corresponding environment variable is
NOVAS_FSDB_ENV_DUMP_SEQ_NUM)

- +fsdb+strength=on (its corresponding environment variable is
NOVAS_FSDB_STRENGTH)

- +fsdb+esdb (its corresponding environment variable is FSDB_ESDB)
* If the +fsdb+gate option is enabled, the +strength option in dumping tasks is ignored
with a warning message.

Unified Transaction Debug - Verdi and Protocol Analyzer
Integration
This section consists of the following subsections:
* Introduction
* Use Model

Introduction
Protocol Analyzer and Verdi are now integrated for VIP to improve productivity in
protocol, transaction, and signal-level debugging. With this integration, you can invoke
Protocol Analyzer directly from Verdi. Protocol-related information is automatically loaded
into Protocol Analyzer. After Protocol Analyzer launches, it synchronizes with Verdi
automatically. You can also invoke Verdi with the loaded FSDB file from Protocol Analyzer.
This invoking mechanism reduces the time spent setting different configurations for Verdi
and Protocol Analyzer. It also reduces the time spent comparing corresponding objects
at different levels. This enables more efficient protocol-level analysis and signal-level
debugging, and increases debug productivity.
Additionally, you can generate or convert transaction-based FSDB directly from VIP
simulation results. You can use these FSDB files in both Protocol Analyzer and Verdi.

Unified UVM Library

The transaction debug capability offers the following features:
* Integrating Verdi and the Protocol Analyzer GUI
* Generating Transaction-Level FSDB File for VIP
* Reading Transaction-Based FSDB in Protocol Analyzer

Unified UVM Library
The unified UVM library is provided to integrate the instrumented UVM libraries of VCS
and Verdi. VCS and Verdi transaction recorder and message catcher coexist and are
compiled together.
You can directly use the unified UVM library with the Verdi-provided recording mechanism
during simulation, and for debugging with Verdi. Thus, accelerating the overall verification
cycle.
The unified UVM library also improves debug productivity in UVM-based environments
with VCS and Verdi. Both tools use the same UVM library, which eliminates the disparity
between simulation and debug libraries.
Single compilation, UUM, and UVM-VMM interoperability flows are supported in the unified
UVM library. The unified UVM library can also be qualified and validated using Synopsys
VIPs.

For the details about its usage, see the Verdi UVM Debug User Guide.

The scope-based peak analysis is now provided to analyze which time has the most
transitions (peak analysis) based on the scope for the design and FSDB file. The report
of the analysis is displayed in the scope-based table view. You can also check the result
in the waveform and in a Comma Separated Values (CSV) format. After checking the
report, you can further generate the What-if configuration files to perform advanced power
estimation based on the checking result.

The scope-based peak analysis capability offers the following features:
* Viewing reports in the scope-based table view
* Generating waveform of certain scopes
* Saving and restoring report as an XML file
* Dumping report in the Comma Separated Values (CSV) format
* Exporting the What-if configuration file

After loading your design and the FSDB file, use the Tools -> Switching Analysis -> New
Query command to invoke the Switching Analysis form.

title: 0.5 percent, unless overridden through the
text:
Figure 517

Switching Analysis Form

Enable the following options to configure the scope-based peak analysis for power
estimation:
* Include Instances under the Hierarchy
Includes sub-scopes of the specified scope to the analysis. If this option is not enabled,
the analysis only includes the selected scope.
* Time Grouping for the Peak Activity Report
Groups time in the report based on the time window size and sliding delta specified
respectively in the Time Window Size and With Sliding Delta fields. It is strongly
recommended to enable this option and specify the time window size and sliding delta.
* Report Type: Scope Based Peak Activity Report
Enables to generate the scope-based peak activity report.
You can also generate the report with the following options:
* Output to File
Generates the output file with the specified file type (based on the enabled Save
as XML File or Save as CSV File toggle options) for the report. The output file is
generated while the analysis is completed and the report is ready.

* Save as XML File
When the file is saved as an XML format, the XML file can be loaded in the Switching
Analysis Report form using the File -> Load from XML file command.
* Save as CSV File
When the file is saved as a CSV format, the CSV file is readable and is used in the
power estimation flow.
After completing the configurations, click the OK button in the Switching Analysis form
and click the Yes button in the Question dialog to open the Behavior Analysis form.

Click the OK button to perform the behavior analysis and the scope-based peak
analysis.
If the behavior analysis is performed in the current working directory, the dialog
box is not displayed.
The analysis report is shown in the invoked Switching Analysis Report frame.

You can see the transition counts and accumulative counts for the module in the Module,
Transition Count, and Accumulative Count columns accordingly.
The time windows, for example, 0~99, 100~199, 200~299, are displayed based on the
values specified in the Time Window Size and With Sliding Delta fields of the Switching
Analysis form. You can also change them in the Switching Analysis Report frame.

You can enter a scope name in the Scope filter and click the Filter button to select the
scope..

Generating Waveform With Report Entry
You can select a report entry and use the Add Selections to Waveform right-click
command or the Tools -> Add Selections to Waveform menu command to add the
selected entry into the nWave frame.

The selected entry is added in the nWave frame as a computed signal.

title: 0.5 percent, unless overridden through the
text:
Exporting the What-if Configuration File
After checking the analysis report, you may want to perform the What-if correlation flow
for power estimation with the specified scope and time duration. You can use the File ->
Export What-if Configuration File command to generate the What-if configuration file
and its related scripts that are needed in the What-if flow. The generated configuration file
and script files make it easy for you to complete the configurations during the What-if flow.
To generate the configuration file and script files, perform the following steps:
1. In the Switching Analysis Report frame, use the File -> Export What-if Configuration
File command to invoke the Export What-if Configuration File form.
2. Specify the FSDB file, scope, and time period in the corresponding fields.
3. Click the OK button.

The following configuration file and script files are generated accordingly:
* wi_config_file
The configuration file for the What-if flow.
* vcs_wi_compile.rc
The VCS compilation script used in the What-if flow.
* vcs_wi_run.rc
The VCS simulation script used in the What-if flow.
* ius_wi_compile.rc

Customizing Top View Name Encoding in Verdi Distsim Design
System Import
When Verdi imports a VCS Distsim design system, it encodes top view names
automatically. This encoding prevents duplicate or conflicting top view names across
multiple simv.daidir directories. For example, Verdi encodes the module top from
simulator S1 as top_$distsim_1.
You can customize this encoding postfix for each simulator's top views.

Customizing Top View Name Encoding in Verdi Distsim Design System Import

Distsim System Import Run File
Verdi uses a Distsim system import run file named dverdi.f to store target system
information. This file contains:
* All involved simv.daidir directories
* All dumped FSDB files
The master simv of the Distsim system generates this file automatically. You can also
create or modify this text file manually.

Customizing the Top View Postfix
To customize the postfix for top views of each simulator, follow these steps:
1. Open the Distsim system import run file in a text editor.
2. Locate the [distsim_design] section.
3. Add a new key-value pair using the topviews_postfix parameter.
4. Specify the postfix for each simulator using this format:
simulator_index:postfix_name.
Example configuration:
[distsim_design]
dbdir = 1:, 2:
ssf = 1:, 2:
topviews_postfix = 0:top0, 1:top1

In this example:
* Simulator 0 uses top0 as the top view postfix.
* Simulator 1 uses top1 as the top view postfix.
1. Save the import run file.
2. Import the Distsim design system in Verdi.
Verdi applies your specified postfix names when encoding each top view.

Accessing SolvNetPlus
The SolvNetPlus site includes a knowledge base of technical articles. It also answers
frequently asked questions about Synopsys tools. The SolvNetPlus site also gives
you access to Synopsys online services. These services include software downloads,
documentation, and technical support.
To access the SolvNetPlus site, go to the following address:
https://solvnetplus.synopsys.com
If prompted, enter your user name and password. If you do not have a Synopsys user
name and password, follow the instructions to sign up for an account.
If you need help using the SolvNetPlus site, click REGISTRATION HELP in the top-right
menu bar.

Contacting Customer Support
To contact Customer Support, go to https://solvnetplus.synopsys.com

Introduction
Overview
Power intent for a design is captured using the UPF (IEEE P1801). Generating an
individual UPF for each design instance exponentially increases the generated file size.
For a large design, it becomes overhead for the tools to handle it.
The Verdi UPF Architect (UPFA) tool automatically generates the UPF. It uses the latest
UPF syntax and suggested coding style that Synopsys low power tools support. For
example, the UPFA tool can generate UPF 2.0, 2.1, or 3.0 syntax with same input.
The UPFA tool lets you maintain a single power intent for different tools or UPF versions.
It also reduces UPF overhead in compilation, simulation, and emulation stages. It checks
power intent correctness with or without RTL. It also reports missing isolation strategies
(the VC Static tool is required for this feature).

Chapter 2: Introduction
Setting Up the UPFA Tool

Setting Up the UPFA Tool
To set up the UPFA tool, you need to set the VERDI_HOME variable to your UPFA install
path. The following is an example to setup TD UPFA in Synopsys environment:
setenv VERDI_HOME /remote/vtgimages/SAFE/linux64_TD.VERDI/releasestructure/verdi

To support HDL accessing, the VC_STATIC_HOME variable is required for the following
commands:
* ugo_vlog_analyze
* ugo_vhdl_analyze
* ugo_elaborate
* ugo_include_vclp_script
* ugo_optimize_power_intent

Using the UPFA Tool
The following sections describe how to invoke and use the Verdi UPFA tool:
* Invoking the UPFA Tool
* UPFA Tcl Commands

Invoking the UPFA Tool
You can use the upfa compile option to invoke the UPFA tool. In the command mode,
UPFA uses Tcl (Tool Command Language) as user interface, therefore you can use
Normal Tcl Commands.
The following section describes the UPFA Tcl commands:
* Use Model
* Arguments

Use Model
upfa [-batch] [-db <dir_name>] [-file <file_name>] [-help] [-id] [-log
<file_name>]

-batch

Starts the tool in the batch mode (non-interactive).
-db

Specifies the name of database directory. Default directory is ugo.db in the current
directory.
-file

Specifies the name of the script file to execute after setup.
-help

Prints help message.
-id

Prints the build/environment information of the tool.
-log

Specifies the name of log file. Default file name is ugo.log in the current directory.

The following sections describe the UPFA Tcl commands:
* Commands for Library Files
* Commands for HDL
* Command for Upgrading Message Severity
* Commands for Power Intent

Commands for Library Files
Following are the Tcl commands for library files:
* ugo_search_path
* ugo_link_library

ugo_search_path
Specifies a list of directories where the tool searches for library (.db), design, or UPF files.
ugo_search_path <dir_list>

<dir_list>

Specifies the directories to search for library, design, or UPF files. The path can be
absolute or relative to the tool working directory.
Returns 1 always.

ugo_search_path {. ./rtl ./upf}

ugo_link_library
Specifies a list of library (.db) files.
ugo_link_library <db_list>

<db_list>

Specifies all the library (.db) files.
Returns 1 always.
ugo_link_library {lib1.db lib2.db}

Commands for HDL
Following are the Tcl commands for HDL:
* ugo_vlog_analyze
* ugo_vhdl_analyze
* ugo_elaborate
* ugo_save_vclp_session
* ugo_restore_vclp_session

ugo_vlog_analyze
Analyzes Verilog or SystemVerilog files.
ugo_vlog_analyze {<vlogan_options>}

<vlogan_options>

Uses the options same as vlogan.
ugo_vlog_analyze {-f run.f -sverilog}

ugo_vhdl_analyze
Analyzes VHDL files.
ugo_vhdl_analyze {<vhdlan_options>}

<vhdlan_options>

Use the options as same as vhdlan.
ugo_vhdl_analyze {-f run.f -vhdl08}

ugo_elaborate
Elaborates HDL.
ugo_elaborate -top {[<library name>.]<top module>*} [{<vcs_options>}]

<library name>

Specifies the library of top module.
<top module>

Specifies the top module for elaboration.
<vcs_options>

Specifies the additional options for elaboration.
ugo_elaborate -top {TB_LIB.tb1 TB_LIB.tb2}

ugo_save_vclp_session
Saves a VCLP session. The background VCLP tries to save a session. The session is a
directory and can be restored by VCLP or UPFA. This command can be used to save the
RTL design session.
ugo_save_vclp_session [-session <session_name>]

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Specifies the session name.
ugo_save_vclp_session [-session <ses1>]

ugo_restore_vclp_session
Restores a VCLP session. The background VCLP tries to load the session.
ugo_restore_vclp_session [-session <session_name>]

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Specifies the session name.

ugo_restore_vclp_session [-session <ses1>]

Command for Upgrading Message Severity
Following is the Tcl command for upgrading message severity:
* ugo_set_rule_severity

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
ugo_set_rule_severity
Modifies the severity of the specified message. It does not change the name of the
message.
ugo_set_rule_severity
[-error <message names>] \
[-warning <message names >] \
[-phase <phase>] \
[-clear]

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
-error

Specifies the new severity value.
<message names> lists the warning/information message names or patterns. Patterns can

include the wildcard characters "*" and "?". When multiple names or patterns are specified,
they should be enclosed with " " or {}.
-warning

Specifies the new severity value. Valid values are parser, database, generator, optimizer,
and upf2csv.
<message name> lists the information message names or patterns. Patterns can include

the wildcard characters "*" and "?". When multiple names or patterns are specified, they
should be enclosed with " " or {}.
-phase

Specifies the phase of the given message to upgrade severity.

-clear

Clears all new severity rules of messages.
If the non-existing message name matches with the specified message name or
pattern, UPFA reports the Info message.
Input
upgrade_severity.tcl - Collection of the ugo_set_rule_severity commands to

define the new severity of the message.
Use Model
Usage Model-1:

upfa -f upgrade_severity.tcl -gui

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Usage Model-2:
ugo_set_rule_severity ### you can set rule at any time
ugo_read_power_intent
ugo_set_rule_severity
ugo_generate

text:
The following example sets the severity for TCL_VAR_NOT_DEFINED_WARNING and
FILE_NOT_FOUND_WARNING to error:
ugo_set_rule_severity -error { TCL_VAR_NOT_DEFINED_WARNING
FILE_NOT_FOUND_WARNING } -phase database

File 'partition.upf' cannot access: No such file.
Please specify a valid file.

Tcl variable '${AAA}' is used but not found in user-defined variable
Please consider to define a new item in user-defined variable section.

Commands for Power Intent
Following are the Tcl commands for power intent:
* ugo_read_power_intent
* ugo_remove_power_intent
* ugo_check_power_intent
* ugo_report
* ugo_set_var
* ugo_generate
* ugo_include_vclp_script
* ugo_optimize_power_intent
* ugo_target_scope
* ugo_upf2csv
* ugo_save_vclp_session
* ugo_restore_vclp_session

ugo_read_power_intent
Reads the power intent from several forms.
ugo_read_power_intent -csv <file name>

-csv

Reads the power intent based on CSV format.
ugo_read_power_intent -csv pd.csv

ugo_remove_power_intent
Removes the current power intent.
ugo_remove_power_intent

ugo_read_power_intent -csv cpu1.csv
ugo_report -error -file cpu1.err
ugo_remove power_intent
ugo_read_power_intent -csv cpu2.csv
ugo_report -error -file cpu2.err

Checks if there is any issue in the current power intent.
[-check_condition]

Where, -check_condition enables you to check the UGO_CONDITION_IF structure
intention.
Messages
See Appendix C: UPFA Database Messages.
ugo_read_power_intent -csv pd.csv
ugo_read_power_intent -csv ss.csv
# some ugo_read_power_intent commands

ugo_report
Displays detailed UPFA report.
ugo_report [-error] [-warning] [-info] [-phase <phase_name>] [-file
<file_name>]

-error

Displays error message.
-info

Displays information message.
-warning

Displays warning message.
-phase

You can use one of the following phase types:
* parser
* database
* generator
-file

Writes the messages to <file_name>
If this option is not specified, messages are displayed on console.
* ugo_report
Shows the summary of all messages. Following is the example report:
parser: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 info(s)
database: 3 error(s), 1 warning(s), 0 info(s)
generator: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 info(s)

* ugo_report -error
Displays the detailed error message report on the console. The following steps
describe the format of the message:
1. Format:
Severity-[phase][tag] Short description
formal description
[what next]

2. The line of short description has no indentation. The first letter of severity should be
uppercase. Phase should be in lowercase. Tag should be in uppercase. First letter
of the first word should be in uppercase, and others in lowercase.
3. All lines of formal description should have 2 indentation. If the formal description
contains file name and line number, it should be specified in the first separated line
without indentation.
4. What next section is optional. It should have 2 indentation.
Example:
Error-[database][TCL_VARIABLE_NOT_DEFINED] Tcl variable is
not defined
test.csv, 9
Tcl variable '$t1' is not checked without design.
Consider defining a new item in user-defined variable

ugo_set_var
Allows you to set up Tcl variable in the UPFA session. The Tcl variable setup is available in
the UPF generation flow.
ugo_set_var <variable name> <value>

Following are some special Tcl variables you can set:
escape_hdl_index 1

UPFA replaces [ to \[ and ] to \] for HDL index escaping for the generated UPF.
collection_result_display_limit <number>

Limit the result displayed for VCLP.

vclp_tmp_upf_dir <path>

Setup tmp_sub.upf path for VCLP check.
ugo_set_var escape_hdl_index 1
ugo_set_var SIM 1

ugo_generate
Generates the UPF based on the current power intent.
ugo_generate
-upf <file name>
[-version <upf version>]
[-apr <file name>]
[-stub <file name>]
[-constraint <file name>]
[-gen_spec <apr_spec>]
[-no_implicit_supply_function]
[-disable_opt_pst]
[-flatten_connection]
[-lrm]
[-bias_ref]
[-iso_config <file name>]
[-iso_info <file name>]
[-iso_constraint <file name>]
[-hier_iso_config <file name>]
[-include_pst]
[-exclude_pst]
[-top <top budgeted UPF name>]
[-partition <budgeted scope list>]
[-put_begin_patch]
[-disjoin_connection]
[-disable_sort_supply_function]
[-prefix <prefix>]

-upf

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Allows you to specify the file name for the generated UPF.
-version <2.0|2.1|3.0>

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Allows you to specify the UPF version for the generated UPF. For example, -version 2.0.
-apr

Allows you to specify the name for APR refine file.
-stub

Specify the name for the STUB UPF file. This file only contains the following UPF
commands:
* upf_version
* set
* find_objects
* source
* create_supply_port
* create_supply_net
* connect_supply_net:top_port
* create_supply_set
* create_power_domain
* set_port_attributes
* set_related_supply_net
-constraint

Allows you to specify the constraint file. see Appendix A: Tcl commands to Specify Detail
Categories in Constraint File.
-gen_spec <0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4>

value = 0, nwell/pwell/ground is in RTL, power is in APR
value = 1, nwell/pwell is in RTL, power/ground is in APR
value = 2, all (nwell/pwell/ground/power) is in APR
value = 3, all (nwell/pwell/ground/power) is in RTL
value = 4, power/ground is in RTL, nwell/pwell is in APR
-no_implicit_supply_function

Tool does not generate implicit supply function unspecified by the user.

-disable_opt_pst

Disables the power state table optimization feature.
-flatten_connection

Flattens foreach syntax to individual command for the [Connection] section.
-lrm

Generates UPF by strictly following the UPF LRM.
-bias_ref

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
If nwell and pwell are not specified, then nwell follows power and pwell follows ground.
-iso_config <file name>

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Generates the isolation configuration file for the ISOGEN flow. You must specify the
required intention in the [ISOGEN Config] section.
-iso_info <file name>

Generates the isolation.info file for the ISOGEN flow. You must specify the required
intention in the [ISOGEN Config] section.
-iso_constraint <file name>

Generates isolation constraint file for the ISOGEN flow. You must specify the required
intention in the [Scope Condition] section.
-hier_iso_config <file name>

Generates isolation configuration file for the ISOGEN flow. You must specify the required
intention in the [ISOGEN Config] section.
-include_pst

Used together with the -stub option. It includes power states and power state table in the
generated stub file.
-exclude_pst

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Does not generate power states and power state table in the output file.
-partition <scopes>

Specifies the scopes to budget.
-top <top>

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Specifies the file name of the top UPF while budgeting.
-disjoin_connection

Enables disjoin_connection constraint setting. Tool does not merge [Connection] text
format based on the SCOPE attribute.
-disable_sort_supply_function

Enables disable_sort_supply_function constraint setting. Tool follows the name order
in the specified supply functions in [Supply].
-put_begin_patch

Enables put_begin_patch constraint setting. Tool generates "puts" commands for [UPF
Patch].
-prefix <prefix>

Adds <prefix>_for every LRM UPF command.
ugo_generate_upf -upf system.upf -version 3.0 -apr system_refine.upf

Key Points to Note
* The -upf option generates the RTL UPF.
* The -apr option generates the APR UPF part. This UPF is the additional UPF for the
RTL UPF.
* The UPFA tool separates the power intent into the following two parts:
Power intent for major RTL
Power intent for APR connection
* In the front-end verification, the UPFA tool separates the physical supply net
connection from the RTL UPF. You can use the -apr option to direct such physical
information into another APR UPF file.
* The supply net and supply port along with their connection information (for supply set's
power supply function) should be generated in the APR UPF file. For example:
NAME,power,ground,nwell,pwell
SS1,VDD,VSS,VDDC,VSS

From the above example, the UPF generation of supply net VDD and supply set's
power function would be the physical connection. If you want to generate them, you
can use the -apr option to direct them into the APR UPF file.

* By default, the ground, nwell and pwell information is generated in the major RTL UPF,
whereas power information is generated in the APR UPF file.
* The -constraint option provides another mechanism to generate UPF. For more
information, see Appendix A: Tcl commands to Specify Detail Categories in Constraint
File.

ugo_include_vclp_script
Allows you to pass a script to background VCLP.
ugo_include_vclp_script
[-f <to_vclp_tcl>]

-f

Allows you to specify the script file.
The ugo_include_vclp_script Tcl command enables you to pass the vclp script for
background VCLP. This script should contain both analyze and elaboration information.

ugo_optimize_power_intent
Optimizes power intent based on the current power intent, and generates a supplemental
CSV file.
To use this command, you must import the design and read UPF (optional). In some
cases, search path and link library are also required for elaborating the design information
for VCLP.
Before using the ugo_optimize_power_intent command, you must generate
the design information using the ugo_include_vclp_script command.
ugo_optimize_power_intent
[-isolation_strategy -csv <output_file_name>]
[-isogen [-upf <upf_file_name>] [-iso_config <iso_config_file>]
[-dump_cross_domain <iso_info_file>]]
[-dump_iso_domain <iso info file>]
[-v <upf version>]
[-map_iso]
[-allow_unconnected]

[-src_sink_iso]
[-iso_place <source|sink>]
[-hetero_iso]
[-strict_lrm]]
[-spagen
-partition <partition list>
[-upf <upf file name>]
[-ref_spa_file <file name>]
[-force_spa_file <file name>]
[-rewrite_spa]
[-constraint_spa_file <constraint_file>]
[-spa_module_name]
[-no_pw_port]
[-merge_signal]
[-j2|-j4]
[-hdb]]
[-pstgen
-upf <upf file name>]
[-hier_iso_gen
-hier_iso_config <hier_iso_config JSON file>
[-upf <upf file name>]
[-iso_place <source|sink>]
[-hetero_iso]]
[-out_dir <output directory>]
[-wrapper_upf <wrapper upf file name>]

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Optimizes isolation strategies/intent and writes to <output file name> with CSV
format. This option checks for any missing/uncovered isolation strategy and generates
a supplemental CSV file to complete the power intent based on the current power
specification.
-isogen

Enables the ISOGEN flow. You cannot specify -spagen or -pstgen together.
-upf

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Specifies the UPF file input to the -isogen/-spagen/-pstgen flow. This option is
mandatory for the -pstgen flow
-iso_config

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Allows you to specify the isolation configuration file in JSON format.
-dump_cross_domain

Generates all cross-domain settings required for the UPF. The output is reported to the
specified file.

-dump_iso_domain

Generates all isolation domain settings required for the UPF. The output is reported to the
specified file.
-v <2.0 | 3.0>

Specifies the version of the output UPF.
-map_iso

Enables the generation of the map_isolation commands.
-allow_unconnected

Includes Logic Sink Unconnected elements for iso_gen.
-src_sink_iso

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Generates the source/sink type isolation command.
-iso_place <source|sink>

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Specify source or sink. In ISOGEN flow, this option allows you to set up the preference of
generating isolation at the source domain side or sink domain side.
-hetero_iso

Generates isolation at the sink domain side.
-strict_lrm

Generates the UPF strictly following LRM.
-spagen

Enables SPAGEN flow. You cannot specify -isogen and -pstgen together. The output file
name is <partition>_spa.upf for sub-scope partition and <top scope>_spa.upf for
top-most scope.
-partition

Specifies the block list for generating SPA strategy. You must specify this option for the
SPAGEN flow. You can specify "." for the top-most scope.
-ref_spa_file

Specifies the input file to compare with the final result SPA. The input file format should be
as follows:
<signal name> <supply set>
<signal name> <supply set>

-force_spa_file <file name>
<signal name> <supply set>
<signal name> <supply set>

-rewrite_spa

Specifies the SPAGEN flow to rewrite only the boundary SPA value.
-constraint_spa_file

* Specifies the input file to specify custom SPA rule. The input file format should be:
<partition name>,<driver supply set>,<receiver supply set>,<port
regular pattern>,<custom SPA value>

* If a target port is under scope <partition name> and its driver supply is <driver
supply set>, receiver supply is <receiver supply set>, and the name matched
<port regular pattern>, then assign final SPA value as <custom SPA value>.
* <driver supply set> and <receiver supply set> can be empty, which means
don't care.
-spa_module_name

Generates SPA file name by referring to the module name instead of scope name.
-no_pw_port

Does not generate the port defined in the UPF.
-merge_signal

SPAGEN merges bus signals and structural signals with a single SPA command if they
have the same SPA value.
-j2 |-j4

You can use these options with -hdb to enable multi-process SPAGEN to speed up.
-hdb

Enables Verdi trace driver/load engine to speed up. it is recommended to always enable
this option.
-pstgen

Enables the PSTGEN flow. You cannot specify both -isogen and -spagen together.
-hier_iso_gen

Enables hierarchical ISOGEN flow. You cannot specify -isogen, -spagen, or -pstgen
together.

-hier_iso_config

Allows you to specify the isolation configuration file in JSON format.
-wrapper_upf

Generates a wrapper UPF which includes generated UPFs.
-out_dir

Specifies the output directory for the isogen/spagen generated UPF files.
-wrapper_upf

Generates a wrapper UPF which includes generated UPFs.
Example 1

ugo_read_power_intent -csv system.csv
ugo_optimize_power_intent -isolation_strategy -csv system.iso.csv
// modified the proper value for system.iso.csv
ugo_read_power_intent system.iso.csv

title: Verification ContinuumTM
Verification ContinuumTM
text:
ugo_include_vclp_script -f to_vclp.tcl
// the Tcl script should contain analyze, elaborate, read_upf
ugo_optimize_power_intent -spagen -partition "par1 par2"
ugo_optimize_power_intent -spagen -partition "."

For more information on ISOGEN, see Appendix B: ISOGEN Native Support in UPFA.

ugo_target_scope
Setup the target scope of the CSV generating the UPF.
ugo_target_scope <scope_name>

ugo_elaborate SOC
ugo_target_scope parA
ugo_read_power_intent -c parA.csv
ugo_generate -upf parA.upf

ugo_upf2csv
Allows you to convert UPF file to power intent CSV format.
ugo_upf2csv
[ -upf <Input UPF File>]
[-csv <Output CSV File>]

-upf

Specifies the target UPF file to be converted.
-csv

Specifies the output CSV file.
Input UPF File Requirements
TCL and UPF Related:
Input UPF files should pass to the VCLP compilation.
UPFA Related:
The ugo_upf2csv command transforms the UPF commands to CSV format. If a UPF
command is not converted to the CSV format (for example, unsupported commands or
command format error), an error message is reported, and the command is ignored.
The UGO engine does not support all the UPF commands. If the input UPF file contains
unsupported commands, the transformed output CSV file may not pass VCLP because of
the unsupported UPF commands. There is no output CSV file requirement. A CSV file is
generated correctly when the specified input UPF file meets all the requirements. For more
information, see The ugo_upf2csv Command Limitations section.

CSV Format
The following sections describe the CSV format of the Verdi UPFA tool:
* Keywords
* Tcl Variable
* Comment
* Boolean Expression
Keywords
All special keywords are wrapped with #. For example, #INTERNAL#.
Tcl Variable
All Tcl variables are wrapped with "${var_name}". For example, "${pd_name}".
Comment
The comment should begin with // in a separate line.
Boolean Expression
Boolean expression can be specified in specific cells. The following Boolean operators are
supported:
Operator

CSV Format

!

Logical negation

~

Bitwise negation

<

Less than

<=

Less than or equal

>

Greater than

>=

Greater than or equal

==

Equal

!=

Not equal

&

Bitwise conjunction

^

Bitwise exclusive disjunction

|

Bitwise disjunction

&&

Logical conjunction

Fast Signal-Based Expression Statement
Following is the fast signal-based expression statement:
<#AND# | #OR# | #LAND# | #LOR# | #XOR#>{<word>[RANGE]*}

This statement results in a parenthesis expression that contains the expansion according
to the keyword.
* #AND#
The expression is expanded by `&'.
* #OR#
The expression is expanded by `|'.
* #LAND#
The expression is expanded by `&&'.
* #LOR#
The expression is expanded by `||'.
* #XOR#

CSV Syntax

The expression is expanded by `^'.
* <word>
Specifies the prefix of each expansion. Verdi issues an error message if word contains
any Boolean operator.
* [RANGE] = [start:end:step=1]
The start option specifies the starting value for an expansion.
If only start is specified, RANGE is treated as a bit signal and is not expanded.
The end option specifies the end value for an expansion. Verdi issues an error
message if end is smaller or equal than start.
The step option specifies the step for an increment. Verdi issues an error message if
step is smaller or equal than 0.
Example 4

"ena && #AND#{sig[0][-2:5:2][0]}" results in
"ena && (sig[0][-2][0] & sig[0][0][0] & sig[0][2][0] &
sig[0][4][0])"

CSV Syntax
You can use the following format to describe the CSV syntax:
[Section Name]
MUST_HAVE[, OPTIONAL, <user-defined field>*]

Where,
* Section Name is the section header.
It tells the tool how to handle the table between any two section headers.
If there are multiple tables in one section, use an empty line to separate it.
* MUST_HAVE is must have field for the table.
* An error is issued if any cell under the must have field is empty.
* OPTIONAL is the optional field for the table.
The optional field is wrapped by [ ]
Cells under optional field can be empty
* <user-defined field> allows you to define the field.

User-Defined Comment in the Header of Table

* <user-defined field>* means the field can be defined multiple times.
* Single Value means the field supports only single value. If you specify it multiple
times for the same object, the value is updated and only keeps the last value. Verdi
issues error message if you specify multiple values in the field.
* List Value means the field supports multiple values. If you specify it multiple times for
the same object, the list of values is appended to the field.
* If you specify multiple objects in the same cell, you must specify " " in the
csv format.
* If you specify multiple tables for the same category, you must specify at least
one \n character between each table.

User-Defined Comment in the Header of Table
You can add user-defined header for comment purpose only. Comment should be
specified within parenthesis.
For example:
[Variable]
NAME,VALUE,(MY_COMMENT)

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Example: test, test_value, (this is comment)
* Multiple comments are supported in header
* Comments are supported in all sections
* If comma exists in the comment, it should be specified within quotations
* Comma do not reflect in the output to generated UPF

User-Defined Variable
This section describes the syntax of the user-defined variable.
[Variable]NAME, PATTERN, OBJECT_TYPE, [,SCOPE, METHOD, TRANSITIVE, OTHER,
DIRECTION, TRAVERSE_MACROS, CHECK_LIST]
[Variable]
NAME, VALUE [,SUBSTITUTE]

User-Defined Variable

Specifies the variable name for keeping the search result.
The variable name can be referenced by ${<var_name>} in another table.
If the value contains any escaped identifier, it should be enclosed with {}. For
example, {!@PO}iop
* PATTERN
Specifies the string used for searching.
* METHOD (optional)
Specifies the method used for string searching. The value can be one of the following:
#GLOB#: Uses Tcl glob expression
#REGEX#: Uses regular expression
#EXACT#: Disallows wildcard expansion
The default value is #GLOB#.
* OBJECT_TYPE
Limits the result objects. The value can be one of the following:
#MODEL#: Returns the instances of the models whose name matches the pattern.
#INST#: Returns the instances whose name matches the pattern.
#PORT#: Returns the ports whose name matches the pattern.
#NET#: Returns the nets whose name matches the pattern.
#PROC#: Returns the process whose name matches the pattern.
The default value is #INST#.
* TRANSITIVE (optional)
#YES#: Performs search in entire sub-tree
#NO#: Default is sub-scopes only
* OTHER (optional)

User-Defined Variable

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Performs search with other constrains. The value can be one of the following:
#CASE_INSENSITIVE#: Performs case-insensitive search. Default is case-sensitive
search.
#TRANSITIVE#: Performs search in entire sub-tree. Default is sub-scopes.
#LEAF#: Returns leaf objects only.
#NON_LEAF#: Returns non-leaf objects only.
* DIRECTION (Optional)
#INOUT#
* TRAVERSE_MACROS (optional)
Generate -traverse_macros for the find_objects command. It could be:
#NO#: Default
* CHECK_LIST (optional)
Generate UPF context to check whether the find_objects result is empty. It could be:
#NO#: Default
* VALUE
Specifies literal string or Tcl expression. String is treated as the LIST value if there is
","as the separator.
* SUBSTITUTE
Specifies if expand Tcl variable is in VALUE. It can be:
#YES# -> Uses " " to quote the value
#NO# -> Uses {} to quote the value
The default value is #YES#.
Allows you to identify if different attributes are specified for the same object.

Power Domain
This section describes the syntax of Power Domain.

Specifies the name of the power domain.
* ELEMENTS

Power Domain

Specifies the applied elements of the power domain. You can specify the following
keywords in this column:
#DEFAULT#: Specifies top power domain. An error is issued if no or more than one
of these keywords is specified.
${<variable name>}: See User-Defined Variable section.
Specifying " . " in the ELEMENTS column is the same as specifying #DEFAULT#.
In addition to keywords, you can also specify list of instances.
Values are appended to power domain object if the object is previously defined.
* EX_ELEMENTS (optional)
Specifies a list of instances or ports to which the strategy does not apply.
* AVAILABLE_SUPPLIES (optional)
Specifies the supply sets that are available for use by the implementation tool to insert
power cell for the power domain. You can specify the following keyword in this column:

Values are appended to the power domain object if the object is previously defined.

Default is #NO#

be a Tcl variable.
If the name of supply handle exists in previously defined power domain object, then
the value of supply handle is updated.
* NAME is the key to identify if you are specifying different attributes for the same object.

This section describes the syntax of Power Domain Intent.
[Power Domain Intent]
NAME,ELEMENTS[,POWER, GROUND, RESOLVE, STATENUM, VOLTAGE,
LOGIC_CONDITION, NWELL, PWELL]

Specifies the name of the power domain.
If not specified, Verdi creates supply net instead of power domain.
* ELEMENTS
Specifies the applied elements of the power domain:
#DEFAULT#:Specifies instances
#EMPTY#:Creates supply set with NAME and supply net instead of power domain.
Specifying " . " in the ELEMENTS column is the same as specifying #DEFAULT#.
* POWER
The supply net that would be created for the primary power supply of the domain.
* GROUND
The supply net that would be created for the primary ground supply of the domain.
* RESOLVE
Used for tool to create APR refinement. It could be:
#UNRESOLVED#
#ONE_HOT#
#PARALLEL#
#PARALLEL_ON_HOT#
The default value is #UNRESOLVED#
* STATENUM
Specifies the number of power state for the supply net.
Reports an error if mismatch occurs with data input.
* VOLTAGE
Digital value that specifies the domain's state.
* LOGIC_CONDITION
Logic expression specified for the supply set state.

Specifying Tcl variable is allowed. However, tool generates expanded value in output
UPF.
* NWELL
The supply net that would be created for the supply set function.
* PWELL
The supply net that would be created for the supply set function.
* The NAME is the id key to identify the domain.
* If the NAME value is empty, previous line value would be referred.
* UPFA creates supply set for the primary of power domain, and specifies
POWER, GROUND, NWELL, and PWELL to the supply functions. The
name of supply set would be following format:
SS_<PD NAME>

If NAME is #EMPTY#, the format would be SS_<IDX>.
* UPFA creates the supply set' state and power domain's state by referring
the VOLTAGE value with the following format:
SS_<PD NAME>_ON_<VOLTAGE>: For supply set, and if VOLTAGE is not OFF.
SS_<PD NAME>_OFF: For supply set, and if VOLTAGE is OFF.
SS_<IDX>_ON_<VOLTAGE>: For supply set, empty power domain, if VOLTAGE

is not OFF

SS_<IDX>_OFF: For supply set, empty power domain, if VOLTAGE is OFF.
<PD NAME>_ON_<VOLTAGE>: For power domain, and if VOLTAGE is not OFF.
<PD NAME>_OFF: For power domain, and if VOLTAGE is OFF

* The -simstate option is added with:
NORMAL if VOLTAGE is not OFF.
CORRUPT if VOLTAGE is OFF.

* The ground is assumed to be 0.0v.
* Following is the limitation to specify the
STATENUM,VOLTAGE,LOGIC_CONDITION:
It is NOT allowed to redefine the
STATENUM,VOLTAGE,LOGIC_CONDITION for the same POWER.

This section describes the syntax of a supply.

Supply

NAME,[DIRECTION,RESOLVE,SS_ONLY,<supply function>*]

Specifies the name of the supply set. If you specify #EMPTY#, supply set is not created,
only supply net for supply function is created.
* DIRECTION (optional)
Allows Verdi to create APR refinement. You can use the following keywords:
#INTERNAL#
The default value is #INTERNAL#.
* RESOLVE (optional)
Allows Verdi to create APR refinement. You can use the following keywords:
#UNRESOLVED#
#ONE_HOT#
#PARALLEL#

<resolution _function_name>
The default value is #UNRESOLVED#.
* <supply function>* (optional)
Allows Verdi to create APR refinement.
If the value is non-empty, Verdi uses this value to name the supply net.
If the value is empty, Implicit Naming Rule is considered to name the supply net.
The name of supply function and the value of supply function should be a single value.
If the name of supply function exists in the previously defined supply, the value of
supply function is updated. The name and value of supply function cannot be a Tcl
variable.

Supply

It can be:
If value = #YES#, only the supply set object and supply set function are created.
Supply net and supply port are not created.
You can use this option while creating a supply set and to refer existing supply net as

Supply Map
This section describes the syntax of a supply map.
[Supply Map]
NAME,MAPPING

Specifies the name of the supply map that is used for [Apply Power
Model]:SUPPLY_MAP. If the value is empty, the value in the previous line is referred to.
* MAPPING
Specifies a list value. Following is the syntax:
{<instance scope supply set ref> <current scope supply set ref>}
"{<instance supply set1 ref> <current supply set1 ref>}, {<instance
supply set2 ref> <current supply set2 ref>},"

Specify a space between <instance supply set ref> with <current supply
set ref>

You must surround {} with <instance supply set ref> and <current supply
set ref>.

Switchable Supply
This section describes the syntax of the switchable supply.
[Switchable Supply]
OUT,STATE[,SW_NAME,PD,IN,ACK,ACK_DELAY,ACK_CONTROL,SUPPLY,CELL]

Switchable Supply

* OUT
Specifies the supply set name or supply net which can be switched. The supply set/
supply net should be defined in [Supply] or [Power Domain Intent]
The value cannot be a Tcl variable
* STATE
Specifies the switch state for OUT. You can use the following keywords:
#OFF#{<condition>}
#ON#{<condition>}
#PARTIAL_ON#{<condition>}
Verdi issues an error message if <condition> is not specified

This section describes the syntax of the power spec.

The value should be the power state of <supply set>.
* <power domain>
The value should be the power state of <power domain>.

Specifies a simstate for the power states associated with a supply set.

The value should be the power state of <power state group>.
* LOGIC_CONDITION (optional)
Logic expression specified for the supply set state.
* LEGAL(optional)

Power Spec

Specify legal or illegal for the transition.
The value can be #YES# or #NO#.
* ADD_ONLY(optional)

This section describes the syntax of isolation.
[Isolation]
NAME[,PD,INSERT_SIDE,ISO_SIGNAL,ELEMENTS,EX_ELEMENTS,CLAMP,ISO_SENSE,SRC,
SINK,LOCATION,SUPPLY,CELL,NO_ISOLATION,OPTIMIZABLE,NAME_PREFIX,NAME_SUFFI
X,DIFF_SUPPLY_ONLY,FORCE,APPLIES_TO_BOUNDARY,UPDATE]

Specifies the name of the isolation rule.
Specifies the applied power domain of the isolation rule.
* INSERT_SIDE
If INSERT_SIDE is present, (1) SRC and SINK are mandatory, and power domain
should be specified (2) It is an error if PD, LOCATION, or SUPPLY is specified.
The following four keyword values can be specified:
#FROM# - PD is SRC location is self, supply is the SINK domain's primary.
#FROMPARENT# - PD is SRC, location is parent, supply is the SINK domain's primary.
#TOPARENT# - PD is SINK, location is parent, supply is the SINK domain's primary.
#TO# - PD is SINK, location is self, supply is the SINK domain's primary.

* ISO_SIGNAL
Specifies the control signal for the isolation cell.
* ELEMENTS (optional)
Specifies the applied elements of the isolation rule. You can specify the following
keywords in this column:
#INPUTS#: The elements are restricted to any port that the direction is input relative
to the specified domain.
#OUTPUTS#: The elements are restricted to any port that the direction is output
relative to the specified domain.

#BOTH#: The elements are restricted to any port that the direction is both relative to
the specified domain.
#ALL#: Every port on the interface of the domain is applied
${<variable name>}: See User-Defined Variable section.
Other than keywords, you can also specify list of instances or ports.
The values are appended to isolation object if it is previously defined. However, if
multiple #INPUTS# and #OUTPUTS# are specified, only the last keyword value is applied.
If keyword #ALL# is specified, all values are ignored except #INPUTS# and #OUTPUTS#.
* EX_ELEMENTS (optional)
Specifies a list of instances or ports to which the strategy does not apply.
* CLAMP (optional)
Specifies the value of the inferred isolation cell's output when isolation is enabled. You
can specify one of the following:

The if-else Structure Support
UPFA supports if-else structure in the power intent csv file using the following keywords.
This support allows you to generate if-else block UPF code.
* UGO_CONDITION_IF(<condition>)
* UGO_CONDITION_ELIF(<condition>)
* UGO_CONDITION_ELSE
* UGO_CONDITION_END
UGO_CONDITION_IF( ${TOOL} == VCS )
NAME, ELEMENTS
PD_TOP_IF, #DEFAULT#
UGO_CONDITIONELIF( ${TOOL} == VCF )
NAME, ELEMENTS
PD_TOP_ELIF, #DEFAULT#
UGO_CONDITION_ELSE
NAME, ELEMENTS
PD_TOP_ELSE, #DEFAULT#
UGO_CONDITION_END

if { ${TOOL} == VCS } {
# [Power Domain]
create_power_domain PD_TOP_IF -elements { . }
} esleif { ${TOOL} == VCF } {
# [Power Domain]
create_power_domain PD_TOP_ELIF -elements { . }
} else {
# [Power Domain]
create_power_domain PD_TOP_ELSE -elements { . }
}

Detailed Usage
* The <condition> inside UGO_CONDITION_IF and UGO_CONDITION_ELIF with
surrounding with () would be the condition string and is generated into UPF condition
with the string.
* All the keywords should be specified with an empty line to identify the block is begin.
* You must specify the UGO_CONDITION_IF keyword to identify if the condition is the
begin block.
* You must specify the UGO_CONDITION_END keyword to identify the condition block is
end.
* It is an error if there is UGO_CONDITION_ELIF, UGO_CONDITION_ELSE,
UGO_CONDITION_END, but no previous UGO_CONDITION_IF.
* It is an error if there is previous UGO_CONDITION_IF, UGO_CONDITON_ELIF,
UGO_CONDITION_ELSE, but no UGO_CONDITION_END.
* All sections in the CSV condition block are generated inside the UPF condition block.
The sections surrounding with UGO_CONDITION_IF and front of

UGO_CONDITION_ELIF/UGO_CONDITON_ELSE/UGO_CONDITION_END are generated

inside the "if" block in the UPF code.

The sections surrounding with UGO_CONDITION_ELIF and front of

UGO_CONDITION_ELIF/UGO_CONDITION_ELSE/UGO_CONDITION_END are generated

inside the "elseif" block in the UPF code.

The sections surrounding with UGO_CONDITION_ELSE and front of
UGO_CONDITION_END are generated inside "else" block in the UPF code.
* Nested if-else block is supported.
Limitation
* All the sections inside the condition blocks are not checked for the power intent. That
is, UPFA does not report power intent error if the section is inside the condition blocks.

Foreach support
UPFA supports the foreach syntax in the power intent CSV file using the following
keyword:
UGO_FOREACH(<value1>, <value2>)
UGO_FOREACH_END

This support allows you to generate the following UPF code.

}

For Loop Statement Support
The following is the structure of the for loop in the power intent CSV file for generating the
for loop in the UPF code:
UGO_FORLOOP(<start>,<test>,<next>)
UGO_FORLLOP_END

Example Usage CSV File
UGO_FORLOOP(${set x 0}, {$x<10}, {incr x})
NAME, DIRECTION, RESOLVE, ground, nwell
SS1, #INTERNAL#, #ONE_HOT#, VSS, VDD
UGO_FORLOOP(,,)
UGO_FORLOOP_END
UGO_FORLOOP_END

for {set x 0} {$x<10} {incr x} {
for {} {} {} {}
# [CREATE_SUPPLY_NET]
create_supply_net VSS -resolve one_hot
create_supply_net VDD -resolve one_hot

# [CREATE_SUPPLY_SET:NO_FUNC]
# [CREATE_SUPPLY_SET:FUNC_SUPPLY_NET]
create_supply_set SS1 -function { ground VSS } -function {nwell VDD}

}

Detail Usage
1. You must specify the two keywords and an empty line to identify the block.
2. You must use UGO_FORLOOP to identify the opening of a for loop.
3. The UGO_FORLOOP keyword requires three arguments: start, test, and next.
4. If an argument is empty, the generated argument in the for loop is "{}".
5. If an argument is not empty, it should be enclosed with curly braces "{}".
6. You must use the UGO_FORLOOP_END keyword to identify the end of a for loop.
7. Nested for loop is supported.
Limitation
* All the sections inside the for loops are not checked for the power intent. That is,
power intent error is not reported if the section is inside a for loop.

UPFA supports partition UPF integration [PIntegration] in CSV format to describe
integration work. UPFA analyzes the partition UPF file to get information, generate network
and connection automatically. UPFA generator takes CSV file and partition UPF as input
and output of the top level integrated UPF file.
Figure 1

Partition UF Integration

[PIntegration]
SCOPE,UPF [, LOW_CONN_INTEG, CONDITION, IS_MACRO]
[PROPAGATE_SS, PROPAGATE_PSTATE, INTERNAL_SUPPLY, COMMON_PD,
COMMON_POWER, COMMON_GROUND, COMMON_NWELL, COMMON_PWELL]

Specifies the scope to load the UPF file.
* UPF
UPF file to be loaded.
* LOW_CONN_INTEG (Optional)
The value can be:
#YES#: Automatically connect top-level supply net logic net with block UPF supply
port/logic port. The default value is #YES#.
#NO#: No connection.
* CONDITION (Optional)
Expression specified for integrating partition UPF. It can be:
#IF#{<condition>}
#ELIF#{<condition>}
#ELSE#
* IS_MACRO (Optional)
Specifies macro or not. It can be:
The default value is #NO#. By default, the connection of sub blocks is also generated
inside the condition. If this value is #YES#, then the connection is generated outside the
condition.
* PROPAGATE_SS (Optional)
Creates a supply set or supply net. This option takes effect only when LOW_CONN_INTEG
is #YES#.

Creates a supply set with same supply functions in block UPF. In block UPF, if
the supply function is not connected to the supply port, this supply net cannot be
propagated and is discarded. If all supply functions are not connected to the supply
port, this supply set is not propagated and discarded.
It can be:
The default value is #YES#
* PROPAGATE_PSTATE
Specifies power state and propagation in SoC UPF. This option takes effect only when
LOW_CONN_INTEG and PROPAGATE_SS are #YES#.
In the following cases, the state is discarded:
Supply set state with logic expression is not supported.
Existing objects (supply set) cannot be propagated.
The power state of power domain is discarded.
In the power state group and the power state table if the state's objects include power
domain, supply net, supply port, logic port, and logic net, the state is discarded. The
power domain cannot be propagated. The power state table does not support supply
net and supply port. The power state group does not support logic port and logic net.
It can be:
The default value is #YES#
* INTERNAL_SUPPLY (Optional)
A supply that does not create a supply port at top level is considered an internal supply.
* COMMON_PD
Specify the name to create top-level power domain.
#EMPTY#: Specified when top-level power domain creation is not required.

Default is PD_TOP
Creates a supply set named SS_<COMMON_PD> as the primary supply set of COMMON_PD.

* COMMON_POWER (Optional)
Specify common power supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates a supply net only.
The default value is the most common power supply net for all partitions. UPFA
automatically identifies the default value. If automatic identification fails, the default
value is VDD.
This option is the power function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).
* COMMON_GROUND (Optional)
Specify common ground supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates a supply net only.
The default value is the most common ground supply net for all partitions. UPFA
automatically identifies the default value. If automatic identification fails, the default
value is VSS.
This option is the ground function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).
* COMMON_NWELL (Optional)
Specify common nwell supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates the supply net only.

The default value is the most common nwell net for all partitions. UPFA automatically
identifies the default value.
This option is the nwell function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).
* COMMON_PWELL (Optional)
Specify common pwell supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates the supply net only.
The default value is the most common pwell net for all partitions. UPFA automatically
identifies the default value.
This option is the pwell function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).

Key points to Note:
If common power, ground, nwell, or pwell is not defined, UPFA performs automatic
identification as follows:
1. Initially, if a supply set specified in the block UPF can be propagated, the priority
is to get the most frequent power, ground, nwell, or pwell supply functions as
COMMON_POWER/COMMON_GROUND/COMMON_NWELL/COMMON_PWELL.
If the identification of COMMON_POWER is a success and COMMON_NWELL is a
fail, then COMMON_POWER is assigned to COMMON_NWELL.
If the identification of COMMON_GROUND is a success and COMMON_PWELL is a
fail, then COMMON_GROUND is assigned to COMMON_PWELL.
2. For inappropriate supply set or failed identification in the first step, UPFA identifies
the power and ground from the supply net. It treats the supply net with a name
starting with VSS (case insensitive, Vss, vss, and so on) as ground supply net.
Others are treated as power supply net. The most frequent ground supply net is
treated as COMMON_GROUND and the most frequent power supply net is treated as
COMMON_POWER.
3. If there is no inappropriate supply net or failed identification in the second step, UPFA
sets COMMON_POWER and COMMON_GROUND with the default value.
