Level Shifter
This section describes the syntax of level shifter.
[Level Shifter]
NAME,[PD,
INSERT_SIDE,ELEMENTS,EX_ELEMENTS,RULE,SRC,SINK,INPUT_SUPPLY,OUTPUT_SUPPL
Y,LOCATION,THRESHOLD,CELL,NO_SHIFT,NAME_PREFIX,NAME_SUFFIX,FORCE,APPLIES_
TO_BOUNDARY,UPDATE]

Specifies the name of the level shifter rule.
Specifies the applied power domain of the level shifter rule.
* INSERT_SIDE
If INSERT_SIDE is present, (1) SRC and SINK are mandatory, and power domain should
be specified (2) It is an error if PD or LOCATION is specified.
The following four keyword values can be specified:
#FROM# - PD is SRC location is self.
#FROMPARENT# - PD is SRC, location is parent.
#TOPARENT# - PD is SINK, location is parent.
#TO# - PD is SINK, location is self.

Level Shifter

* ELEMENTS (optional)
Specifies the applied elements of the level shifter rule. You can specify the following
keywords in this column:
#INPUTS#: The elements are restricted to any port that the direction is input relative
to the specified domain.
#OUTPUTS#: The elements are restricted to any port that the direction is output
relative to the specified domain.
#BOTH#: The elements are restricted to any port that the direction is both relative to
the specified domain.
#ALL#: Every port on the interface of the domain is applied
${<variable name>}: See User-Defined Variable section.
Other than keywords, you can also specify list of instances or ports.
The values are appended to the level shifter object if it is previously defined. However,
if multiple #INPUTS# and #OUTPUTS# are specified, only the last keyword value is
applied. If keyword #ALL# is specified, all values are ignored except #INPUTS# and
#OUTPUTS#.
* EX_ELEMENTS (optional)
Specifies a list of instances or ports to which the strategy does not apply.
* RULE (optional)
The elements are restricted to any port for which the driving and receiving logic have
the specified voltage relationship. It can be:
#H2L#
#L2H#
#BOTH#(Default value)
* LOCATION (optional)

Level Shifter

Specifies the location for the inferred level shifter cell to be placed. It can be:
#FANOUT#
The default value is #SELF#.
* SRC (optional)
When specified, the elements are restricted to any port that is driven by the logic
powered by a supply set that matches the specified one.
* SINK (optional)
When specified, the elements are restricted to any port that is present on a path for
which the receiver supply set matches the specified one.
* INPUT_SUPPLY (optional)
Allows you to power the input portion of the level-shifter.
* OUTPUT_SUPPLY (optional)
Allows you to power the output portion of the level-shifter.
* THRESHOLD (optional)
When specified, the elements are restricted by any port for which the magnitude of
the difference between the driver and receiver supply voltages can exceed a specified
threshold value.
The default value is 0.000000
Specifies the level shifter model to be used for implementation tool.
* NO_SHIFT (optional)
Specifies the no-shift. It can be:
#YES#: Tool generates -no_shift for the power intent
The default value is #NO#.
If value is #YES#, (1) PD is mandatory, (2) INSERT_SIDE should not present.

Level Shifter

Specifies the isolation model to be used for implementation tool.
* NAME_PREFIX (optional)
Specifies the name format for the generated isolation instances or nets related to
* NAME_SUFFIX (optional)
Specifies the name format for the generated isolation instances or nets related to
* NAME_PREFIX (optional)
Specifies the name format for generated isolation instances or nets related to the
* NAME_SUFFIX (optional)
Specifies the name format for generated isolation instances or nets related to the
* NAME and PD are the keys to identify if you specify different attributes for the same
object.
* FORCE (optional)
Generates -force_shift for the set_level_shifter UPF command. It could be:
Default is #NO#
* APPLIES_TO_BOUNDARY
Generates -applies_to_boundary for the set_level_shifter UPF command. It
could be:
#LOWER#
#UPPER#
#BOTH#

Generates -update for the set_isolation UPF command. It could be:
Default is #NO#

This section describes the syntax of retention.
[Retention]

Retention

NAME,PD[,TYPE,ELEMENTS,RES_SIGNAL,RES_SENSE,SAVE_SIGNAL,SAVE_SENSE,RES_CO
NDITION,SAVE_CONDITION,SUPPLY,CELL,LIB_MODEL,PORT_MAP,NO_RETENTION]

Specifies the name of the retention rule.
Specifies the applied power domain of the retention rule.
* TYPE
Specifies the implementation cell type of the retention rule. It can be:
#1_PIN#:Single-pin retention flip-flop
#2_PIN#: Two-pin retention flip-flop
#ZPR#: Zero-pin retention flip-flop
#NORET#: No retention
* ELEMENTS
Specifies the applied elements of the retention rule. You can specify the following
keywords in this column:
#ALL#: Every port on the interface of the domain is applied
${<variable name>}: See User-Defined Variable section
Other than keywords, you can also specify list of instances or ports.
The values are appended to retention object if the object is previously defined.

Repeater
This section describes the syntax of repeater.
[Repeater]
NAME,PD,SUPPLY[ ,ELEMENTS,EX_ELEMENTS,SRC,SINK,CELL,NAME_PREFIX,NAME_SUFF
IX]

Repeater

Specifies the name of the repeater rule.
Specifies the applied power domain of the repeater rule.
* SUPPLY
The power domain, supply set, or supply net that powers the repeater cell.
* ELEMENTS
Specifies the applied elements of the repeater rule. You can specify the following
keywords in this column:
#INPUTS#: The elements are restricted to any port whose direction is input relative
to the specified domain.
#OUTPUTS#: The elements are restricted to any port whose direction is output
relative to the specified domain.
#ALL#: Every port on the interface of the domain is applied.
#BOTH#: The elements are restricted to any port that the direction is both relative to
the specified domain.
Other than keywords you can also specify list of instances or ports.
Values are appended to repeater object if it is previously defined. However, if multiple
#INPUTS# and #OUTPUTS# are specified, only the last keyword value is applied. If
keyword #ALL# is specified, all values are ignored except #INPUTS# and #OUTPUTS#.
* RES_SIGNAL
Specifies the restore signal for the retention cell
Verdi issues an error message if #2_PIN# or #1_PIN is specified for TYPE, but this
column is not present in the table.
Verdi issues an error message if #ZPR# is specified for TYPE, but this column is present
in the table.
Both RES_SIGNAL and RES_SENSE should be specified together.
* EX_ELEMENTS (optional)
Specifies a list of instances or ports to which the strategy does not apply.

Load UPF

* SRC (optional)
The elements are restricted to any port that is driven by logic powered by a supply set
that matches the specified one.
* SINK (optional)
The elements are restricted to any port that is present on a path for which the receiver
supply set matches the specified one.
Specifies the repeater model to be used for implementation tool.
* NAME_PREFIX (optional)
Specifies the name format for generated isolation instances or nets related to
* NAME_SUFFIX(optional)
Specifies the name format for generated isolation instances or nets related to

Load UPF
This section describes the syntax of load UPF.
[Load UPF]
UPF, SCOPE, [PRE_SCRIPT_PRE_SCOPE, PRE_SCRIPT_POST_SCOPE,
POST_SCRIPT_PRE_SCOPE, POST_SCRIPT_POST_SCOPE,LOADER_TOP]

Load UPF

* UPF
Specifies the UPF file to be loaded.
Specifies the scopes to load the UPF file.
* PRE_SCRIPT_PRE_SCOPE (optional)
Specifies the scripts to source before you set the corresponding scope.
* PRE_SCRIPT_POST_SCOPE (optional)
Specifies the scripts to source before you load the UPF file.
* POST_SCRIPT_PRE_SCOPE (optional)
Specifies the scripts to source after you load the UPF file.
* POST_SCRIPT_POST_SCOPE (optional)
Specifies the scripts to source after you set the scope back to top.
* LOADER_TOP (optional)
Specifies one or more top UPF names. In some cases you must load the UPF. If you
set this option, the tool matches only the loader top file name. It then generates the
load_upf command.

Connection
This section describes the syntax of connection.
[Connection]HIGH_CONN, SCOPE, LOW_CONN [,PINNUM, TYPE, IS_RTL]

* HIGH_CONN
Specifies the highconn to make connection. It should be supply set, supply net, or logic
net. The value cannot be a Tcl variable.
Specifies the scopes to connect the lowconn.
* PINNUM (optional)
Specifies the number of connections for the scope.

have the same time if generated at the same execution. The time format is YYYY/MM/DD
HH:MM:SS. The time zone is dependent on the local machine.

The if-else Structure Support
UPFA supports if-else structure in the power intent csv file using the following keywords.
This support allows you to generate if-else block UPF code.
* UGO_CONDITION_IF(<condition>)
* UGO_CONDITION_ELIF(<condition>)
* UGO_CONDITION_ELSE
* UGO_CONDITION_END
UGO_CONDITION_IF( ${TOOL} == VCS )
NAME, ELEMENTS
PD_TOP_IF, #DEFAULT#
UGO_CONDITIONELIF( ${TOOL} == VCF )
NAME, ELEMENTS
PD_TOP_ELIF, #DEFAULT#
UGO_CONDITION_ELSE
NAME, ELEMENTS
PD_TOP_ELSE, #DEFAULT#
UGO_CONDITION_END

title: 0 -isolation_sense low -isolation_supply SS_PD_AON -location self
0 -isolation_sense low -isolation_supply SS_PD_AON -location self
text:
Detailed Usage
* The <condition> inside UGO_CONDITION_IF and UGO_CONDITION_ELIF with
surrounding with () would be the condition string and is generated into UPF condition
with the string.
* All the keywords should be specified with an empty line to identify the block is begin.
* You must specify the UGO_CONDITION_IF keyword to identify if the condition is the
begin block.
* You must specify the UGO_CONDITION_END keyword to identify the condition block is
end.
* It is an error if there is UGO_CONDITION_ELIF, UGO_CONDITION_ELSE,
UGO_CONDITION_END, but no previous UGO_CONDITION_IF.
* It is an error if there is previous UGO_CONDITION_IF, UGO_CONDITON_ELIF,
UGO_CONDITION_ELSE, but no UGO_CONDITION_END.
* All sections in the CSV condition block are generated inside the UPF condition block.
The sections surrounding with UGO_CONDITION_IF and front of

UGO_CONDITION_ELIF/UGO_CONDITON_ELSE/UGO_CONDITION_END are generated

inside the "if" block in the UPF code.

The sections surrounding with UGO_CONDITION_ELIF and front of

UGO_CONDITION_ELIF/UGO_CONDITION_ELSE/UGO_CONDITION_END are generated

inside the "elseif" block in the UPF code.

The sections surrounding with UGO_CONDITION_ELSE and front of
UGO_CONDITION_END are generated inside "else" block in the UPF code.
* Nested if-else block is supported.
Limitation
* All the sections inside the condition blocks are not checked for the power intent. That
is, UPFA does not report power intent error if the section is inside the condition blocks.

Detail Usage
1. You must specify the two keywords and an empty line to identify the block.
2. You must use UGO_FORLOOP to identify the opening of a for loop.
3. The UGO_FORLOOP keyword requires three arguments: start, test, and next.
4. If an argument is empty, the generated argument in the for loop is "{}".
5. If an argument is not empty, it should be enclosed with curly braces "{}".
6. You must use the UGO_FORLOOP_END keyword to identify the end of a for loop.
7. Nested for loop is supported.
Limitation

power intent error is not reported if the section is inside a for loop.

UPFA supports partition UPF integration [PIntegration] in CSV format to describe
integration work. UPFA analyzes the partition UPF file to get information, generate network
and connection automatically. UPFA generator takes CSV file and partition UPF as input
and output of the top level integrated UPF file.
Figure 1

Partition UF Integration

[PIntegration]
SCOPE,UPF [, LOW_CONN_INTEG, CONDITION, IS_MACRO]
[PROPAGATE_SS, PROPAGATE_PSTATE, INTERNAL_SUPPLY, COMMON_PD,
COMMON_POWER, COMMON_GROUND, COMMON_NWELL, COMMON_PWELL]

Specifies the scope to load the UPF file.
* UPF
UPF file to be loaded.
* LOW_CONN_INTEG (Optional)
The value can be:
#YES#: Automatically connect top-level supply net logic net with block UPF supply
port/logic port. The default value is #YES#.
#NO#: No connection.
* CONDITION (Optional)
Expression specified for integrating partition UPF. It can be:
#IF#{<condition>}
#ELIF#{<condition>}
#ELSE#
* IS_MACRO (Optional)
Specifies macro or not. It can be:
The default value is #NO#. By default, the connection of sub blocks is also generated
inside the condition. If this value is #YES#, then the connection is generated outside the
condition.
* PROPAGATE_SS (Optional)
Creates a supply set or supply net. This option takes effect only when LOW_CONN_INTEG
is #YES#.

Creates a supply set with same supply functions in block UPF. In block UPF, if
the supply function is not connected to the supply port, this supply net cannot be
propagated and is discarded. If all supply functions are not connected to the supply
port, this supply set is not propagated and discarded.
It can be:
The default value is #YES#
* PROPAGATE_PSTATE
Specifies power state and propagation in SoC UPF. This option takes effect only when
LOW_CONN_INTEG and PROPAGATE_SS are #YES#.
In the following cases, the state is discarded:
Supply set state with logic expression is not supported.
Existing objects (supply set) cannot be propagated.
The power state of power domain is discarded.
In the power state group and the power state table if the state's objects include power
domain, supply net, supply port, logic port, and logic net, the state is discarded. The
power domain cannot be propagated. The power state table does not support supply
net and supply port. The power state group does not support logic port and logic net.
It can be:
The default value is #YES#
* INTERNAL_SUPPLY (Optional)
A supply that does not create a supply port at top level is considered an internal supply.
* COMMON_PD
Specify the name to create top-level power domain.
#EMPTY#: Specified when top-level power domain creation is not required.

Default is PD_TOP
Creates a supply set named SS_<COMMON_PD> as the primary supply set of COMMON_PD.

* COMMON_POWER (Optional)
Specify common power supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates a supply net only.
The default value is the most common power supply net for all partitions. UPFA
automatically identifies the default value. If automatic identification fails, the default
value is VDD.
This option is the power function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).
* COMMON_GROUND (Optional)
Specify common ground supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates a supply net only.
The default value is the most common ground supply net for all partitions. UPFA
automatically identifies the default value. If automatic identification fails, the default
value is VSS.
This option is the ground function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).
* COMMON_NWELL (Optional)
Specify common nwell supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates the supply net only.

The default value is the most common nwell net for all partitions. UPFA automatically
identifies the default value.
This option is the nwell function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).
* COMMON_PWELL (Optional)
Specify common pwell supply net in the following format:
<direction>{<resolve>{<Port/Net Name>}}

Following is the format for all possible cases:
#IN#|#OUT#|#INOUT#{#PARALLEL#|#ONE_HOT#|#PARALLEL_ONE_HOT#{<Port/Net
Name>}}

If you specify a direction attribute, UPFA creates a supply port and connects it to the
supply net with the same name. Otherwise, it creates the supply net only.
The default value is the most common pwell net for all partitions. UPFA automatically
identifies the default value.
This option is the pwell function of the primary supply set (SS_<COMMON_PD>).

Key points to Note:
If common power, ground, nwell, or pwell is not defined, UPFA performs automatic
identification as follows:
1. Initially, if a supply set specified in the block UPF can be propagated, the priority
is to get the most frequent power, ground, nwell, or pwell supply functions as
COMMON_POWER/COMMON_GROUND/COMMON_NWELL/COMMON_PWELL.
If the identification of COMMON_POWER is a success and COMMON_NWELL is a
fail, then COMMON_POWER is assigned to COMMON_NWELL.
If the identification of COMMON_GROUND is a success and COMMON_PWELL is a
fail, then COMMON_GROUND is assigned to COMMON_PWELL.
2. For inappropriate supply set or failed identification in the first step, UPFA identifies
the power and ground from the supply net. It treats the supply net with a name
starting with VSS (case insensitive, Vss, vss, and so on) as ground supply net.
Others are treated as power supply net. The most frequent ground supply net is
treated as COMMON_GROUND and the most frequent power supply net is treated as
COMMON_POWER.
3. If there is no inappropriate supply net or failed identification in the second step, UPFA
sets COMMON_POWER and COMMON_GROUND with the default value.

Implicit Naming Rule
This chapter describes the naming rule for the tool to generate implicit name for different
objects in the following sections:
* Supply net
* Supply port
* Power Switch
* Isolation Naming
* Level Shifter Naming

Supply net
VDD_<supply function>_of_<supply_set>[_<count>]
VSS[_<count>]

VDD is used as prefix for power and VSS is used as prefix for ground.
Verdi adds _<count> when there is a name conflict.

Supply port
VDD[_<direction>]_<supply function>_of_<supply
set>[_<count>]
VSS[_<direction>]

VDD is used as prefix for power and VSS is used as prefix for ground.
Verdi ignores _<direction> when its value is in.

Chapter 6: Implicit Naming Rule
Power Switch

Verdi adds _<count> when there is a name conflict.

Power Switch
PSW_<supply set>[_<count>]
* in_<count>
* out
* ctrl_<count>
* ack_<count>
* on_<input supply port>
* off_<count>
You can use PSW_ as prefix for power switch.
* in_<count>: input supply ports
* out: output supply ports
* ctrl_<count>: control ports
* ack_<count>: ack ports
* on_<input supply port>: on states
* off_<count>: off states

Isolation Naming
ISO_{pd_name}_<C{clamp_value}/NoIso>_{src_name}_{sink_name}_{object_name}

Example: ISO_PD1_C0_SS1_SS2_OUTPUTS

Level Shifter Naming
LS_{pd_name}_<H2L/L2H/NoShift>_{src_name}_{sink_name}_{object_name}

Example: LS_PD1_H2L_SS1_SS2_IN

General Limitations

* For the condition command if elseif else, the condition branch to apply cannot be

* In some cases, Tcl variable or Tcl [] evaluation expression usage might not be legal
if the corresponding csv attribute does not accept Tcl value or Tcl expression. For
example, the following specification is not valid:

* UPFA supports set_scope from current scope. It does not support set_scope from
root or set_scope without -scope.
The set_scope command should be used in pairs, the first set_scope should only
have scope_name and no ../ or ./. The second set_scope should contain only ../ to
return to the scope before you call set_scope. For example:

(now at /top/a/b)

(now at /top/a/b/c)

because the depth of scope does not match)

(now at /top/a)
set_scope ../

You can use Tcl variable as first set_scope, but you should make sure that the second
set_scope has the correct number of "../" to return to the correct scope, or you might
get different output.

* Since upf2csv can neither treat the end of option "--" as a string nor consider the
position of "--" to treat the following arguments as string for the switch command, the
following case is acceptable in Tcl but NOT in upf2csv:

Introduction
UPFA provides Tcl commands to specify detailed categories in the constraint file. This
feature allows you to specify the strategies to generate the UPF designs in a different
design flow.

Use Model
Following is the use model:
ugo_generate -c constraint_file -v [2.0|2.1|3.0|3.1]

Tcl Commands

You can specify the categories in a constraint file. It is a Tcl-based script file. The following
figure shows the detailed format of the constraint file:
Figure 69

Category Format

Tcl Commands
UPFA supports the following new Tcl commands:

create_category
You can use the create_category Tcl command to create a new category with specified
UPF command list.
create_category category_name -cmds { upf_command_list }

Where, the -cmds option allows you to specify the UPF command list.
create_category switch -cmds { create_power_switch}

All create_power_switch commands are generated in the ugo_switch.upf
file.
* UPFA decides the order of UPF commands if sub UPF meets the correct power intent.
See section UPF Commands Supported by UPFA for more information. For example,
consider the following command:
create_category example -cmds { set_isolation create_power_domain }

In this example, power domain should be created before set_isolation. UPF resolves
the order issue to create_power_domain first.
Error handling

Tcl Commands

An error message is issued if the specified command is not in the UPF LRM or not a
special keyword type.

gen_upf
You can use the gen_upf Tcl command to specify how to generate the UPF design with
specified categories.
gen_upf upf_file_name -c {category_list}

Where,
-c: Allows you to specify the category list

gen_upf file.upf -c { logical physical library}

In this example, three sub UPF files (ugo_logical.upf, ugo_physical.upf, and
ugo_library.upf) are loaded in the file.upf file.
Key Points to Note
* The sub UPF file name would have prefix ugo_.
* The format of file name is ugo_<category name>.upf.
* The order of sub UPF in the top wrapper UPF file is same as the order specified in
gen_upf.
For example: gen_upf -c {first second third}
In this example, in the top wrapper upf, load_upf order would be ugo_first.upf,
ugo_second.upf, and then ugo_third.upf.
* For [Variable] section, the ugo_variable.upf file is created and loaded in the
beginning.
* For [Script] section, source commands are created and written in the top UPF
directly.
The script with #BEGIN# is sourced after load_upf ugo_variable.upf.
The script with #END# is sourced at the end of top wrapper UPF file.
Error handling
An error message is issued if the specified category_name is not defined.

UPFA issues the [REDUNDANT_SPECIFIED_CMD] warning message if the
specified UPF commands in create_category are not used for specific UPF
version.

Appendix B: ISOGEN Native Support in UPFA
The following sections describe the ISOGEN native support in UPFA in detail:

Introduction
The ISOGEN tool is a set of scripts that operate on post-process of a VCLP run on an
RTL+UPF design that has no isolation strategies. Based on the ISO_STRATEGY_MISSING
violations and other options, ISOGEN creates isolation strategies in the UPF that are used
in the source UPF. The ISOGEN tool feature and functionality is natively supported in
UPFA.

Prerequisites
RTL design should be ready in UPFA (using ugo_vlog_analyze, ugo_elaborate, or
ugo_include_vclp_script)
The template UPF file should be passed by VCLP.

ugo_optimize_power_intent
-isogen

[-upf <template.upf>]
[-iso_config <iso config file>]
[-dump_cross_domain <iso info file>]
[-dump_iso_domain <iso info file>]
[-v 2.0||3.0]
[-map_iso]
[-allow_unconnected]
[-src_sink_iso]
[-strict_lrm]
[-iso_place <source|sink>]
[-hetero_iso]
[-wrapper_upf <generated wrapper UPF file name>]
-hier_isogen
[-upf <template.upf>]
[-hier_iso_config <hierarchical iso config file>]
[-v 2.0|3.0]
[-map_iso]
[-strict_lrm]
[-iso_place <source|sink>]
[-hetero_iso]
[-wrapper_upf <generated wrapper UPF file name>]

* -isogen: Enables the ISOGEN flow.
* -upf: Specifies the UPF file input to the ISOGEN flow.
* -iso_config: Specifies the isolation configuration file. The configuration file is in JSON
format.
* -dump_cross_domain: Generates all cross-domain settings required for the UPF. The
output is saved to <iso info file>.
* -dump_iso_domain: Generates all required isolation domain settings required for the
UPF. The output is saved to <iso info file>.
* -v: Specifies the generated UPF version for the isolation command. The supported
versions are 2.0 and 3.0.
* -map_iso: Generates the isolation command along with map_isolation_cell.
* -src_sink_iso: Generates -source/-sink type isolation policy.
* -strict_lrm: Generates UPF by strictly following the UPF LRM.
* -wrapper_upf: Specifies the output wrapper UPF file name.
* -hier_isogen: Enables the hierarchical ISOGEN flow. You cannot use this option with
-isogen.

Inputs

* -iso_place: Specifies source or sink. Allows you to set up the preference of inserting
isolation at the source domain or sink domain.
* -hetero_iso: Handles hetero isolation fanout scenario and inserts isolation at the sink
domain.

Inputs
* iso.config: Configuration file (JSON format) to specify isolation strategy information
for ISOGEN.
* hier_iso.config: Configuration file (JSON format) to specify isolation strategy
information for hierarchical ISOGEN.
* template.upf: The UPF file processed to generate isolation strategy. It should be
passed by VCLP.

Usage Model
Use Model-1
ugo_vlog_analyze ### import design by UPFA
ugo_elaborate ### elaborate design by UPFA
ugo_optimize_power_intent -isogen -iso_config
template.upf

iso.config -upf

Use Model-2
ugo_include_vclp_script -f to_vclp.tcl
### the script should contains
analyze, elaborate, read_upf
ugo_optimize_power_intent -isogen -iso_config iso.config

Use Model-3
ugo_include_vclp_script -f to_vclp.tcl
### the script should contains
analyze, elaborate
ugo_optimize_power_intent -isogen -upf template.upf -iso_config
iso.config

Output
* <template>_isolation.upf
With missing isolation strategy commands in the UPF.
* <template>_wrapper.upf

Isolation Configuration File Format

With sourced template.upf and template_isolation.upf.
source template.upf
source template_isolation.upf

* For isolation supply, -isolation_supply is used in UPF 3.0 and
-isolation_supply_set is used in UPF 2.0.
* The map_isolation_cell command is generated along with each isolation strategy
with the following rule:
map_isolation_cell <iso name> -domain <domain> -lib_cells <cell name>

Where, <cell name> is the following under specific criteria:
$FW_AND_CELL: Default value
$FW_OR_CELL: When the isolation's clamp value is 1
$FW_CLOCK_CELL: When the isolation has clock type element (should be defined in
clock.list)
You must set the above three TCL variables before using the isolation.upf file.
set FW_AND_CELL <iso cell for clamp value 0>
set FW_OR_CELL <iso cell for clamp value 1>
set FW_CLOCK_CELL <iso cell for clock>

Isolation Configuration File Format
You must specify isolation signal, isolation clamp, and isolation sense under specific
condition to generate complete isolation strategy commands. The isolation configuration
file helps UPFA to complete the missing isolation strategy commands. The following code
shows the format of the isolation configuration file:
{

"spa_clamp_files": {
"0": [ "spa_clamp_0.list" ],
"1": [ "spa_clamp_1.list" ],
"Z": [],
"latch": []
},
"clamp_value_info_files": {
"0": [ "isolation_clamp_0.list" ],
"1": [ "isolation_clamp_1.list" ],
"Z": [],
"latch": []
},
"diff_ctrl_info_files": [ "diff_ctrl.list" ],
"clock_info_files": [ "clock.list" ],

Isolation Configuration File Format

}

"include_info_files": [ "include.list" ],
"exclude_info_files": [ "exclude.list" ],
"isolation_info": [
{
"include_files": [ "isolation_template.info" ]
}
]

The config template is at the following location:
$VERDI_HOME/share/ugo/etc/iso_gen

The isolation configuration file (iso.config) is a JSON file. It contains the following
ISOGEN information:
* clamp_value_info_files
This field specifies a list of files. The files contain the signals to specify the clamp value.
Format of the file: only the signal name is required, and regex is supported:
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

The file is a list of signals (wildcard supported) that are intended to be clamped
at values. For example, IP can include signals that must be isolated to 1 inside
pcf20_aon_clamp1.list and isolation_clamp1.list.
* diff_ctrl_info_files
Specifies a list of files.
You can list the signals in a file to let the flow know the signals to isolate with a different
control signal. Only signal name is required, and regex is supported.
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

* isolation_info
You can specify two types of JSON objects in this block. One is to specify the
included file and the other is to specify the information explicitly. The keyword is
include_files. Once the keyword is present, it is the first kind of JSON object. Other
keywords (like source_domain, sink_domain, and so on) are ignored.
* spa_clamp_files
This field specifies a list of files. The files contain the signals to specify the
set_port_attributes clamp value.

Isolation Configuration File Format

Format of the file: only the signal name is required, and regex is supported:
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

* include_files
Specifies a list of files that represent the isolation information with the following format:
<source power domain>,<destination power domain>, <isolation
control signal>,<isolation supply>,<isolation location>,<duplicate
or not>,<isolation sense>,<source or sink>, <isolation clamp>,
<isolation cells>

The duplicate keyword should be specified. If keyword is present, the signals
specified in diff_ctrl_info_fils apply isolation control specified with duplicate.
The source or sink keyword should be specified if it must be forced to insert at the
source/sink domain.
* clock_info_files (optional)
Specifies a list of files.
Clock signals (wildcard supported) and isolation cells are used for clock signals.
The clock signals apply Cell: $FW_CLOCK_CELL
The clamp value 1 applies Cell: $FW_OR_CELL
The clamp value latch applies Cell: $FW_LATCH_CELL
By default, Cell: $FW_AND_CELL is applied
Only signal name is required, regex is supported:
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

* include_info_files (optional)
Specifies a list of files. To force isolation on certain signals as desired by IPs, ISOGEN
includes the signals in the file under the generated isolation strategy. The signals
should be defined with the complete hierarchy path with respect to the top module.
Following is the format:
<source power domain>,<sink power domain>,<clock or normal>,<clamp
value>,<signal with full hierarchical path>

Example: PD1,PD2,normal,0,unit1/sigA

Hierarchical Isolation Configuration File Format

The unit1/sigA element is added to the elements list of the generated isolation
command with matching cross domain as follows:
<source power domain>,<sink power domain>, and the clamp_value <clamp
value>

If no isolation command is generated with the specified constraint, the signal is ignored:
(1) crossing-domain <src domain>, <sink domain> and (2) clamp value
<clamp value>

* exclude_info_files (optional)
Specifies a list of files.
The format of the files should be the list of signals (wildcard supported).
SigA
.*SigB_.*

When this list is provided, ISOGEN excludes the signals included for isolation.
The flavor of regular expression is Python style.
Matching mechanism is performed. For example, signal name is
top/a1/a2/pdd_exx_pert

The pattern pdd_exx_pert, pdd_exx_p.* matches.
The pattern pdd_exx does not match.

Hierarchical Isolation Configuration File Format
You must specify partition scope, partition UPF, and partition isolation configuration file to
generate partition isolation strategy. The following code shows the format of the isolation
configuration file:
{

"PARTITION": [
{"SCOPE":"paracemem", "UPF":"${UPF_INSTALL_DIR}/paracemem.upf",
"ISO_CONFIG":"config_iso/isogen_paracemem.config",
"ISO_CONSTRAINT":"config_iso/isogen_paracemem.constraint"},
{"SCOPE":"parcfmia", "UPF":"${UPF_INSTALL_DIR}/parcfmia.upf",
"ISO_CONFIG":"config_iso/isogen_parcfmia.config"},
{"SCOPE":"parcse", "UPF":"${UPF_INSTALL_DIR}/parcse.upf",
"ISO_CONFIG":"config_iso/isogen_parcse.config"}
]

}

Hierarchical Isolation Configuration File Format

The hierarchical isolation configuration file (hier_iso.config) is a JSON file. It contains
the following ISOGEN information:
* SCOPE: Specifies the partition name required to generate isolation.
* UPF: Specifies the partition UPF file for generating the partition wrapper UPF file.
* ISO_CONFIG: Specifies the partition isolation configuration file for generating isolation.
* ISO_CONSTRAINT: Optional. Specifies the partition isolation constraint file for generating
isolation.

ugoDetailViewInsertCopiedRows

Allows you to insert rows containing data at a specified row position.
ugoDetailViewInsertCopiedRows -row [row_pos] -value [copied_data]

-row

Specifies the row position to insert. Should be followed by row_pos.
row_pos

-Value

Specify the data of the rows to insert. Should be followed by copied_data.

ugoDetailViewInsertCopiedRows -row 1 -value \
"PSW1%^&SW1%^&PD_SD1%^&6%^&
VDD%^&VDD%^&POWER_SW1"

ugoDetailViewInsertCopiedColumns -column [column_pos] -table
[table_index] -value [copied_data]

-column

Specifies the column position to insert. Should be followed by column_pos.
column _pos

The number specifies the column position to insert. Should be used with -table
-table

Specify the table index to insert. Should be followed by table_index.
table_index

Specifies the table index to insert. Should be used with -table.
-value

Specify the data of the columns to insert. Should be followed by copied_data.
copied_data

The string specifies the data of the rows to be insert. Should be used with -value.
ugoDetailViewInsertCopiedColumns -column 1 -value
"STATE%^&SS2%&OFF%^&OFF%&

ugoShowUPFInVerdi
ugoShowUPFInVerdi

Invokes Verdi to show the power design of the currently opened CSV files or specified
UPF file name.
ugoShowUPFInVerdi -file [upf_file_name]

-file
Specifies the UPF file which must be shown in Verdi. If this argument is not specified,
Verdi shows the power intent of the currently opened CSV file.
upf_file_name

Allows you to specify the absolute or relative path of the UPF file name.

ugoShowUPFInVerdi -file [test.upf]

Implicit Naming Rule
This chapter describes the naming rule for the tool to generate implicit name for different
objects in the following sections:
* Supply net
* Supply port
* Power Switch
* Isolation Naming
* Level Shifter Naming

Supply net
VDD_<supply function>_of_<supply_set>[_<count>]
VSS[_<count>]

title: 2 -table 1 -count 3
text:
VDD is used as prefix for power and VSS is used as prefix for ground.
Verdi adds _<count> when there is a name conflict.

Introduction
UPFA provides Tcl commands to specify detailed categories in the constraint file. This
feature allows you to specify the strategies to generate the UPF designs in a different
design flow.

Use Model
Following is the use model:
ugo_generate -c constraint_file -v [2.0|2.1|3.0|3.1]

Tcl Commands

You can specify the categories in a constraint file. It is a Tcl-based script file. The following
figure shows the detailed format of the constraint file:
Figure 69

Category Format

Tcl Commands
UPFA supports the following new Tcl commands:

create_category
You can use the create_category Tcl command to create a new category with specified
UPF command list.
create_category category_name -cmds { upf_command_list }

Where, the -cmds option allows you to specify the UPF command list.
create_category switch -cmds { create_power_switch}

All create_power_switch commands are generated in the ugo_switch.upf
file.
* UPFA decides the order of UPF commands if sub UPF meets the correct power intent.
See section UPF Commands Supported by UPFA for more information. For example,
consider the following command:
create_category example -cmds { set_isolation create_power_domain }

In this example, power domain should be created before set_isolation. UPF resolves
the order issue to create_power_domain first.

Tcl Commands

An error message is issued if the specified command is not in the UPF LRM or not a

gen_upf
You can use the gen_upf Tcl command to specify how to generate the UPF design with
specified categories.
gen_upf upf_file_name -c {category_list}

Where,
-c: Allows you to specify the category list

gen_upf file.upf -c { logical physical library}

In this example, three sub UPF files (ugo_logical.upf, ugo_physical.upf, and
ugo_library.upf) are loaded in the file.upf file.
Key Points to Note
* The sub UPF file name would have prefix ugo_.
* The format of file name is ugo_<category name>.upf.
* The order of sub UPF in the top wrapper UPF file is same as the order specified in
gen_upf.
For example: gen_upf -c {first second third}
In this example, in the top wrapper upf, load_upf order would be ugo_first.upf,
ugo_second.upf, and then ugo_third.upf.
* For [Variable] section, the ugo_variable.upf file is created and loaded in the
beginning.
* For [Script] section, source commands are created and written in the top UPF
directly.
The script with #BEGIN# is sourced after load_upf ugo_variable.upf.
The script with #END# is sourced at the end of top wrapper UPF file.
Error handling
An error message is issued if the specified category_name is not defined.

UPFA issues the [REDUNDANT_SPECIFIED_CMD] warning message if the
specified UPF commands in create_category are not used for specific UPF
version.

Figure 70

Simple Example

* Based on the specified categories in the constraint file, UPFA generates the following
five sub UPF files:
ugo_logical.upf, ugo_physical.upf, ugo_library.upf, ugo_switch.upf, and
ugo_set.upf

UPFA also generates the following two top UPF files:
file.upf and name.upf

* If there is a [Variable] section in the power intent CSV file, UPFA generates the
ugo_variable.upf file and loads it inside top wrapper UPF. If there is no [Variable]
section in the CSV, then the ugo_variable.upf file is not generated.
* If there is a [Script] section in the power intent CSV file, and if the script contains
#BEGIN#, it is sourced at the beginning of top wrapper UPF file. If the script contains
#END#, it is sourced at the end of the top wrapper UPF file. Otherwise, if there is no
corresponding CSV, then sourced commands are not generated inside the top wrapper
UPF file.
* The following three sub UPF files are loaded in the top UPF file file.upf:
ugo_logical.upf, ugo_physical.upf, ugo_library.upf

Specifying Category Using UPF Commands

With ugo_variable.upf for [Variable] and source command for [Script], the paths
in [Script] are directly used in top wrapper UPF as shown in the following file.upf
example:
/// file.upf ///
/// gen_upf file.upf -c { logical physical library }
set dir [file dirname [info script]]
load_upf ${dir}/ugo_variable.upf
source pre_script.tcl
load_upf ${dir}/ugo_logical.upf
load_upf ${dir}/ugo_physical.upf
load_upf ${dir}/ugo_library.upf
source post_script.tcl

* The following three sub UPF files are loaded in the top UPF file name.upf:
ugo_logical.upf, ugo_switch.upf, ugo_set.upf

Priority

If the purpose is not specified, all connect_supply_net commands are
generated together in the ugo_csn.upf file.
create_category csn -cmds { connect_supply_net:top_port}
gen_upf csn.upf -c { csn}

All connect_supply_net commands with top_port purpose are generated together in
the ugo_csn.upf file.
Key Points to Note
* If keyword is not specified, all create_supply_net commands are covered.
* An error is issued if usage is mixed (with no keyword and with keyword) in single
category. For example:
create_category cat1 -cmds { connect_supply_net:top_port
connect_supply_net }

* UPFA reports a warning message if a command specified does not meet conditions of
any of specified. For example, if power intent contains following:
connect_supply_net -ports p1/VDD SS1.power

A warning is issued if no category is specified:
connect_supply_net:hier_supply_set

Priority
If you specify both -upf option and gen_upf command in a constraint file, the gen_upf
command has the higher priority.

Error and Warning Handling
* In the gen_upf command, if certain UPF command is specified multiple times in the
category_list, UPFA issues a warning message and generates UPF design without
any error recovery.
* UPFA issues the following warning message if power intent CSV defines some
spec (for example, PSW), but corresponding UPF command (for example,
create_power_switch) is not mapped to any category, including the command with
keyword.

UPF Commands Supported by UPFA

UPF Commands Supported by UPFA
The following commands are supported by UPFA to generate UPF command. You can
specify these commands inside create_category. All sub UPF files follow this order to
generate UPF commands.

Key Points to Note
* [set tclvar], [source pre-script], [source post-script] are fixed and cannot
be specified in any category. These are generated in the top-wrap UPF file.
* The create_supply_set command dominates create_supply_set:keyword and
connect_supply_net dominates connect_supply_net:keyword.
create_category cat { create_supply_set } is equal to
create_category cat { create_supply_set:no_func
create_supply_set:func_supply_set create_supply_set:func_supply_net
create_supply_set:others }
create_category cat { connect_supply_net } is equal to
create_category cat { connect_supply_net:top_port
connect_supply_net:hier_supply_set connect_supply_net:hier_supply_net
connect_supply_net:others }

* The use_interface_cell command dominates the map_isolation_cell and
map_level_shifter_cell commands.
* The create_power_state_group and describe_state_transition commands are
supported only for UPF 3.0. The create_pst and add_pst_state commands are
supported only for UPF 2.0.

Rules:
If the same supply net is specified multiple times in the [Power Domain Intent]
table, generated create_supply_set commands should refer to that object by
supply net name only once. The rest of the occurrences are referred to as supply
set function.
Single create_supply_set command should not mix supply net name and supply
set function. Instead, generate separate create_supply_set commands for each
kind to be directed to separate sub UPF.
The create_supply_set command without -update should not refer to its own
function. Instead, generate two create_supply_set commands, one for definition
and the other for updating with function.
When choosing the occurrence to use the supply net name for rule 1, scan power
and ground in the table and choose the first occurrence, and then scan nwell and
pwell and choose the first occurrence.

Introduction
The ISOGEN tool is a set of scripts that operate on post-process of a VCLP run on an
RTL+UPF design that has no isolation strategies. Based on the ISO_STRATEGY_MISSING
violations and other options, ISOGEN creates isolation strategies in the UPF that are used
in the source UPF. The ISOGEN tool feature and functionality is natively supported in
UPFA.

ugo_include_vclp_script)

text:
* -isogen: Enables the ISOGEN flow.
* -upf: Specifies the UPF file input to the ISOGEN flow.
* -iso_config: Specifies the isolation configuration file. The configuration file is in JSON
format.
* -dump_cross_domain: Generates all cross-domain settings required for the UPF. The
output is saved to <iso info file>.
* -dump_iso_domain: Generates all required isolation domain settings required for the
UPF. The output is saved to <iso info file>.
* -v: Specifies the generated UPF version for the isolation command. The supported
versions are 2.0 and 3.0.
* -map_iso: Generates the isolation command along with map_isolation_cell.
* -src_sink_iso: Generates -source/-sink type isolation policy.
* -strict_lrm: Generates UPF by strictly following the UPF LRM.
* -wrapper_upf: Specifies the output wrapper UPF file name.
* -hier_isogen: Enables the hierarchical ISOGEN flow. You cannot use this option with
-isogen.

title: 2 -table 1 -count 3
text:
Inputs

* -iso_place: Specifies source or sink. Allows you to set up the preference of inserting
isolation at the source domain or sink domain.
* -hetero_iso: Handles hetero isolation fanout scenario and inserts isolation at the sink
domain.

Inputs
* iso.config: Configuration file (JSON format) to specify isolation strategy information
for ISOGEN.
* hier_iso.config: Configuration file (JSON format) to specify isolation strategy
information for hierarchical ISOGEN.
* template.upf: The UPF file processed to generate isolation strategy. It should be
passed by VCLP.

Usage Model
Use Model-1
ugo_vlog_analyze ### import design by UPFA
ugo_elaborate ### elaborate design by UPFA

template.upf

iso.config

Output
* <template>_isolation.upf
With missing isolation strategy commands in the UPF.
* <template>_wrapper.upf

Isolation Configuration File Format

With sourced template.upf and template_isolation.upf.
source template.upf
source template_isolation.upf

* For isolation supply, -isolation_supply is used in UPF 3.0 and
-isolation_supply_set is used in UPF 2.0.
* The map_isolation_cell command is generated along with each isolation strategy
with the following rule:
map_isolation_cell <iso name> -domain <domain> -lib_cells <cell name>

Where, <cell name> is the following under specific criteria:
$FW_AND_CELL: Default value
$FW_OR_CELL: When the isolation's clamp value is 1
$FW_CLOCK_CELL: When the isolation has clock type element (should be defined in
clock.list)
You must set the above three TCL variables before using the isolation.upf file.
set FW_AND_CELL <iso cell for clamp value 0>
set FW_OR_CELL <iso cell for clamp value 1>
set FW_CLOCK_CELL <iso cell for clock>

Isolation Configuration File Format
You must specify isolation signal, isolation clamp, and isolation sense under specific
condition to generate complete isolation strategy commands. The isolation configuration
file helps UPFA to complete the missing isolation strategy commands. The following code
shows the format of the isolation configuration file:
{

"spa_clamp_files": {
"0": [ "spa_clamp_0.list" ],
"1": [ "spa_clamp_1.list" ],
"Z": [],
"latch": []
},
"clamp_value_info_files": {
"0": [ "isolation_clamp_0.list" ],
"1": [ "isolation_clamp_1.list" ],
"Z": [],
"latch": []
},
"diff_ctrl_info_files": [ "diff_ctrl.list" ],
"clock_info_files": [ "clock.list" ],

Isolation Configuration File Format

}

"include_info_files": [ "include.list" ],
"exclude_info_files": [ "exclude.list" ],
"isolation_info": [
{
"include_files": [ "isolation_template.info" ]
}
]

The config template is at the following location:
$VERDI_HOME/share/ugo/etc/iso_gen

The isolation configuration file (iso.config) is a JSON file. It contains the following
ISOGEN information:
* clamp_value_info_files
This field specifies a list of files. The files contain the signals to specify the clamp value.
Format of the file: only the signal name is required, and regex is supported:
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

The file is a list of signals (wildcard supported) that are intended to be clamped
at values. For example, IP can include signals that must be isolated to 1 inside
pcf20_aon_clamp1.list and isolation_clamp1.list.
* diff_ctrl_info_files
Specifies a list of files.
You can list the signals in a file to let the flow know the signals to isolate with a different
control signal. Only signal name is required, and regex is supported.
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

* isolation_info
You can specify two types of JSON objects in this block. One is to specify the
included file and the other is to specify the information explicitly. The keyword is
include_files. Once the keyword is present, it is the first kind of JSON object. Other
keywords (like source_domain, sink_domain, and so on) are ignored.
* spa_clamp_files
This field specifies a list of files. The files contain the signals to specify the
set_port_attributes clamp value.

Isolation Configuration File Format

Format of the file: only the signal name is required, and regex is supported:
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

* include_files
Specifies a list of files that represent the isolation information with the following format:
<source power domain>,<destination power domain>, <isolation
control signal>,<isolation supply>,<isolation location>,<duplicate
or not>,<isolation sense>,<source or sink>, <isolation clamp>,
<isolation cells>

The duplicate keyword should be specified. If keyword is present, the signals
specified in diff_ctrl_info_fils apply isolation control specified with duplicate.
The source or sink keyword should be specified if it must be forced to insert at the
source/sink domain.
* clock_info_files (optional)
Specifies a list of files.
Clock signals (wildcard supported) and isolation cells are used for clock signals.
The clock signals apply Cell: $FW_CLOCK_CELL
The clamp value 1 applies Cell: $FW_OR_CELL
The clamp value latch applies Cell: $FW_LATCH_CELL
By default, Cell: $FW_AND_CELL is applied
Only signal name is required, regex is supported:
abc_tf_en
.*testing.*\[0\]

* include_info_files (optional)
Specifies a list of files. To force isolation on certain signals as desired by IPs, ISOGEN
includes the signals in the file under the generated isolation strategy. The signals
should be defined with the complete hierarchy path with respect to the top module.
Following is the format:
<source power domain>,<sink power domain>,<clock or normal>,<clamp
value>,<signal with full hierarchical path>

title: 2 -table 1 -count 3
text:
Hierarchical Isolation Configuration File Format

The unit1/sigA element is added to the elements list of the generated isolation
command with matching cross domain as follows:
<source power domain>,<sink power domain>, and the clamp_value <clamp
value>

If no isolation command is generated with the specified constraint, the signal is ignored:
(1) crossing-domain <src domain>, <sink domain> and (2) clamp value
<clamp value>

* exclude_info_files (optional)
Specifies a list of files.
The format of the files should be the list of signals (wildcard supported).
SigA
.*SigB_.*

When this list is provided, ISOGEN excludes the signals included for isolation.
The flavor of regular expression is Python style.
Matching mechanism is performed. For example, signal name is
top/a1/a2/pdd_exx_pert

The pattern pdd_exx_pert, pdd_exx_p.* matches.
The pattern pdd_exx does not match.

Hierarchical Isolation Configuration File Format
You must specify partition scope, partition UPF, and partition isolation configuration file to
generate partition isolation strategy. The following code shows the format of the isolation
configuration file:
{

"PARTITION": [
{"SCOPE":"paracemem", "UPF":"${UPF_INSTALL_DIR}/paracemem.upf",
"ISO_CONFIG":"config_iso/isogen_paracemem.config",
"ISO_CONSTRAINT":"config_iso/isogen_paracemem.constraint"},
{"SCOPE":"parcfmia", "UPF":"${UPF_INSTALL_DIR}/parcfmia.upf",
"ISO_CONFIG":"config_iso/isogen_parcfmia.config"},
{"SCOPE":"parcse", "UPF":"${UPF_INSTALL_DIR}/parcse.upf",
"ISO_CONFIG":"config_iso/isogen_parcse.config"}
]

}

Hierarchical Isolation Configuration File Format

The hierarchical isolation configuration file (hier_iso.config) is a JSON file. It contains
the following ISOGEN information:
* SCOPE: Specifies the partition name required to generate isolation.
* UPF: Specifies the partition UPF file for generating the partition wrapper UPF file.
* ISO_CONFIG: Specifies the partition isolation configuration file for generating isolation.
* ISO_CONSTRAINT: Optional. Specifies the partition isolation constraint file for generating
isolation.

Appendix C: UPFA Database Messages
The following sections list the UPFA database phase messages:
* Introduction
* Info Messages
* Warning Messages
* Error Messages

Introduction
This appendix lists the information, warning, and error messages that UPFA can report
during the database phase. Messages use the following format:
Severity-[phase][tag] Short description
formal description
[what next]

title: 2 -table 1 -count 3

Where:
* Severity is Info, Warning, or Error.
* phase is database for the messages in this appendix.
* tag is the unique message name.
* The formal description can include @(file,line) placeholders that are replaced with
the CSV or design file location when the message is issued.
* The what next guidance is optional and suggests how to resolve the issue.
You can change the severity of some of these messages by using the
ugo_set_rule_severity command. For more information about reporting and message
severity, see Commands for Power Intent and Command for Upgrading Message Severity.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Introduction
The Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) is a methodology for functional verification
using the SystemVerilog base class library. It allows you to construct class-based
verification environments using verification component objects. It also allows you to create
stimulus using sequence objects.
The UVM Debug solution in the Verdi Automated Debug Platform is designed to provide
you with sufficient information about the UVM verification environment. Information
that helps you understand the UVM architecture - class and object structure, resource/
configuration access, factory override and creation, phase transition and objection raise/
drop, sequence generation and execution - and to make the debug of UVM testbench
easier.
The Verdi platform supports debugging of UVM testbench designs as follows:
* View classes and objects in UVM mode in Class/Object Browser.
* Set predefined UVM related breakpoints, for example, break at phase_start() in the
Breakpoints form.
* View UVM component instance hierarchy and TLM port connectivities in the OVM/UVM
Hierarchy Tree
* View resource/configuration items in the testbench in the Resource View pane.
* View the set/get history of a resource/configuration item.
* View all the predefined and user-defined phases/domains and their transitions in the
Phase View pane.
* Set breakpoints on the important phases or on the phase methods of uvm_component.
* View raise/drop of the objections for a certain phase and other details.
* View factory object creation and override histories in the Factory View pane.
* View active and executed sequences with start/end time, executing thread,
corresponding sequencer and sequencer ID in the Sequence View pane.
* Cross-probing between UVM-aware windows and Object/Class Browser, source code
pane, Breakpoints form, and Watch pane.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Chapter 2: Introduction

* Convenient filtering mechanism to easily locate the information you want.
* View the access operation history (such as read and write) to the register models.
The main focus of this document is UVM Aware Debug windows under
Verdi's interactive mode. Verdi also provides UVM debug features for postprocess mode. For Example:
The OVM/UVM Hierarchy tree also support post-process. This is covered
in the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree Pane Usage section.
The Register View also supports post-process. This is covered in the
Debugging UVM Registers in Verdi Post-Processing Mode section.
The UVM transactions and sequences can be dumped into FSDB
by Verdi Transaction Recorder. It is displayed and analyzed in
Verdi Transaction Browser and Analyzer. See $VERDI_HOME/
doc/ Verdi_Transaction_Debug_Platform.pdf for more details.

Before You Begin
Before you begin using the UVM Debug capability, note the following:
* Verdi UVM Aware Debug feature windows require the UVM library from VCS or Verdi.
Use that library to get the full capabilities.
* To perform Interactive Debug, you need access to both Verdi and VCS. The VCS
release version must not be newer than the Verdi release version.
If the VCS release is older than the Verdi release, set VCS_UVM_HOME. This setting
directs VCS to use the Verdi UVM library:
% setenv VCS_UVM_HOME <Verdi_UVM_library_path>

* If you use a custom or third-party UVM library, merge Verdi instrumentations and
additions into that library. Contact Synopsys support for merge instructions.
* Without Verdi instrumentations and additions, your access to Verdi UVM debug
features is limited.
For example:
The factory creation history cannot be viewed in the Factory View pane.
The OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree is not accessible
The following sections describe how to compile the UVM testbench. They also describe
how to configure the Interactive Simulation Console mode. Use that mode to run
interactive UVM Debug features.

The following sections are included:
* Set Environment Variables
* Compile Designs With the UVM Libraries
* Configure the Simulation
* Points to Note

* Perform Interactive Simulation with UVM Aware Debug
* Behavior of OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree View at the Startup of the Simulation
* UVM Debug Panes

Set Environment Variables
The following environment variables must be set before compiling the UVM testbenches
and invoking the Verdi platform.
% setenv VCS_HOME <VCS_INST_DIR>
% setenv LD_LIBRARY_PATH <VERDI_INST_DIR>/share/PLI/VCS \
<PLATFORM>:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
You can also set these variables to help facilitate the script:
% setenv VERDI_HOME <VERDI_INST_DIR>
% setenv tab $VERDI_HOME/share/PLI/VCS/LINUXAMD64/novas.tab
% setenv pli $VERDI_HOME/share/PLI/VCS/LINUXAMD64/pli.a

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Compile Designs With the UVM Libraries
The following sections describe how you can compile a design with UVM libraries.
If you want to specify a different UVM library, you can use the VCS_UVM_HOME
environment variable to specify it.
The UVM debug features of Verdi are available under the -ntb_opts uvm option.
Alternately, you may specify the following options:
At parsing:
%vlogan -sverilog -kdb
+incdir+${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/src
${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/src/uvm_pkg.sv
+incdir+${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/verdi
${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/verdi/uvm_custom_install_verdi_recorder.sv
+incdir+${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/vcs
${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/vcs/uvm_custom_install_vcs_recorder.sv

At elaboration:
%vcs <my top> -kdb -debug_access \
${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/src/dpi/uvm_dpi.cc -CFLAGS "-DVCS"
${VCS_HOME}/etc/uvm/verdi/dpi/uvm_verdi_dpi.cpp
uvm_custom_install_recording
uvm_custom_install_verdi_recording

Compile With UVM
The current default UVM version is 1.1d. To use UVM-1.2, use -ntb_opts
uvm-1.2 instead of -ntb_opts uvm.
To use UVM-IEEE, use -ntb_opts uvm-ieee.
You can load UVM-IEEE-2020 library using the -ntb_opts uvm-ieee-2020
compile-time option.
You can load UVM-IEEE-2020-2.0 library using the -ntb_opts uvmieee-2020-2.0 compile-time option.
Add the -ntb_opts uvm and -debug_access[+argument] compile option for the UVM
library. For example:
% vcs -full64 -kdb -lca -debug_access+all -ntb_opts uvm-1.2 \ -sverilog
-l compile.log -timescale=1ns/1ns -V +incdir+../sv \ ubus_tb_top.sv

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
The -kdb option enables the UFE flow.
The -debug_access+thread option enables the debugging of the SystemVerilog threads.
This is the minimum debug option to record transactions and messages into FSDB.
For more information on the arguments supported with the -debug_access option, see the
VCS User Guide.
Compile in VCS UUM Flow
The examples used in the document are located in:
$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm-1.2/lib/examples/integrated/ubus/examples

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
To compile these examples with VCS, execute the following commands:
% vlogan -full64 -kdb -lca -timescale=1ns/1ns -ntb_opts uvm
% vlogan -full64 -kdb -lca -ntb_opts uvm +incdir+../sv ubus_tb_top.sv
% vcs -lca -kdb -debug_access+all -ntb_opts uvm ubus_tb_top -full64

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
The -debug_access[+argument] VCS option is available only with VCS
J-2014.12 or later versions.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Configure the Simulation
Simulation can be configured either in the Verification Compiler Platform flow or in Verdi
flow. The two configuration flows are documented as below:
* Import Design and Configure Simulation in Verdi
* Configure Simulation with UFE Flow

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Import Design and Configure Simulation in Verdi
To import a UVM Testbench design into Verdi, perform the following steps:
1. Invoke the Verdi platform and import the UVM testbench with the -uvmDebug option.
For example:
% verdi +UVM_TESTNAME=test_read_modify_write -uvmDebug \
-ntb_opts uvm -sv ./ubus_tb_top.sv +incdir+../sv

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
2. Use the Tools -> Preferences option in the nTrace main window to configure the
simulation options. Select the Simulation page on the Preferences form and follow
these steps:
a. Select VCS as the Simulator.
b. Type the path of the simulator executable file in the Executable Path field.
c. Add the desired simulator options in the Options field. For example, add the
+UVM_TESTNAME=test_read_modify_write option to specify a UVM example.
d. The UVM Debug option is automatically enabled when the -uvmDebug option is
added in the Verdi command line.
e. Click OK to complete the simulation settings.
Figure 1

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Preference Setting for UVM Interactive Debug

3. Run the simulation.
If the UVM Debug option is enabled in the Preferences form, the
+UVM_VERDI_TRACE=UVM_AWARE option is automatically added to the
interactive console.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Configure Simulation with UFE Flow
Perform the following steps to configure simulation with the UFE flow in the Verification
Compiler Platform environment:
1. Include the -kdb option during compilation in VCS as shown in the Figure 1
2. Execute simv -verdi or simv -gui=verdi in Verdi or simv -gui in the Verification
Compiler Platform environment.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Points to Note
By default, some data are not available in the UVM Aware Debug windows. You have to
specify special options for simv to record the data.
* If you want to view the sequence history in the Sequence View pane, add the
+UVM_TR_RECORD option to enable transaction recording
* If you want to view the OVM/UVM hierarchy tree, add the +UVM_VERDI_TRACE=HIER
option to enable OVM/UVM hierarchy tree and TLM port connectivity dumping.
However, if the OVM/UVM hierarchy tree is deep and complex, it may take a lot of time
to traverse all the OVM/UVM components. You can add the compilation directive in
compilation time, +define+VERDI_DHIER_INTERFACE_BY_CLASS_DEFN, which is used
to optimize the traverse time during building the UVM hierarchy tree. This optimization
works only if the runtime option, +UVM_VERDI_TRACE=HIER, is added.
* If you want to view the register read/write access history in the Register View, add the
+UVM_VERDI_TRACE=RAL option to enable register history dumping.
* If you want to view the register read/write access history in the Register View, add
the +UVM_VERDI_TRACE=RAL option at simulation runtime to enable register history
dumping. This option dumps the register hierarchy and access history data into the
FSDB file.
* If you specify the +UVM_VERDI_TRACE=MSG option, all UVM messages are recorded
into FSDB, but the messages are not displayed on console. You must use the
+UVM_VERDI_TRACE=MSG+PRINT option to view the UVM messages on console.

Perform Interactive Simulation with UVM Aware Debug
Prerequisite: Load the design and the UVM testbench in the Verdi platform and complete
the simulation configuration.
Perform the following steps to start the Interactive Simulation Debug mode:
1. Select Tools -> Run Simulation option to start the Interactive Simulation Debug mode.
After the simulation finishes execution phase, the Object, Member, Source Code,
and Interactive Console panes open automatically. All the defined classes and the
instantiations are shown with a hierarchical view in the Class pane.
2. Select an item either the Class or Object panes, to automatically display the related
content in the Member pane. In the Object pane, right-click the object and select the
Show in Class Browser option to view all the defined classes and the instantiations
are shown with a hierarchical view.
You can observe the hierarchical and dynamic changes of objects with the instances
trees in the Object pane.
Figure 2

Classes Derived from UVM Object and Object Names

3. Select the UVM Components or UVM Objects viewing modes in the Mode menu of
the Object pane to focus on the UVM library group of interest, as show in the following
Figure 3

Mode Menu in the Object Browser

4. After enabling the Interactive Simulation Debug mode, use the UVM Menu
associated with the UVM icon
Figure 4

to select the UVM panes, as shown in the following

UVM Debug Panes

You can also select the All Views option to select all the UVM Aware panes. Verdi
displays the UVM icon
in the toolbar only when the current loaded design includes
the UVM package. Otherwise, Verdi hides this icon in the toolbar. You can disable this
by setting the environment variable NOVAS_UVM_ICON_SHOW_DEPAND_UVM_PKG as 0. The
default value is 1.
If the -uvmDebug option is not added while invoking the Verdi platform and
the UVM Debug options are not enabled in the Preferences form, a warning
message is displayed when opening the UVM-Aware panes. The warning

message specify that the UVM debug features for interactive mode cannot be
completely supported with the above situation.

Behavior of OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree View at the Startup of the
Simulation
The following is the behavior of the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree View at the startup of the
simulation:
Mode

is

text:
The OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree View status (hidden/display) is saved to the novas.rc file.
If you invoke Verdi next time, the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree View status is the same as
last time you exit Verdi (if novas.rc file exists).

UVM Debug Panes
The UVM Debug feature support is integrated with the Interactive Simulation Debug
mode in the Verdi platform. The OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree view is docked in the same

location as the Object Browser and Class Browser. The UVM related panes are opened
and docked automatically as new tabs in the same location as the Interactive Console
tab of the Message pane after selecting the All Views option in the UVM menu as shown in
the following figure:
Figure 5

UVM Aware Layout

The UVM Debug panes: the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree View, Resource View, Factory
View, Phase View, Sequence View and Register View panes are described in the following
chapters. You can drag and drop or dock/undock these panes the same as other panes in
the Verdi platform to the desired location as needed.

UVM Debug Usage
This chapter contains the following topics:
* OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree Pane Usage
* Specifying UVM Runtime Options
* Save/Restore Session Support in UVM Aware Debug
* Resource View
* Factory View
* Phase View
* Sequence View

* Multitasking Task
* Debugging UVM Registers in Verdi Post-Processing Mode

The options in each of these views are documented in the UVM Interactive
Simulation Debug chapter of the Verdi Command Reference Guide.

The Verdi platform supports the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree pane to display the component
hierarchy of a testbench. The OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree pane is docked at the upper left
corner of the main window, when invoked. Along with the other UVM Aware window, it is
invoked from the

UVM/OVM/VMM Debug Windows icon.

When you select a component in the OVM/UVM Tree Hierarchy pane, you can view the
detailed information of the component, perform a search in the tree hierarchy, drag and
drop components from the hierarchy tree to the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer and
vice versa.

OVM/UVM hierarchy tree supports both interactive and post-process
mode. If you want to view the OVM/UVM hierarchy tree, add the
+UVM_VERDI_TRACE=HIER option at simulation runtime to enable OVM/UVM
hierarchy tree and TLM port connectivity dumping.

Tree pane.
Figure 7

For more information regarding the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree pane right-click option
menu, see the Verdi Command Reference Guide.

View Detailed Information
Select the Show Detailed Information option from the right-click option menu in the
OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree pane to view the detailed information for the Show Creation
and Show Connections options. A new panel is created with three tabs: Creation,
Connection, and Connected Path.
The Connection and Connected Path tabs are available only when the
selected node is a port/export.

The connection parameters of a component is shown in the following figure:
Figure 8

Detailed Information Folders

Tab Name

Creation

Displays the Call Stack creation for the selected node.
On double-clicking on the node in the Call Stack list, the
source code of the corresponding node is displayed in
the Source Code pane.

Connection

This folder is enabled only on selecting a port in the
OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree pane The following fields are
displayed:
Connection: Displays multiple port connections of the
selected port.
Call Stack grid: Displays the Call Stack of the
connection corresponding to the value that appears in
the Connection field.

Connection Paths

This folder is enabled only on selecting a port in the
OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree pane. The following fields
are displayed:
Path: For a multi-path selection, the last three
segments of a path are displayed. If a port has multiple
paths, switch to the port connection folder in the port
grid.
Ports: Displays connection details. Double-click a grid
item to switch the definition.

Creation Tab Usage
The Creation tab displays the calling sequence (Call Stack) of the instrumentation code
tracking the component creation in the testbench. #0 represents the top of the Call Stack
while a bigger number represents a deeper level in the Call Stack.
Double-click other levels in the Call Stack to examine the corresponding statement in the
Source Code pane.
Figure 9

Call Stack Information in the Creation Tab

Connection Tab
The Connection tab displays the calling sequence (Call Stack) of the instrumentation
code tracking the port connection in the testbench as shown in the following figure. #0
represents the top of the Call Stack while a bigger number represents a deeper level in the
Call Stack. By default, the statement that connects the port is highlighted.
Double-click other levels in the Call Stack to examine the corresponding statement in the

Verdi provides a right-click menu item Add to Waveform that you can use to dump a
component object to nWave window. To use this functionality, right-click on the component
object for which you want to dump the waveform to the nWave window, and select the
option Add to Waveform. The component object in the nWave window is shown in
Figure 21
The Add to Waveform menu option is only enabled when the selected
component object exists in FSDB.
In the interactive mode, this item is always enabled because the dumper can dump the
object values even if they are not dumped in the FDSB file. In the batch mode, this item
should be enabled in OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree when the component object exists in the
FSDB file. The operation of this menu item is in the following order:
1. If the object is not in FSDB, it is enabled for the dynamic object dumping.
2. Load the FSDB data of this object into nWave.
The operation is only applicable to single selection.

In the post-process mode, add +UVM_VERDI_TRACE=COMPWAVE as the
runtime option. Refer to the Viewing OVM/UVM Component Waveforms in
nWave chapter for detailed usage.

Difference Between a VIF and a VIF in a Non-Component Class
A VIF under a UVM component is a direct member of that component. On the other hand,
a VIF in a non-component class object is a direct member of a class object that itself is a
direct member of a UVM component. The hierarchy tree displays the VIFs only if the class
object is not derived from uvm_component and is one level below the UVM component.
Viewing a VIF in a Non-Component Class
To view a VIF in a non-component class object associated with a UVM component, add
the +VERDI_DHIER_COMP_MEMBER_VIF runtime option when you run your simulation:
./simv -verdi +VERDI_DHIER_COMP_MEMBER_VIF

Usage Example
Suppose you have a UVM component my_env that contains a non-component class object
my_agent. If my_agent owns a VIF, expand the my_env node in the OVM/UVM Hierarchy
Tree pane. You see the VIF listed under my_agent, which is a direct member of my_env.
Limitations
This feature has the following limitations:
* It supports only one-level inspection under non-component class objects. You cannot
view VIFs owned by class objects nested deeper than one level below a UVM
component.
* VIFs contained within array, struct, and union members are not supported.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Limitations of the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree Pane
* If there is no data in the FSDB file, you cannot open an empty OVM/UVM Hierarchy
Tree pane. The option is enabled only after the data is available in FSDB.
* Unlike the rest of the UVM windows, in the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree pane, a check
mark appears before the option in the menu to indicate whether the pane is opened or
not. If the check mark is unchecked, the pane is removed. Such a behavior does not
exist for the other UVM Aware Debug windows.

Specifying UVM Runtime Options
Verdi only adds the following runtime option in the interactive console if the UVM Debug
check box is enabled:
+UVM_VERDI_TRACE=UVM_AWARE

For simulation with UVM not provided by Verdi or VCS, you must specify the following
runtime options in the interactive mode even if the UVM Debug check box is enabled:
+UVM_CONFIG_TRACE, +UVM_PHASE_TRACE, +UVM_OBJECTION_TRACE,
+UVM_RESOURCE_DB_TRACE,
+UVM_LOG_RECORD

Verdi supports session save and restore for all UVM views. The following sections
describe this support is detail:
* Commands to Save/Restore Session for all UVM Views in Interactive Mode
* Save/Restore Session Support for the Register View in Post-Processing Mode

Commands to Save/Restore Session for all UVM Views in
Interactive Mode
Verdi provides the following two functionalities to save the current debugging session:
* Using File -> Save Session command. Select this command to view the Save Session
dialog box, as shown in the following figure:
Figure 26

Save Session Dialog Box

You can use the Save Session command to save the Verdi session with current
simulation state. You must enable the Save Simulation State check box to save the

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
current Verdi session. You can use the File -> Restore Session command to restore
the saved Verdi session.
* Using Simulation -> Save State command. Select this command to view the Save
State dialog box, as shown in the following figure:
Figure 27

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Save State Dialog Box

The Save State command allows you to save the current simulation state and dumped
FSDB file. It does not save the current Verdi session.
The Simulation -> Restore State command allows you to restore the current simulation
state and the FSDB file. All interactive debug windows, including the UVM Aware windows,
are refreshed to reflect the current simulation state.
During the debug process, if you want to restart debugging again from the saved
simulation state, you can restore the simulation state again. In this case, only the
simulation state and FSDB are restored. The current Verdi session (for example, which
signals are present in Wave window, and so on) is not restored.
The following sections describe what would be saved and restored in each UVM Aware
view:
* Register View Save/Restore Session
* Factory View Save/Restore Session
* Phase View Save/Restore Session
* Sequence View Save/Restore Session
* Resource View Save/Restore Session
* OVM/UVM Hierarchy View Save/Restore Session

Register View Save/Restore Session
In the Register View, the following items are restored as they were before the save
session:
* Register View pane layout (Register Hierarchy/Register Attribute/Register Access
History pane on or off)
* Register hierarchy data and selected items if exist
* Register attribute data and selected items if exist
* Register access history of the selected register data and selected items if exist
* Quick Filter on/off status, the values inside it and the status of check boxes
* If you have performed the radix display change on some signals before save session,
those are restored too.
Figure 28

Register View Save/Restore Session

* Verdi displays a warning message if it cannot find original radix change file during the
restore session.
Figure 29

In the Factory View, the following items are restored as they were before the save session:
* Factory View pane layout (Factory Override Instance Creation pane on/off)
* Factory data and selected items if exist
* Factory override instance creation data and selected items if exist
* Quick Filter on/off status, the values inside it and the status of check boxes
Figure 30

Factory View Save/Restore Session

* Phase hierarchy data and selected items if exist

The Resource View is a configuration interface which displays all available configurations/
resources in the design. It allows you to exchange information across different
components to configure topology, mode of operation, and runtime parameters.
This section describes the Resource View in the following topics:
* Viewing the Resource View
* Displaying Radix in the Resource View

Viewing the Resource View
To view the Resource View, click the UVM/OVM/VMM Debug Windows drop-down button
and select the Resource/Config View option from the drop-down menu as shown in the
following figure:
Figure 36

Viewing the Resource View

You can view the Resource View in the Resource View page of the UVM Debug pane.
It contains Resource View pane, Access History View pane, and Quick Filter pane, as
shown in the following figure. This view updates when the simulation stops.

Figure 37

The Resource View pane displays all available configurations in your design. This view
contains four columns, namely, Name, Scope, Value, and Type, as shown in Figure 37,
and displays names and values of function arguments defined in your design. The
following table describes the columns of the Resource View pane. You can select only one
item at a time.
Column

Name

Displays the name argument of the get function of uvm_config_db

Scope

Displays the scope argument of a function

Value

Displays the value or val argument of a function

Type

Displays the argument type

The recording for the following common configuration items is disabled by
default:
check_connection_relationship, recording_detail,
default_sequence

You must use the +UVM_INC_INTERNAL_RSRC runtime option to enable
recording for these configuration items.
The Access History pane displays the set/get history of the resource/configuration item
selected in the Resource View pane. This view contains five columns, namely, Action,
Scope, Value, Time, and Accessor, as shown in Figure 37. You can double-click an item
in the Access History pane to view the code from where the set/get function is called.
You can select only one item at a time. The following table describes the columns of the
Access History pane.
Column

Action

Displays the set/get history of the resource item selected in the
Resource View pane.

Scope

Displays the actions of the scope patterns that match the selected
scope. Double-click this item to view the source line of the set/get
call in the Source Code pane

Value

Displays the value or val argument of a function
