Delay Control
"Delay control" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

reg reset, r1;
/* process always */
/* delay control statement*/
begin: BLK
/* scope: named begin */
if(reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

In the example code above, for the delay control statement, applying npi_handle(npiDelay,
delay_ctrl_handle) returns expression "100". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt,
delay_ctrl_handle) returns the named begin scope "BLK".

For delay control associated with assignment, the statement is always NULL.

Refer to the npiDelayControl section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

Disable
"Disable" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

disable blk_n; /* disable */

Distribution, Dist Item
A distribution (npiDistribution) is a set of weighted value. The distribution set is a commaseparated list of integral expressions and ranges.
Each term in the list is named dist item (npiDistItem). Optionally, each dist item can have
a weight, which is specified using the ":=" (npiEqualDist) or ":/" (npiDivDist) operators.

class CLS_DIST;
rand int x, y, z;
constraint CX {
x dist { 100 := 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5 }; /* distribution with
three dist items, each dist item contains range value and weight with
npiEqualDist type */
}
constraint CY {
y dist { [100:102] :/ 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5 }; /* distribution with
three dist items, each dist item contains range value and weight. Range
[100:102] uses npiDivDist operator, the rest items use npiEqualDist
}
constraint CZ {
z dist { 100, 200, 300 }; /* distribution with three dist items. No
weight is specified so each dist item uses default weight ":=1" */
}

In the aforementioned example, "y dist { [100:102] :/ 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5}" is a distribution
expression (npiDistribution) with an integral expression "y" and three dist items. Each
dist item (npiDistItem) contains a range value and a weight.
For example, the first dist item "[100:102]:/ 1" is constructed by a range value "[100:102]"
and a weight "1" that is specified by a divided operator ":/" (npiDivDist).
The rest two dist items contain weight value that are specified by equal operators
"=/" (npiEqualDist).
When no weight is specified for dist item, default weight ":=1" is used and the property
npiDistType returns "-1".

1. The npiDistType property of a dist item (npiDistItem) returns npiEqualDist,
npiDivDist, or npiUndefined. npiEqualDist implies the weight is specified by equal
operator ":=1". npiDivDist implies the weight is specified by a divided operator ":/".
If no weight is specified, npiDistType is npiUndefined.
2. The npiWeight method of a dist item (npiDistItem) returns a weight expression. If no
weight is specified, npiWeight returns NULL.

Refer to the npiDistType section in the Language Model - List of All Return Types section

Do-while
"Do while" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

do
// do while statement
begin : fff
x = x - 1;
if (x > 5) begin
end
end
while (x > 0);
return x + 10;
end

In the example code above, for the do-while statement, applying npi_handle(npiCondition,
dowhile_handle) returns the expression "x > 0". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt,
dowhile_handle) returns the named scope "fff".

N/A

Foreach Stmt
"Foreach" belongs to the class "scope".

int prod [1:8] [1:3];
initial begin:INIT
foreach(prod[x,]) /* npiForeachStmt */
prod[x] = {0, 0, 0};
end

In example.v, for the foreach stmt, applying one-to-one method npiVariables obtains
npiArrayVar "top.prod", and applying one-to-many method npiLoopVars obtains
npiIntVar "x" whose scope is foreach stmt and npiOperation whose npiOpType is
npiNullOp.

* The variable obtained through the npiVariables relation from a foreach stmt represents
packed array, unpacked array, or string var being indexed.
* The npiLoopVars iteration returns the index variables of the foreach stmt in left-to-right
order.
If an index variable is skipped, its place is represented as a npiOperation for which the
npiOpType is npiNullOp.
* The scope of each loop control variable in a foreach stmt is the foreach stmt.

Refer to the npiForeachStmt section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

Event Control
The execution of a procedural statement that is synchronized with a value change on a net
or variable or the occurrence of a declared event is treated as an event control object in
NPI Language model.

reg clk, reset, r1;
always @(posedge clk or negedge reset) /* event control */
begin: BLK
if(!reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

In the example code above, the npiCondition transition for event control statement returns
an operation object (npiOperation) that represents "posedge clk or negedge reset", while
the npiStmt transition returns the named begin object (npiNamedBegin) named "BLK".

N/A

Refer to the npiEventControl section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

"Event statement" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

wire clk;
event ev;
always @(negedge clk)
-> ev; /* event statement */

TD
/*
TD
/*

t0 [1:0] = '{{0, 0}, {0, 0}};
Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiMultiAssignmentPatternOp */
t1 [1:0] = '{2{'{0, 0}}};
Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiConcatOp; TD'{0, 1}:
npiOperation with op-type npiAssignmentPatternExprOp */
TD t2 [1:0] = {TD'{0, 1}, TD'{default:0}};
mm m0(r[0]);
r[1:0] /* part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
r[2-:3] /* indexed part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
r[p-:4] /* indexed part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
if (r[0] == 0/* operation with npiOpType: npiEqOp */)
r[3] = 0;
end

In the example code above, part-select "top.r[1:0]" (size is equal to 2) gets constant "1"
and "0" by applying method npiLeftRange and npiRightRange, respectively, and gets bitvar "top.r" by applying method npiParent.
Similarly, indexed-part-select "top.r[2-:3]" (size is equal to 3) gets constant "2" and "3" by
applying method npiBaseExpr and npiWidthExpr, respectively, and gets bit-var "top.r" by
applying method npiParent.
Besides, the default expression of t0, t1 and t2 are operations with npiOpType:
npiAssignmentPatternOp, npiMultiAssignmentPatternOp and npiConcatOp respectively.
For t0's default expression, applying 1-to-many method npiOperand gets two npiConcatOp
operations.
For t1's default expression, applying 1-to-many method npiOperand get a npiConstant 2
and a npiAssignmentPatternOp operation. For t2's default expression, applying 1-to-many
method npiOperand gets two npiAssignmentPatternExprOp operations.
npiAssignmentPatternExprOp operation TD'{default:0} get a npiBitTypespec named "TD"
and a npiAssignmentPatternOp operation by applying 1-to-many method npiOperand.

* For an operator whose type is npiMultiConcatOp, the first operand is the multiplier
expression. The remaining operands are the expressions within the concatenation.
* The cast operation, for which npiOpType returns npiTypeCastOp, npiSigningCastOp,
npiSizeCastOp or npiConstCastOp, is represented as a unary operation, with its sole
argument being the expression being cast.
Only for cast operation of npiTypeCastOp, it can obtain the typespec of the cast
expression being the type to which the argument is being cast.

In the following example, the first RHS operation's npiOptype is npiTypeCastOp so it
can get the typespec by applying npiTypespec.
The second RHS operation's npiOptype is npiSigningCastOp, and its signed property
returns 1. The third RHS operation's npiOptype is npiSizeCastOp, and its size property
returns 8. The last RHS operation's npiOptype is npiConstCastOp.
int cast_int = int'(2.0 * 3.0);
integer cast_signed = signed'(2'b11);
byte cast_size = 8'(1234);
logic [31:0] cast_const = const'(cast_int);

* The operation with npiOpType: npiAssignmentPatternOp could get expr, typespec or
pattern item by applying 1-to-many method npiOperand. This is discussed in detail in
the section "pattern item".
* For a part-select or indexed part-select, the npiParent object is correspond to the
expression formed by removing the part-select range from the expression represented
by the part-select or indexed part-select itself.
For example, given the following declaration:
logic [0:3][7:0] r [1:4];

The parents of various part-selects or indexed part-selects is as shown in the following
table:
part-select or indexed part-select
expression

parent expression

r[4][3][1:0]

r[4][3]

r[i+1][3][j+:2]

r[i+1][3]

r[0][j-:4]

r[0]

r[0:2]

r

* npiSize for part select or indexed part select always returns the number of the flatten
bits. For example, a is declared as below, and npiSize of a[1:0] is 16.
reg [7:0] a [7:0];

* npiSize for constant whose npiConstType property is npiNullConst always returns -1
(npiUndefined).

* For an operation, npi_get_value() gets the value of calculation if:
its npiOpType is not npiAssignmentPatternOp, npiMultiAssignmentPatternOp,
npiAssignmentPatternExprOp or npiListOp.
all its operands can get the value by npi_get_value().
* For npiTypeCastOp and npiAssignmentPatternExprOp, if the cast type is type operator
(example as follows), the size and signed property should be -1.
int i1 = type(ia+ib)'{default:0}; // size and signed of this operation
should be -1

* For npiTypeCastOp and npiAssignmentPatternExprOp, if the cast type is type operator
(example as follow), the size and signed property should be -1. (unsupported now)
int i1 = type(ia+ib)'{default:0}; // size and signed of this operation should be -1

For
"For" belongs to the class "atomic statement" and "scope".

parameter int SIZE = 256;
integer index=0;
function myfunc;
for(index=0; index<SIZE; index=index+1) /* for statement */
begin: ggg
$display("aaa");
end
myfunc = 1;

In the example code above, for the for statement, applying npi_iterate(npiForInitStmt,
for_handle), the atomic statement "index=0" is returned from the iterator.
Applying npi_iterate(npiForIncStmt, for_handle), the atomic statement "index=index+2" is
returned from the iterator. Applying npi_handle(npiCondition, for_handle), the expression
"index < SIZE" is returned. Applying npi_handle(npiStmt, for_handle), the named begin
scope "ggg" is returned.

N/A

Forever
"Forever" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

forever CYCLE clk = ~clk;
end

In the example code above, for the forever statement, applying npi_handle(npiStmt,
forever_handle) returns the delay control "#CYCLE clk = ~clk"

N/A

text:
. A generate block is a collection of one or more module items.

"Generate scope" belongs to the class "scope".

parameter p = 4;
wire [7:0] a;
wire [7:0] aa;
if(p > 0)
begin: B
/* gen scope, top.B */
and u0 (a[0], a[1],b);
end
for (i=0; i<p; i=i+1)
begin: BB /* gen scope, top.BB[0] ~ top.BB[3] */
assign a[i] = ^a[p-1:i];
end
for (i=0; i<p; i=i+1)
begin /* unamed gen scope, top.gblk1[0] ~ top.gblk1[3] */
assign aa[i] = ^aa[p-1:i];

end

In the example code above, for the first generate description, the gen scope "top.B" is
generated. For the second generate description, four gen scopes, "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]",
"top.BB[2]", and "top.BB[3]" are generated.
For the third generate description, four unnamed gen scope, "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]", and "top.gblk1[3]" are generated. Refer SystemVerilog LRM Chapter 27.for
details of the unnamed gen scope.
The property npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.B" is "0" (FALSE). The property
npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]", "top.BB[2]" and "top.BB[3]" is
"1" (TRUE).
The property npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]" and "top.gblk1[3]" is "1" (TRUE).
The property npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.B" is "0" (FALSE). The property
npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]", "top.BB[2]" and "top.BB[3]" is
"0" (FALSE). The property npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]" and "top.gblk1[3]" is "1" (TRUE).

1. For an unnamed generate, an implicit scope is created. Its npiImplicitDecl property
returns TRUE.
2. References to gen vars within the gen scope is treated as local parameters.
3. Parameters within the gen scope must be local parameters.

If, If-else
"If" (npiIf) and "If-else" (npiIfElse) belong to the class "atomic statement".

reg a, b, x, y, z;
if( a & b ) /* if statement */
x = y;
if( a | b ) /* if-else statement */
x = ~y;
x = z;
end

In the example code above, for the if-else statement, applying npi_handle(npiCondition,
ifelse_handle) returns the expression "a|b". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt, ifelse_handle)
returns the atomic statement "x = ~y".
Applying npi_handle(npiElseStmt, ifelse_handle) returns the atomic statement "x = z".

npiPriorityQualifier.

In NPI Language model, instance is a class. It contains four types - module, interface,

An optional qualifier, automatic or static, is used to specify the default lifetime of all
variables declared in a task, function, or block defined within a module, interface, package,
or program. The default lifetime is static.

* The npiTypedef iteration returns the user-defined typespecs that have typedefs
explicitly declared in the instance.
* The npiInstance always returns the immediate instance (package, module, or interface)
in which the object is instantiated.
* Imported items are not accessible through npi_handle_by_name().
* The propertynpiContainProtect returns 1 if any protected code (embraced by protect
and endprotect) is written inside the definition (could be module/interface/package) of
the instance. Otherwise, it returns 0.
* The property npiBind returns 1 if the instance is created by "bind" statement.

* The property npiLibraryName returns the working library name for the instance. If the
design that declares this instance is not imported from working library, the return string
is NULL.
* The property npiDefLibraryName returns the working library name for the definition of
instance. If the design that declares this definition is not imported from working library,
the return string is NULL.
* For a package object, the property npiIsRoot is used to identify if a package object is
root or a general package. If the returned value is 1, the package object is root. Else,
the object is a general package.

Instance Arrays
The instantiations of modules/interfaces/primitives/programs can contain a range
specification. This allows an array of instances to be created.
In the NPI Language model, there are five kinds of instances array objects - module array,
interface array, gate array, switch array and UDP array.
The later three instance array objects belong to the class "primitive array".

module top; /* module */
mm u1 /* module */(w1, w2[0]);
mm u2[3:0] /* module array */ (w1, w2);
initial begin : INIT_BLK

end

In the example code above, "top.u2" is an object with type "module
array" (npiModuleArray).
Applying method "npiExpr" to the handle "top.u2", an operation handle (npiOperation) with
two operands w1, w2 is returned (operands w1 and w2 are the objects with type npiNet
and npiArrayNet, separately).
Applying method "npiRange" to the handle "top.u2", an iterator handle that contains
one range object (npiRange) is returned. Applying methods "npiLeftRange" and
"npiRightRange" to the range object, constant handles (npiConstant) "3" and "0" is
returned, separately.

* Traversing from the instance array to expr returns a simple expression object of type
npiOperation with a npiOpType of npiListOp. This expression is used to access the
actual list of connections to the instance array in the SystemVerilog source code.
* npiIterator(npiRange, instance_array_handle) returns the set of instance array ranges
beginning with the left-most range of the array declaration and iterating through the
right-most range. Using the npiLeftRange/npiRightRange properties returns the bounds
of the left-most dimension of a multidimensional array.
* The property npiContainBlackBox identifies if an interface array or a module array
contains at least one black box that is set by ZeBu synthesis command.

In the example code above, "input [7:0] data", "output [7:0] result", and "ref int cnt" are
objects with type "IO declaration" (npiIODecl).
Applying method "npiExpr" to the first IO declaration of task "convert" (npiTask) returns a
reg var (npiReg) named "data".
Applying method "npiExpr" to the second IO declaration of task "convert" (npiTask) returns
a reg var (npiReg) named "result".
Applying method "npiExpr" to IO declaration of task "counter" (npiTask) returns a ref obj
named "cnt".

* npiDirection returns npiRef for pass by ref ports or arguments.
* A ref obj type handle might be returned for the npiExpr of an io decl if it is passed by
reference or if the io decl is an interface or a modport.
* If the npiExpr of an io decl is a ref objand if the npiActual of the ref obj is an interface or
modport declaration, then the npiDirection of the io decl is undefined.
* For npiDirection, available value includes npiInput, npiOutput, npiInout, and npiRef.
* If the io decl is an importing or exporting of tasks and functions from modport, its
npiExpr is a npiNIY object (NPI doesn't support it currently).
* Similar to item 5, if the io decl is a clocking block from modport, its npiExpr is a npiNIY
object (NPI doesn't support it currently).

Modport
To restrict interface access within a module, there are modport lists with directions
declared within the interface. The keyword "modport" indicates that the directions are
declared as if inside the module.
The modport port objects mean the port of modport. It provides direction information and
name indicates for module ports.

interface I;
logic [7:0] r;
int x=1;
bit R;
modport A (output .P({r[3:1],r[0]}), input x, .S(R)); /* modport */
modport B (input .P(r[3:0]), output x); /* modport */

module M2 ( interface i, output reg clk, input [31:0] varInt);
always@(*) begin
clk = i.P[2];
i.x = varInt ;
end
module M1 ( interface i);
always@(*) begin
i.P = i.x;
end
reg CLK2;
wire [31:0] input2;
I i1 ();
M1 u1 (i1.A);
M2 u2 (i1.B, CLK2, input2);
assign input2[2] = CLK2;

In example.v above, "P", "S" and "x" of modport "A" in interface "top.i1" are the objects with
type npiMpPort;
Applying method npiActual to the npiRefObj "top.u1.i.P", a modport port object (npiMpPort)
named "top.i1.A.P" is returned.
Applying method "npiActual" to the npiRefObj "i.P[2]" of "top.u1", a modport port bit object
(npiMpPortBit) that represents "top.i1.A.P[2]" is returned.
Applying method "npiExpr" to the modport port handle "P" of modport "A", an operation

An identifier declared as an event data type is called a "named event".

event ev; // named event
event evAry1 [3:0]; // named event array
event evAry2 [1:0][2:0]; // named event array
task automatic tsk_auto(input time ii,
output time oo,
inout time io);
event auto_ev;
event auto_ev_arr [1:0];
oo = ii-io;
initial begin:init_blk
@(ev) $display("eventControl");
@(evAry1[1]) $display("eventControl");
@(evAry2[0][1]) $display("eventControl");
end

In the example code above, "ev", "evAry1[1]", and "evAry2[0][1]" are named events. The
property npiArrayMember is TRUE for "evAry1[1]" and "evAry2[0][0]", but FALSE for "ev".

"evAry1" and "evAry2" are named event arrays.
Applying npi_iterate(npiRange, evAry2_handle) and the iterator gives the range "[1:0]"
and then "[2:0]". Applying npi_iterate(npiRange, ev_handle) and the iterator gives NULL
(empty) object. Applying npi_iterate(npiIndex, evAry2[0][1]_handle) and the iterator gives
the expression "0" and then "1". Applying npi_iterate(npiIndex, ev_handle) and the iterator
gives the NULL (empty) object.

1. npi_iterate(npiRange, named_event_array_handle) returns the set of array range
declarations beginning with the left-most unpacked range and iterating through the
right-most unpacked range.
2. npi_iterate(npiIndex, named_event_handle) returns the set of indices for a named
event within an array, starting with the index for the named event and working outward.
If the named event is not part of an array, a NULL (empty) is returned.

assign w1[0] = w2[0][0][0];
assign w2[3] = {64{w2[2][0]}};
assign w3[7] = w2[0][0][0];

Nets
In NPI Language model, there are two main groups of data objects: variables and nets.
A net is written by one or more continuous assignments, by primitive outputs, or through
module ports. The resultant value of multiple drivers is determined by the resolution
function of the net type.
A net cannot be procedurally assigned. If a net on one side of a port is driven by a variable
on the other side, a continuous assignment is implied.
"Nets" belongs to the class "simple expr".

wire w1 [3:0];
wire [7:0] w2 [3:0][63:0];
wire [7:0] w3;
assign w1[0] = w2[0][0][0];
assign w2[3] = {64{w2[2][0]}};
assign w3[7] = w2[0][0][0];

In the example code above, w1 and w2 are "array net" (npiArrayNet), w2[3] is "net
select" (npiNetSelect), w1[0], w2[2][0] and w3 are "net" (npiNet), w3[7] and w2[0][0][0] are
"net bit" (npiNetBit).
The npiParent of w1, w2, w3 are NULL (empty). The npiParent of w1[0] is w1, the
npiParent of w3[0] is w3, the npiParent of w2[2] and w2[2][0] are w2. The npiParent of
w2[0][0][0] is w2[0][0].
The npiIndex of w1, w2, w3 are "NULL", the npiIndex of w1[0], w3[0] are expression "0",
the npiIndex of w2[2] is expression "2" , the npiIndex of w2[2][0] are expression "2" and
then "0", the npiIndex of w2[0][0][0] is expression "0" (reach largest packed array).

* Any net declared as an array with one or more unpacked ranges is an array net. Any
packed struct net or enum net declared with one or more explicit packed ranges is a
packed array net.
* The npiArrayMember property is TRUE for a net that is an element of an array net. It is
FALSE otherwise.
The npiPackedArrayMember property is TRUE for a packed struct net, an enum net, or
a packed array net that is an element of a packed array net.
* For implicit nets, npiLineNo returns 0, and npiFile returns the file name where the
implicit net is first referenced.
* npi_handle(npiIndex, net_bit_handle) returns the bit index for the net bit.
npi_iterate(npiIndex, net_bit_handle) returns the set of indices for a multidimensional
net array bit-select, starting with the index for the net bit and working outward.
* npiSize for an array net returns the number of nets in the array. For unpacked
structures, the size returned indicates the number of members in the structure.
For an enum net, integer net, net, time net, packed struct net, or packed array net,
npiSize returns the size of the net in bits. For a net bit, npiSize returns 1.

* npi_iterate(npiIndex, net_handle) returns the set of indices for a net within an array net,
starting with the index for the net and working outward. If the net is not part of an array
(the npiArrayMember property is FALSE), NULL is returned.
The npiIndex iterator works similarly for packed array net elements (packed struct nets,
enum nets, or packed array nets whose npiPackedArrayMember property is TRUE).
The indices returned starts with the index of the element and work outward until the
npiParent packed array net is reached.
The indices retrieved for packed array net elements are the same as those shown in
the example for detail (8) for each of the sub elements returned by npiElement. The
indices are retrieved in right-to-left order as they appear in the text.
* Neither an array net nor an unpacked struct net has a value property.
* The npiParent transition is allowed on all net objects. It returns one of the types of
objects listed in the following, representing one of its prefix objects (field select prefix or
indexing select prefix as described in SystemVerilog LRM 11.5.3), or NULL, depending
on whether certain criteria are met.
For purposes of defining npiParent, a prefix object is the object obtained from
successively removing the right-most index or identifier from a compound or indexed/
multidimensional object name. Consider the following npiArrayNet objects:
wire logic [1:0][2:3] mda [4:6][6:8];
wire struct { int i1; logic[1:0][2:3]bvec[4:5]; } spa [9:11][12:13];

mda[6][8][1][3] is a npiNet, mda[6][8][1] is its first prefix object (a 2-bit npiNet vector),
and mda[6][8] is its second prefix object (a 2 x 2 packed array npiNet), and so on.
The spa[9][12].bvec[4] object is a npiNet (a 2 x 2 packed array npiNet), and spa[9]
[12].bvec is its first prefix object (a npiArrayNet struct member), and spa[9][12] is the
second prefix object (the npiStructNet containing the bvec member) and so on.
For a net object with prefix objects, the npiParent transition returns one of the following
prefix objects, whichever comes first in prefix order (right-most to left-most):
Struct or union net.
Struct or union member net.
The largest containing packed array net object.
The largest containing unpacked array net object.
If there is no prefix object, or no prefix object meets at least one of the aforementioned
criteria, npiParent returns NULL.
Using the declarations above, the npiParent of mda[6][8][1][3] is mda[6][8], the npiNet
representing the largest containing packed array prefix.

The npiParent of mda[6][8] is mda, the npiArrayNet representing the largest containing
unpacked array net prefix. Likewise, the npiParent of spa[9][12].bvec[4][0] is spa[9]
[12].bvec[4] (the largest containing packed array net); the npiParent of spa[9]
[12].bvec[4] is spa[9][12].bvec (struct member), and applying npiParent again yields
spa[9][12], the struct net for member bvec.
The npiParent of spa[9][12] is spa, the largest containing unpacked array of the struct
net. npiParent of spa (or mda) would return NULL.
* The npiStructUnionMember property is TRUE for any enum net, integer net, time net,
struct net, packed array net, or array net that is a direct member of a struct net that is,
whose npiParent is a struct net.
This property is FALSE for any net, array net, or net bit whose npiParent is not a struct
net.

npiTriAnd, npiTriOr, npiSupply1, npiSupply0, npiNone, npiUwire, or npiWreal.

In the NPI Language model, a range object denotes the range specification in

wire [0:7] w3; /*object range*/

In the example code above, "[0:7]" is a range object that is obtained from the object with

Applying method "npiLeftRange" and "npiRightRange" to the range object, constant

Parameter, param assign, and def param
The NPI Language model provides two elaboration-time constants: "parameter" and
"localparam". Each parameter might be assigned a default value when declared.
The value of a parameter of an instantiated module or interface is overridden in each
instance using "param assign". The "type parameter" can specify a data type, allowing
modules or interfaces to have ports and data objects whose type is set for each instance.
Using "defparam", parameter values can be changed in any module, interface, or program
instance throughout the design using the hierarchical name of the parameter.

module sub_mod(clk);
parameter signed NUM = 4'b1; /* parameter */
parameter int RANGE = 1024;
localparam int BOB = 3; /* local parameter */
parameter int param2 = RANGE + 256;
typedef logic signed [5:0] LOGIC;
parameter type TYPE = LOGIC; /* type parameter */
sub_mod (.RANGE(512)/* param assign */) subMod(.clk(clk));

In the example code above, the typespec of parameter NUM and RANGE are NULL
and npiIntTypespec respectively. The method npiExpr is used to get the default value
expression without elaboration.
Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, parameter_handle) to the object "top.subMod.param2"
returns the parameter value at the end of the elaboration, for example. the expression
"RANGE + 256".
Applying npi_get_value() to the parameter handle returns the parameter value at the end
of the elaboration, for example, the value of "top.subMod.param2" is 768. "#(.Range(512))"
refers to the "param assign" whose right-hand-side expression is "512" and left side
expression is the handle of "top.subMod.Range".
module sub_mod(clk);
logic [4:0][3:0] aaaa;
parameter [4:0][3:0] bbbb = 21'bz_11xx_xzzz_0001_11xx_01xz;
assign aaaa[4][1] = bbbb[4][1]; /* parameter bit */
assign aaaa[4] = bbbb[4]; /* parameter */
assign aaaa[0][3:2] = bbbb[0][3:2]; /* part-select */
integer cccc;
parameter dddd = 55;
assign cccc[32] = dddd[32]; /* bit-select */
logic[3:0] eeee;
parameter ffff = 4'bzx01;
assign eeee[3] = ffff[3]; /* parameter bit */

npi_get_value() only supports npiParameterBit and npiParameter, for example,"bbbb[4]
[1]", "bbbb[4]" and "ffff[3]", and npiParameter and npiParameterBit have the same
behavior.

The method npiExpr only supports declaration parameters, any sub parameter, for
example, "bbbb[4]", gets NULL handle. The typespec of npiParameterBit is NULL, if its
parent parameter has no typespec for example, "ffff[3]" has no typespec.
example2.v
module sub_mod(clk);
logic [4:0][3:0] aaaa;
parameter [4:0][3:0] bbbb = 21'bz_11xx_xzzz_0001_11xx_01xz;
assign aaaa[4][1] = bbbb[4][1]; /* parameter bit */
assign aaaa[4] = bbbb[4]; /* parameter */
assign aaaa[0][3:2] = bbbb[0][3:2]; /* part-select */
integer cccc;
parameter dddd = 55;
assign cccc[32] = dddd[32]; /* bit-select */
logic[3:0] eeee;
parameter ffff = 4'bzx01;
assign eeee[3] = ffff[3]; /* parameter bit */

npi_get_value() only supports npiParameterBit and npiParameter, such as, "bbbb[4][1]",
"bbbb[4]", and "ffff[3]", and npiParameter and npiParameterBit have the same behavior.
The method npiExpr only supports declaration parameters, any sub parameter, such as,
"bbbb[4]" gets NULL handle.
The typespec of npiParameterBit is NULL if its parent parameter has no typespec, such
as, "ffff[3]" has no typespec.
example3.v
parameter mp = 0;
defparam m0.mp = 2; /* def param */
mm (1) m0();
genvar i, j;
for (i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1) begin : gb
defparam gb[i].mg.mp = i+1; /* def param */
mm (i) mg();
end

Module instance "top" obtains one "def param" handle by applying one-to-many method
npiDefParam. Similarly, gen-scopes, "top.gb[0]", "top.gb[1]" and "top.gb[2]" obtain one "def

* For a value parameter, npi_get_value() returns the value that the parameter has at the
end of elaboration.
* The npiTypespec of a type parameter returns the typespec that the type parameter has
at the end of elaboration, but without resolving typedef aliases.
* The npiExpr relation of a value parameter returns the default expr, while the npiExpr
relation of a type parameter returns the default typespec.
* npiLhs from a param assign object returns a handle to the overridden value parameter
or type parameter.

Otherwise, the npiTypedefAlias should return NULL. For example:

* If type of parameter is string, its npiConstType should return npiStringConst. If it is

Pattern Item
Pattern item is a group that contains member pattern, position pattern, type pattern and
default pattern. It is used to combine an assignment pattern operation. Member pattern is
used to express the assignment pattern for structure.
Position pattern is used to express the assignment pattern for array. Type and default
pattern are used to express the assignment pattern for structure or array.

typedef bit [1:0] TD;
typedef TD NTD;
byte b;
bit c;
NTD d;
} pst;
/* [ Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiAssignmentPatternOp */
parameter [1:0] p = '{0/* npiConstant */, 0/* npiConstant */};
parameter pst ps = '{a:1/* npiMemberPattern */,
default:0/* npiDefaultPattern */};
/* ] */
mm (/* the types of two operands are npiPositionPattern */
.p('{0:1, 1:1}),
/* the types of two operands are npiTypePattern */
.ps('{bit:0, NTD:1})) m0();

In the example code above, there are two assignment patterns used in module "mm".
The first one is applied to p, the right-hand-side (rhs) operation whose op-type is
npiAssignmentPattern iterates two constants by using 1-to-many method npiOperand.

The second one is applied to ps, the rhs operation whose op-type is npiAssignmentPattern
iterates one member pattern and one default pattern by using 1-to-many method
npiOperand.
Besides, the member pattern handle can get a constant 1 by using one-to-one method
npiExpr and get a struct-member "a" (npiTypespecMember) by using one-to-one method
npiIndex.
Similarly, the other default-pattern handle gets a constant 0 by using one-to-one method
npiExpr, but nothing by using one-to-one method npiIndex.
For the parameter-assign for "p" of the module instance "m0" under "top", its rhs expr is an
operation of npiAssignmentPattern, and this operation iterates two position patterns ("0:1"
and "1:1") by using 1-to-many method npiOperand.
Applying npiIndex to position pattern "0:1" gets a npiConstant 0, and applying npiExpr to
position pattern "0:1" gets a npiConstant 1.
Similarly, the rhs expr of the parameter-assign for "ps" is also an operation of
npiAssignmentPattern, and this operation iterates two type patterns ("bit:0" and "NTD:1")
by using 1-to-many method npiOperand.
Applying npiIndex to position pattern "bit:0" gets a npiBitTypespec, and applying npiExpr to
position pattern "bit:0" gets a npiConstant 0.

* Pattern item consists of index, colon and value-expression in order. The index handle
could be a npiTypespecMember (member of struct), npiExpr or npiTypespec handle,
and it is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiIndex.
Value-expression handle is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiExpr.
* Applying npiIndex to default pattern always returns NULL.

Primitive
The class "primitive" consists of the following objects of types:
* "gate": and, nand, nor, or, xor, xnor, buf, not, bufif0, bufif1, notif0, notif1
* "switch": nmos, pmos, cmos, rnmos, rpmos, rcmos, rtran, rtranif0, rtranif1, tran, tranif0,
tranif1, pullup, pulldown
* "udp"

reg r1, r2;
reg [1:0] r3;
wire wq, wa;
wire pi, pi2;
wire ndata, data, clock;
// gate
not 5 ngate1(ndata, data);
nand (3, 4) nand1(wa, data, clock);
nand 2 nand2[1:0] (r3, pi, pi2);
// switch
pmos pm1(wq, wa, clock);
nmos nm1(wq, wa, clock);
cmos cmArr[1:0] (wq, wa, clock, ~clock);
// udp
latch latch1(wq, r1, r2);
latch latchArr[1:0] (wq, r1, r2);

In the example code above, "ngate1", "nand1", "nand2[1]", and "nand2[0]" are the objects
of type npiGate. "pm1", "nm1", "cmArr[1]", and "cmArr[0]" are the objects of type npiSwitch.
"latch1", "latchArr[1]", and "latchArr[0]" are objects of type npiUdp. "nand2" is the object of
type npiGateArray. "cmArr" is the object of type npiSwitchArray. "latchArr" is the object of
type npiUdpArray.
The object of type "prim term" (npiPrimTerm) means the primitive terminal. For example,
for the gate "nand1", there are three terminals that connect to the expression "wa", "data",
and "clock".
Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, prim_term_0_handle) to the terminal 0 of gate "nand1" gets
the expression "wa". Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, prim_term_1_handle) to the terminal 1
of gate "nand1" gets the expression "data".

Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, prim_term_2_handle) to the terminal 2 of gate "nand1" gets
the expression "clock".
Applying npi_handle(npiDelay, primitive_handle) to the gate "ngate1" gets the expression
"5". Applying npi_handle(npiDelay, primitive_handle) to the gate "nand1" gets the
operation expression "3, 4", whose npiOpType is npiListOp.

* npiSize returns the number of inputs.
* npiTermIndex is used to determine the terminal order. The first terminal has a term
index of zero.
* If a primitive is an element within a primitive array, the npiIndex transition is used to
access the index within the array.
If a primitive is not part of a primitive array, this transition returns NULL (empty).
* npiPrimType is one of the following:
npiGate: npiAndPrim, npiNandPrim, npiNorPrim, npiOrPrim, npiXorPrim,

npiSwitch: npiNmosPrim, npiPmosPrim, npiCmosPrim, npiRnmosPrim,
npiRpmosPrim, npiRcmosPrim, npiRtranPrim, npiRtranif0Prim, npiRtranif1Prim,

Program
In NPI Language model, there are four kinds of instances - interface, package, program
and module. "Program" signifies an instance whose type is program and belongs to
"instance" and "scope" class.

program prg(interface pitf , input addr, inout data);
parameter prgp = 0;
assign data = ~addr;
endprogram
parameter itfp = 0;
logic clk;
always itfp clk = ~clk;
initial clk = 1;
wire addr = 0;
wire data = 0;
itf (5) it();

Property
A property defines a behavior of the design. A named property is used for verification as
an assumption, an obligation, or a coverage specification.
In NPI Language model, a named property declaration (property decl) might be declared
with formal arguments (prop formal decl) and defined by a property specification
(property spec).
A property specification might be composed by its clocking event, property expression
(property expr), and disable condition.
A property expression is a class that contains general operation, sequence expression
(sequence expr), and property instance (property inst).

example.sv
module example ( input clk,
input bit x,
input bit y
);
sequence seq (a, b);
@(posedge clk) a 1 b;
endsequence
property prop1 (a, b); /* property decl with two prop formal decls */
seq(a, b);
/* property spec */
endproperty : prop1
property prop2;
/* property decl */
@(posedge clk)
/* clocking event of property spec */
disable iff (x==y) /* disable condition of property spec */

x |=> y;
endproperty : prop2

/* property expr of property spec */

ASSERT1: assert property ( prop1(x, y) ); /* property inst with two
arguments x and y */

In the aforementioned example, "example.prop1" and "example.prop2" are property
declarations with object type "npiPropertyDecl".
There are two property formal declarations, "a" and "b", that are belonged to
"example.prop1" and the object type is npiPropFormalDecl.
The property is defined by a behavior of a design, the behavior means a property
spec (npiPropertySpec). For example, and the property spec of "example.prop2" is
"@(posedge clk) disable iff (x==y) x |=> y;".
In this property spec, the corresponding clocking event is "@(posedge clk) " that could be
obtained by applying 1-1 method npiClockingEvent.
The corresponding disable condition is "(x==y)" that could be obtained by applying 1-1
method npiDisableCondition.
The rest part "x |=> y" is the property expression. If the clocking event and disable
condition do not exist, the returned object of npiClockingEvent and npiDisableCondition
is NULL.
The prop1 is instantiated in "ASSERT1". By applying npiPropertyDecl relation, the
corresponding property declaration object "example.prop1" would be retrieved.

* For a property instance object, applying 1-1 method npiPropertyDecl returns the
corresponding property declaration.
* For a property declaration object, the npiPropFormalDecl iterator returns the property
declaration arguments.
The npiVariables iterator returns all variables under the scope of a property
declaration.
The 1-1 method npiPropertySpec returns the property specification defined in the
property declaration.
* For a property formal declaration, the npiTypespec relation returns the object directed
to the typespec of the formal.
If the formal is untyped, the returned typespec is NULL. If the formal has an
initialization expression, the expression can be obtained using the npiExpr relation.

The npiDirection returns npiNoDirection if the formal argument is not a local variable.
Otherwises, npiDirection returns npiInput.
* For a property specification, the npiClockingEvent relation returns the clocking scene
to evaluate the property. Applying method npiDisableCondition returns an expression
that described the disable condition.
The npiPropertyExpr relation returns the property expression that is used to evaluate
if the property is hold or failed.

Nets
In NPI Language model, there are two main groups of data objects: variables and nets.
A net is written by one or more continuous assignments, by primitive outputs, or through
module ports. The resultant value of multiple drivers is determined by the resolution
function of the net type.
A net cannot be procedurally assigned. If a net on one side of a port is driven by a variable
on the other side, a continuous assignment is implied.
"Nets" belongs to the class "simple expr".

prefix objects, whichever comes first in prefix order (right-most to left-most):
Struct or union net.
Struct or union member net.
The largest containing packed array net object.
The largest containing unpacked array net object.

criteria, npiParent returns NULL.

Parameter, param assign, and def param
The NPI Language model provides two elaboration-time constants: "parameter" and
"localparam". Each parameter might be assigned a default value when declared.
The value of a parameter of an instantiated module or interface is overridden in each
instance using "param assign". The "type parameter" can specify a data type, allowing
modules or interfaces to have ports and data objects whose type is set for each instance.
Using "defparam", parameter values can be changed in any module, interface, or program
instance throughout the design using the hierarchical name of the parameter.

module sub_mod(clk);
parameter signed NUM = 4'b1; /* parameter */
parameter int RANGE = 1024;
localparam int BOB = 3; /* local parameter */
parameter int param2 = RANGE + 256;
typedef logic signed [5:0] LOGIC;
parameter type TYPE = LOGIC; /* type parameter */
sub_mod (.RANGE(512)/* param assign */) subMod(.clk(clk));

In the example code above, the typespec of parameter NUM and RANGE are NULL
and npiIntTypespec respectively. The method npiExpr is used to get the default value
expression without elaboration.
Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, parameter_handle) to the object "top.subMod.param2"
returns the parameter value at the end of the elaboration, for example. the expression
"RANGE + 256".
Applying npi_get_value() to the parameter handle returns the parameter value at the end
of the elaboration, for example, the value of "top.subMod.param2" is 768. "#(.Range(512))"
refers to the "param assign" whose right-hand-side expression is "512" and left side
expression is the handle of "top.subMod.Range".
module sub_mod(clk);
logic [4:0][3:0] aaaa;
parameter [4:0][3:0] bbbb = 21'bz_11xx_xzzz_0001_11xx_01xz;
assign aaaa[4][1] = bbbb[4][1]; /* parameter bit */
assign aaaa[4] = bbbb[4]; /* parameter */
assign aaaa[0][3:2] = bbbb[0][3:2]; /* part-select */
integer cccc;
parameter dddd = 55;
assign cccc[32] = dddd[32]; /* bit-select */
logic[3:0] eeee;
parameter ffff = 4'bzx01;

npi_get_value() only supports npiParameterBit and npiParameter, such as, "bbbb[4][1]",
"bbbb[4]", and "ffff[3]", and npiParameter and npiParameterBit have the same behavior.
The method npiExpr only supports declaration parameters, any sub parameter, such as,
"bbbb[4]" gets NULL handle.
The typespec of npiParameterBit is NULL if its parent parameter has no typespec, such
as, "ffff[3]" has no typespec.
example3.v
parameter mp = 0;
defparam m0.mp = 2; /* def param */
mm (1) m0();
genvar i, j;
for (i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1) begin : gb
defparam gb[i].mg.mp = i+1; /* def param */
mm (i) mg();
end

Module instance "top" obtains one "def param" handle by applying one-to-many method
npiDefParam. Similarly, gen-scopes, "top.gb[0]", "top.gb[1]" and "top.gb[2]" obtain one "def
param" handle respectively.

* For a value parameter, npi_get_value() returns the value that the parameter has at the
end of elaboration.
* The npiTypespec of a type parameter returns the typespec that the type parameter has
at the end of elaboration, but without resolving typedef aliases.
* The npiExpr relation of a value parameter returns the default expr, while the npiExpr
relation of a type parameter returns the default typespec.
* npiLhs from a param assign object returns a handle to the overridden value parameter
or type parameter.
* If the type parameter assigned a type with a typedef, then the npiTypedefAlias of the
typespec returns a non-null handle, which represents the handle to the aliased typedef.
Otherwise, the npiTypedefAlias should return NULL. For example:
module sub_mod;
typedef logic signed [5:0] LOGIC;
parameter type TYPE = LOGIC;
parameter type TYPE2 = logic signed [5:0];

For the type parameter "TYPE", its npiTypedefAlias returns a handle of the typespec
"LOGIC" of npiType npiLogicTypespec.
For the type parameter "TYPE2", its npiTypedefAlias returns NULL.
* Array and unpacked struct/union parameters are unsupported now, and they become
npiNIY object.
* If implicit type of parameter is assigned by $, its npiConstType should return
npiUnboundedConst, and other properties, such as npiSize, npiSigned and
npi_get_value() , returns invalid value.
* If integer type of parameter is assigned by $, its npiConstType should return
npiDecConst, and its npiSize and npiSigned should be the same as integer.
For the npi_get_value(), the maximum positive integer value (for example, 0x7fffffff)
* If type of parameter is string, its npiConstType should return npiStringConst. If it is
real, shortreal, or realtime, it should return npiRealConst.

Otherwise, it should return npiDecConst.
* When the value of parameter is overridden by Verdi command option like -G, its
property npiSetValueByOption returns 1. Otherwise it returns 0.

Pattern Item
Pattern item is a group that contains member pattern, position pattern, type pattern and
default pattern. It is used to combine an assignment pattern operation. Member pattern is
used to express the assignment pattern for structure.
Position pattern is used to express the assignment pattern for array. Type and default
pattern are used to express the assignment pattern for structure or array.

typedef bit [1:0] TD;
typedef TD NTD;
byte b;
bit c;
NTD d;
} pst;
/* [ Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiAssignmentPatternOp */
parameter [1:0] p = '{0/* npiConstant */, 0/* npiConstant */};
parameter pst ps = '{a:1/* npiMemberPattern */,
default:0/* npiDefaultPattern */};
/* ] */
mm (/* the types of two operands are npiPositionPattern */
.p('{0:1, 1:1}),
/* the types of two operands are npiTypePattern */
.ps('{bit:0, NTD:1})) m0();

In the example code above, there are two assignment patterns used in module "mm".
The first one is applied to p, the right-hand-side (rhs) operation whose op-type is
npiAssignmentPattern iterates two constants by using 1-to-many method npiOperand.

The second one is applied to ps, the rhs operation whose op-type is npiAssignmentPattern
iterates one member pattern and one default pattern by using 1-to-many method
npiOperand.
Besides, the member pattern handle can get a constant 1 by using one-to-one method
npiExpr and get a struct-member "a" (npiTypespecMember) by using one-to-one method
npiIndex.
Similarly, the other default-pattern handle gets a constant 0 by using one-to-one method
npiExpr, but nothing by using one-to-one method npiIndex.
For the parameter-assign for "p" of the module instance "m0" under "top", its rhs expr is an
operation of npiAssignmentPattern, and this operation iterates two position patterns ("0:1"
and "1:1") by using 1-to-many method npiOperand.
Applying npiIndex to position pattern "0:1" gets a npiConstant 0, and applying npiExpr to
position pattern "0:1" gets a npiConstant 1.
Similarly, the rhs expr of the parameter-assign for "ps" is also an operation of
npiAssignmentPattern, and this operation iterates two type patterns ("bit:0" and "NTD:1")
by using 1-to-many method npiOperand.
Applying npiIndex to position pattern "bit:0" gets a npiBitTypespec, and applying npiExpr to
position pattern "bit:0" gets a npiConstant 0.

* Pattern item consists of index, colon and value-expression in order. The index handle
could be a npiTypespecMember (member of struct), npiExpr or npiTypespec handle,
and it is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiIndex.
Value-expression handle is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiExpr.
* Applying npiIndex to default pattern always returns NULL.

cmos cmArr[1:0] (wq, wa, clock, ~clock);
// udp
latch latch1(wq, r1, r2);
latch latchArr[1:0] (wq, r1, r2);

In the example code above, "ngate1", "nand1", "nand2[1]", and "nand2[0]" are the objects
of type npiGate. "pm1", "nm1", "cmArr[1]", and "cmArr[0]" are the objects of type npiSwitch.
"latch1", "latchArr[1]", and "latchArr[0]" are objects of type npiUdp. "nand2" is the object of
type npiGateArray. "cmArr" is the object of type npiSwitchArray. "latchArr" is the object of
type npiUdpArray.
The object of type "prim term" (npiPrimTerm) means the primitive terminal. For example,
for the gate "nand1", there are three terminals that connect to the expression "wa", "data",
and "clock".
Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, prim_term_0_handle) to the terminal 0 of gate "nand1" gets
the expression "wa". Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, prim_term_1_handle) to the terminal 1
of gate "nand1" gets the expression "data".

Applying npi_handle(npiExpr, prim_term_2_handle) to the terminal 2 of gate "nand1" gets
the expression "clock".
Applying npi_handle(npiDelay, primitive_handle) to the gate "ngate1" gets the expression
"5". Applying npi_handle(npiDelay, primitive_handle) to the gate "nand1" gets the
operation expression "3, 4", whose npiOpType is npiListOp.

* npiSize returns the number of inputs.
* npiTermIndex is used to determine the terminal order. The first terminal has a term
index of zero.
* If a primitive is an element within a primitive array, the npiIndex transition is used to
access the index within the array.
If a primitive is not part of a primitive array, this transition returns NULL (empty).
* npiPrimType is one of the following:
npiGate: npiAndPrim, npiNandPrim, npiNorPrim, npiOrPrim, npiXorPrim,
npiXnorPrim, npiBufPrim, npiNotPrim, npiBufif0Prim, npiBufif1Prim, npiNotif0Prim,
npiNotif1Prim.

npiRpmosPrim, npiRcmosPrim, npiRtranPrim, npiRtranif0Prim, npiRtranif1Prim,
npiTranPrim, npiTranif0Prim, npiTranif1Prim, npiPullupPrim, npiPulldownPrim.
npiUdp: npiSeqPrim, npiCombPrim.

Process
In the NPI Language model, there are two kinds of processes: initial and always. Objects
with type npiInitial denote the initial processes, while objects with type npiAlways denote
the always processes.

parameter delay = 10;
initial /*process initial*/
begin: BLK_INIT
end
always /*process always*/
delay clk = ~clk;

In the example code above, "top" has two process objects with types npiInitial and
npiAlways, respectively.
Applying method "npiStmt" to the initial process, named begin object (npiNamedBegin)
named "BLK" is returned.
Applying method "npiStmt" to the always process, delay control object (npiDelayControl)
that represents "#delay" is returned.

npiAlwaysType is one of npiAlways, npiAlwaysComb, npiAlwaysFF, or npiAlwaysLatch.

Program
In NPI Language model, there are four kinds of instances - interface, package, program
and module. "Program" signifies an instance whose type is program and belongs to
"instance" and "scope" class.

program prg(interface pitf , input addr, inout data);
parameter prgp = 0;
assign data = ~addr;
endprogram
parameter itfp = 0;
logic clk;
always itfp clk = ~clk;
initial clk = 1;
wire addr = 0;
wire data = 0;
itf (5) it();
prg (it.itfp) pg(it, addr, data); /* program */
prg pgArr [1:0] (it, addr, data); /* program array */

In the preceding example, top.pg, top.pgArr[1] and top.pgArr[0] are all objects
with type "program" (npiProgram).
The object type of top.pgArr is a program array, where top.pgArr[1] and
top.pgArr[0] are its elements.
* On applying npiInternalScope method to the handle top
The program (npiProgram) type handle top.pg, top.pgArr[1], top.pgArr[0] are
Interface (npiInterface) type handle top.itf is returned.
The "program" and "interface" type also belong to "scope" class. The program array
elements such as top.pgArr[1] can be obtained by npiInternalScope method because
they are also a program type object.
* On the other hand, on applying npiScope method to the handle top.pg,
top.pgArr[1], top.pgArr[0], and top.itf, the module type handle top is
returned. That is, npiScope is used to get the parent scope of a handle.
* On applying npiIndex method to the top.pgArr[1] module type handle, a handle that
refers to expression class "1" is returned.

Property
A property defines a behavior of the design. A named property is used for verification as
an assumption, an obligation, or a coverage specification.
In NPI Language model, a named property declaration (property decl) might be declared
with formal arguments (prop formal decl) and defined by a property specification
(property spec).
A property specification might be composed by its clocking event, property expression
(property expr), and disable condition.
A property expression is a class that contains general operation, sequence expression
(sequence expr), and property instance (property inst).

In the aforementioned example, "example.prop1" and "example.prop2" are property
declarations with object type "npiPropertyDecl".
There are two property formal declarations, "a" and "b", that are belonged to
"example.prop1" and the object type is npiPropFormalDecl.
The property is defined by a behavior of a design, the behavior means a property
spec (npiPropertySpec). For example, and the property spec of "example.prop2" is
"@(posedge clk) disable iff (x==y) x |=> y;".
In this property spec, the corresponding clocking event is "@(posedge clk) " that could be
obtained by applying 1-1 method npiClockingEvent.
The corresponding disable condition is "(x==y)" that could be obtained by applying 1-1
method npiDisableCondition.
The rest part "x |=> y" is the property expression. If the clocking event and disable
condition do not exist, the returned object of npiClockingEvent and npiDisableCondition
is NULL.
The prop1 is instantiated in "ASSERT1". By applying npiPropertyDecl relation, the
corresponding property declaration object "example.prop1" would be retrieved.

* For a property instance object, applying 1-1 method npiPropertyDecl returns the
corresponding property declaration.
* For a property declaration object, the npiPropFormalDecl iterator returns the property
declaration arguments.
The npiVariables iterator returns all variables under the scope of a property
declaration.
The 1-1 method npiPropertySpec returns the property specification defined in the
property declaration.
* For a property formal declaration, the npiTypespec relation returns the object directed
to the typespec of the formal.
If the formal is untyped, the returned typespec is NULL. If the formal has an
initialization expression, the expression can be obtained using the npiExpr relation.

The npiDirection returns npiNoDirection if the formal argument is not a local variable.
Otherwises, npiDirection returns npiInput.
* For a property specification, the npiClockingEvent relation returns the clocking scene
to evaluate the property. Applying method npiDisableCondition returns an expression
that described the disable condition.
The npiPropertyExpr relation returns the property expression that is used to evaluate
if the property is hold or failed.

Reference Objects
A reference object represents a declared object or sub element of that object that is a
reference to an actual instantiated object. A reference object exists for ports with ref
direction, for an interface port, a modport port, or for formal task function ref arguments.

interface sb;
sb s();
// m1's port is a. Its high conn is a ref obj which gets
// an interface named "s" by applying method "npiActual"
mm m1(s /* ref obj*/ );
// m2's port is a. Its high conn is a ref obj which gets
// a modport named "master" by applying method "npiActual"
mm m2(s.master /* ref obj */);
module mm(interface a); // port a's low conn is ref obj named "a"
// which gets an interface "top.s"
// for m1 and get modport "top.s.master"
// for m2 by applying method "npiActual".
logic d1, d2, d3, d4;

always@(a.data) begin
a.tsk(d1, d2, pk); // For each argument, a ref obj is
a.tsk(d3, d4, pk); // obtained by using npiExpr, but this ref
// obj npiExpr, but this ref obj gets
// nothing by applying method "npiActual".
// (limitation)
end

In the example code above, the higher port connection (highconn) "s" of the module
instance "top.m1" is a ref obj. Similarly, the highconn "s.master" of module instance
"top.m2" is a ref obj.
The lower port connection (lowconn) of "top.m1" and "top.m2" is also a ref obj named
"a". By applying the method "npiActual" to the ref obj "top.m1.a", the interface "top.s" is
obtained.
By applying the method "npiActual" to the ref obj "top.m2.a", the modport "top.s.master" is
obtained.

* A ref obj exists for ports with ref direction, for an interface port, a modport port, or for
formal task function ref arguments. The specific cases for a ref obj are:
A variable, named event, named event array that is the lowconn of a ref port.
Any sub element expression of the above.
A local declaration of an interface or modport passed through a port or any net,
variable, named event, named event array of those.
A ref formal argument of a task or function, or sub element expression of it.
* The npiActual relationship always returns the actual instantiated object if the ref obj is
bound to an actual object at the time of the query.
* The npiParent relationship allows the traversal of a ref obj that is a sub element of a ref
obj.
In the following example, r[0] is a ref obj whose parent is the ref obj r. The npiActual
for the ref obj r[0] would return the var bit a[0] and the npiActual of the ref obj r would
return the variable a:
module m (ref logic [2:0] r);
r[0] = 1'b0;
logic [2:0] a;
m u1 (a);

* If any ref obj could have different actual objects during simulation like the following
task call example, npiActual for this ref obj becomes unsupported (treated as a current
limitation).
task automatic tsk(output dout, input din, ref shift);
// ref obj shift doesn't support npiActual
dout = din + shift;
logic dout, din;
bit s0 = 1'b0;
bit s1 = 1'b1;
mm m0();
m0.tsk(dout, din, s0);
// ref obj shift is actually s0 at this time point
m0.tsk(dout, din, s1);
// ref obj shift is actually s1 at this time point
end

* Applying method npiActual gets the actual object no matter how many levels this ref obj
passes through. Besides, the actual object does not contain any non-constant index or
slice.
In the following example, the npiActual for the ref obj top.u1.r[mp] would return the var
bit top.a[0][1], not var bit top.a[p][mp]:
module m (ref logic [2:0] r);
parameter mp = 1;
r[mp] = 1'b0;
logic [2:0][2:0] a;
m u1 (a[p]);

* The npiGeneric property returns TRUE if the ref obj is a reference to a generic interface
and FALSE if the ref obj is a reference to an interface that is not a generic interface.
The npiGeneric property returns npiUndefined for all other kinds of ref obj.
* The npiDefName property when applied to a ref obj that is an actual of an interface or
modport returns the interface definition name or modport name.
* The npiTypespec property returns NULL for a ref obj of which npiActual is a not a net,
net select, variable or var select.

* Ref obj cannot get its actual (gets npiNIY) if its actual is a virtual interface.
* Applying method npiRefObj gets the ref objs whose actual is the same with the
declaration of reference handle.
In the following example, the npiRefObj for the var bit "top.i1.a[0]" would return the ref
obj "top.u1.intf.a":
interface ii ;
reg [5:0] a;
module m(interface intf);
intf.a[3] = intf.a[1];
ii i1();
m u1 (i1);

External Reference
An external reference object represents an expression that is a reference to an actual
instantiated object belonged to external scope.
Method npiActual can retrieve the actual instantiated object belonged to an external
scope. Method npiScope can obtain the scope handle of the given external reference
N/A

import p::*;
wire t1 = intf.data; // external reference
wire t2 = struct_t1.a; // external reference
wire t3 = union_t2.a; // external reference
enum_t3 t4 = a; // external reference
integer t5 = pi; // external reference
always@(intf.data) // external reference
intf.tsk(d1, d2, pk); // external reference

In example.v, the external reference objects are the reference of objects that belongs to
external scope.
For example, "intf.data" is an external reference object whose actual object is directed to
"dut.top_inst.intf.data". By applying method npiActual of the object "intf.data", the actual
object is obtained.
By applying method npiScope, the current scope "dut.top_inst" of the external reference
object is returned.
In addition, the objects that are crossed scope by using "import" are also treated as
external reference objects.

Sequence
A sequence provides the capability to build and manipulate sequential behaviors.
In NPI Language model, a named sequence declaration (sequence decl) might be
declared with formal arguments (seq formal decl) and defined by a sequence expression
(sequence expr).
The sequence expression might be composed by one or several Boolean expressions.
The sequence expression is a class that contains operation, sequence instance
(sequence inst), and expression.

example.sv

module example ( input clk,
input bit x,
input bit y
);

sequence seq (bit a, bit b);
/* sequence decl with two seq formal
decls */
bit c = !a;
@(posedge clk) a 1 b 1 c; /* clocking event: posedge clk */
/* sequence expr: a1 b1 c */
endsequence
property prop;
seq(x, y);
y */
endproperty

/* sequence inst with two arguments x and

In the aforementioned example, "example.seq" is a sequence declaration and the object
type is npiSequenceDecl.
There are two sequence formal declarations belonged to "example.seq", "a" and "b", with
object type npiSeqFormalDecl.
The npiDirection property of both sequence formal declarations is npiNoDirection
because "a" and "b" are not local variables of "example.seq".
Applying npiTypespec relation on "a" or "b" returns the a typespec object whose npiType
is npiBitTypespec.
Applying the method npiExpr on "example.seq" returns the operation "@(posedge clk)
a 1 b 1 c".
The sequence expression "@(posedge clk) a 1 b 1 c" is evaluated to check if the
sequence is true or false.
Since the expression contain a clocking event "@(posedge clk)", the clocking event
expression can be retrieved by the 1-1 method npiClockingEvent from the sequence
declaration.
The sequence expression "a 1 b 1 c" is returned by applying the 1-1 method
npiExpr from the sequence declaration.
The sequence is instantiated under "example.prop". By using npiPropertyDecl relation
on a sequence instance (npiSequenceInst), the corresponding sequence declaration is

* For a sequence instance object, applying 1-1 method npiSequenceDecl returns the
corresponding sequence declaration.
* For a sequence declaration object, the npiSeqFormalDecl iterator returns the
sequence declaration arguments.
The npiVariables iterator returns all variables under the scope of a sequence
declaration. The 1-1 method npiExpr returns the sequence expression defined in the
sequence declaration.
* For a sequence formal declaration, the npiTypespec relation returns the object
directed to the typespec of the formal. If the formal is untyped, the returned typespec is
NULL.
If the formal has an initialization expression, the expression can be obtained using the
npiExpr relation.
The npiDirection returns npiNoDirection if the formal argument is not a local variable.
Otherwise, npiDirection returns npiInput, npiOutput, or npiInout.

In the NPI Language model, scope is a class that contains several objects including
named begin (npiNamedBegin), begin (npiBegin), named fork (npiNamedFork), fork
(npiFork), gen scope (npiGenScope), for (npiFor), class object (npiClassObj), class
definition (npiClassDefn), and class typespec (npiClassTypespec). Scope also contains
two classes: "instance" and "task func".

module top; /*module*/
mm u1 /*module*/(w1, w2[0]);
mm u2 [3:0] (w1, w2);
initial begin: INIT_BLK /*named block*/
end

In the example code above, "top", "top.u1", "top.u2[3]", "top.u2[2]", "top.u2[1]" and
"top.u2[0]" are all objects with type "module" (npiModule).
Module object belongs to class instance, and class instance belongs to class
scope, as a result, all methods supported by scope class is applied to the
module objects.

In addition to the module objects, named begin object named "INIT_BLK" is
also an object which belongs to scope.

1. An unnamed begin or unnamed fork is a scope, if and only if it directly contains a block
item declaration such as a variable declaration or type declaration. A named begin or
named fork is always a scope.
begin : BLK
var logic v; // This declaration is not local to the
// unnamed begin
v = 1'b1;
end
end

In this example, the block BLK is a scope, but the unnamed begin is not a scope
because it does not directly contain a block item declaration.
2. A for statement is a scope if and only if the npiLocalVarDecls property returns TRUE.
In this case, the scope of each loop control variable is the for statement, refer to For

Task and Function Calls
Task call and function call are the statements in SystemVerilog.
"task and function call" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

reg [7:0] v0,v1,v2;
wire clk;
wire w1, w2,w3, a, b, c, w;
wire [31:0] result0, result1;
incr(v0+v1,v2); // this is a task call
// foo(w2,w1) is a function call
assign w3 = foo(w2,w1);
// system function call w/o argument
assign result0 = $random();
// system function call with argument
assign result1 = $usr_sysfunc(a,b,c);

// system task call
$display("value of w = %x",w);
$usr_systask(a,b,c);
end
function foo; // function declaration
input f1, f2;
foo = f1 & f2;
end
task incr; // task declaration
input [7:0] t1;
output [7:0] tout;
tout = t1 + 1;
end

Applying npiArgument to the task call "incr(v0+v1,v2)" gets the expression "v0+v1" and
then simple expression "v2".

* An empty (omitted) argument is represented as an expression with a npiType of
npiOperation and a npiOpType of npiNullOp.
An argument consisting of the special value null is represented as an expression with a
npiType of npiConstant and a npiConstType of npiNullConst. For example:
logic my_var;
$my_task(my_var, "", , null, );

In the call to the user-defined system task $my_task(), my_var is an ordinary argument
of type npiReg. The second argument, an empty string (but not an empty argument), is
a npiConstant for which the npiConstType is npiStringConst.
The third and fifth arguments are empty arguments, while the fourth argument is a
npiConstant with a npiConstType of npiNullConst. NPI represents the third and fifth
arguments as npiOperations with a npiOpType of npiNullOp.
* For the npiFuncCall, npiSysFuncCal and npiMethodFuncCall, if the npiIsExpr is true,
the npiUpperStmt of these handles should be NULL.

Task and Function Declaration
Task (npiTask) and function (npiFunction) declarations provide the ability to execute
common procedures from several different places in a description.
Task and function declaration belongs to the class "scope".

// task declaration
task tsk(output integer y,
input integer x,
ref reg [7:0][1:0] ref_data);
assign x = x+1;
deassign x;
x = x+1;
y <= x+2;
// automatic task
task automatic tsk_auto(input time ii,
output time oo,
inout time io);
oo = ii-io;

// function declaration
function [1:0] cpy (input [1:0] data, inout real success);
cpy = data;
success = 1.0;
// automatic func
function automatic integer factorial (input [31:0] operand);
integer i;
if (operand == 0)
i = 0;
if (operand >= 2)
factorial = factorial (operand - 1) * operand;
factorial = 1;

In the example code above, "tsk", "tsk_auto" are objects with type "task" (npiTask). "cpy"
and "factorial" are objects with type "function" (npiFunction).
Applying npi_handle(npiReturn, function_handle_cpy) to the function "top.cpy", the
variable handle of "top.cpy.cpy" is returned.

1. A SystemVerilog function contains an object with the same name, size, and type as the
function. This object is used to capture the return value for this function.
2. For function where return type is a user-defined type, npi_handle(npiReturn,
function_handle) returns the implicit variable handle representing the return of the
function from which the user can get the details of that user-defined type.
3. npiReturn always returns a var object, even for simple returns.
4. If the npiSize of the npiReturn variable is defined and is determined without evaluating
the function, npiSize for the function returns the same value as npiSize for the
npiReturn variable.
For a void function, npiSize returns 0. For all other cases the behavior of npiSize is
undefined.
5. For every function declaration, there is an implicit signal whose name is the same
as the one of function name, for example, in the following example, there is signal
"top.foo.foo", first "foo" is the function scope, 2nd "foo" is the signal.
function foo;
input f1, f2;
foo = f1 & f2;

end

Typespec
Typespec objects in NPI Language model denote the data type of objects, including both
predefined types and user-defined types.
You can obtain additional information from a typespec object, such as signedness, array
type, and range declaration.

wire [7:0] w [3:0][4:0]; /*array typespec of w*/
real r; /*real typespec of r*/
integer i; /*integer typespec of i*/
time t; /*time typespec of t*/
reg [7:0] r2; /*logic typespec of r2*/
wire [7:0] w2; /*logic typespec of w2*/
nettype logic[1:0] n1; /* nettype typespec */

In the example code above, typespec of signal "w" is an "array
typespec" (npiArrayTypespec) whose range is "[3:0][4:0]" (returned by the npiRange
transition) and whose element typespec (returned by npiElemTypespec) is "logic
typespec" (npiLogicTypespec) with range "[7:0]". Wire is 4-value so its typespec is logic
typespec.
Typespec of variable "r" is "real typespec" (npiRealTypespec), typespec of variable
"i" is "integer typespec" (npiIntegerTypespec), typespec of variable "t" is "time
typespec" (npiTimeTypespec).
Typespec of variable "r2" and "w2" are "logic typespec" (npiLogicTypespec) with range
"[7:0]" (returned by the npiRange transition)
The nettype definition "n1" is a "nettype typespec" (npiNettypeTypespec) that is defined as
"logic[1:0]".

* If a typespec denotes a type that has a user-defined typedef, the npiName property
returns the name of that type. Otherwise, except in the case of a class typespec, the
npiName property returns NULL.
Consequently the npiName property returns NULL for any SystemVerilog built-in type.
If the typespec denotes a type with a typedef that creates an alias of another typedef,
then the npiTypedefAlias of the typespec returns a non-null handle, which represents
the handle to the aliased typedef. For example:
typedef enum bit [0:2] {red, yellow, blue} primary_colors;
typedef primary_colors colors;

If "h1" is a handle to the typespec colors, its npiType returns npiEnumTypespec,
the npiName property returns "colors", npiTypedefAlias returns a handle `h2' to the
typespec `primary_colors' of npiType npiEnumTypespec.

The npiName property for `h2' returns `primary_colors', and its npiTypedefAlias
returns NULL. For general typespec handles that are defined by a basic type, method
npiTypedefAlias returns NULL with the following exception:
For a given nettype typespec handle that is defined by a basic type,
npiTypedefAlias returns the aliased nettype handle to the corresponding basic
typespec.
The npiName of the returned handle is NULL. For example:
nettype bit [1:0] BIT2;
nettype BIT2 SIG;

Both of `BIT2' and `SIG' are handles to nettype typespec (npiNettyeTypespec).
Applying npiTypedefAlias to `SIG' returns a handle to `BIT2' whose npiType is
npiNettypeTypespec.
Applying npiTypedefAlias to `BIT2' returns a handle to a logic typespec handle
(npiLogicTypespec). And the npiName of the logic typespec handle is NULL.
* npiIndexTypespec relation is present only on associative array typespecs and returns
the type that is used as the key into the associative array.
For the wildcard index type, npiIndexTypespec returns NULL.
* If the value of the property npiType of a typespec is npiStructTypesec or
npiUnionTypespec, then it is possible to iterate over npiTypespecMember to obtain the
structure of the user-defined type.
For each typespec member, the typespec relation indicates the type of the member.
* The property npiName of a typespec member returns the name of the corresponding
member, rather than the name (if any) of the associated typespec.
* The name of a typedef might be the empty string if the typespec denotes a typedef field
defined in line rather than through a typedef declaration. For example:
struct
} B
} C;

The typespec representing the typedef C is a struct typespec; it has a single typespec
member named B. The typespec relation for B returns another struct typespec that has
no name and has a single typespec member named "a". The typespec relation for "a"
returns an int typespec.

* If a type is defined as an alias of another type, it inherits the npiType of this other type.
typedef time my_time;
my_time t;

The npiTypespec of the variable named "t" returns a handle h1 to the typespec
"my_time" whose npiType is a npiTimeTypespec.
* The expr associated with a typespec member represents the explicit default member
value, if any, of the corresponding member of an unpacked structure data type.
* The npiElemTypespec transition is used to unwind the typespec of an unpacked array
(array typespec) or a packed array (packed array typespec, or a bit or logic typespec
with one or more dimensions) one dimension level at a time.
This means that for a multi-dimensional array typespec (a typespec with more than
one unpacked range), npi_handle (npiElemTypespec, array_typespec_handle) initially
retrieves npiArrayTypespec equivalent to the original typespec with its left-most
unpacked range removed.
Subsequent calls to the npiElemTypespec method continue the unwinding until a
typespec object is retrieved that has no unpacked ranges remaining.
Similarly, when the npiElemTypespec is applied to a typespec of a multidimensional packed array object, a npiPackedArrayTypespec (or npiBitTypespec or
npiLogicTypespec) is retrieved which is equivalent to the original typespec with its leftmost packed range removed, and so on, until a typespec without an explicit packed
range is retrieved.
When the npiElemTypespec relation is applied to npiStructTypespec,
npiUnionTypespec, npiEnumTypespec, or npiBitTypespec or npiLogicTypespec with no
ranges present, it returns NULL.
This allows packed or unpacked array typespecs constructed with multiple typedefs to
be unwound without losing name information. Consider the complex array typespec
defined below for arr:
typedef struct packed { int i1; bit bvec; } [1:3] parrtype;
typedef parrtype [2:1] parrtype2;
typedef parrtype2 unparrtype [6:4];
unparrtype arr [3:0];

The typespec of the object arr is an unpacked 4 x 3 array typespec with a NULL
npiName property. The typespec retrieved by applying npiElemTypespec to this is a 3element unpacked array typespec with a npiName property of "unparrtype".
The typespec retrieved by using npiElemTypespec on this in turn yields a 2 x 3 packed
array typespec (of packed struct objects) with npiName property of "parrtype2".

Using npiElemTypespec again in turn yields another packed array typespec (of 3
packed struct objects) with npiName property of "parrtype".
One more application of npiElemTypespec to this result yields a struct typespec, a nonarray typespec for which no further array sub elements exist (the unwinding is done).
* For an array typespec, npi_iterate(npiRange, handle) returns the set of array range
declarations beginning with the left-most unpacked range and iterating through the
right-most unpacked range.
* If any dimension of the array typespec corresponds to a dynamic array, associative
array, or queue, the iteration returns an empty range for that dimension.
For a logic typespec or bit typespec that has an associated range, the iteration returns
the set of ranges beginning with the left-most packed range and iterating through the
right-most packed range.
Besides, the iteration always returns the resolved (flatten) ranges to represent its actual
data type. For example:
typedef bit [1:0] DB;
DB [2:0][3:0] db_var;

The typespec of db_var obtains three ranges ([2:0], [3:0] and [1:0]) by applying 1-tomany method, npiRange.
* For a nettype typespec handle (npiNettypeTypespec), npi_handle(npiResFunc, handle)
returns the resolution function of the nettype handle. If the nettype handle does not
have resolution function, npi_handle(npiResFunc, handle) returns NULL.
real field1;
bit field2;
} T;
function automatic T Tsum (input T driver[]);
Tsum.field1 = 0.0;
foreach (driver[i])
Tsum.field1 += driver[i].field1;
nettype T wT; // an unresolved nettype wT whose data type is T
nettype T wTsum with Tsum; // a nettype wTsum with resolution function
"Tsum"

In the aforementioned example, `wT' is handle to a nettype typespec and the resolution
function is NULL. `wTsum' is a handle to a nettype typespec and the resolution function
is `Tsum'.

* Only typedef typespec handles (whose npiName property does not return NULL)
obtains its location information by npiFile and npiLineNo.
The other kinds of typespec handle returns NULL and -1 by applying npiFile and
npiLineNo.

In the aforementioned example, "example.seq" is a sequence declaration and the object
type is npiSequenceDecl.
There are two sequence formal declarations belonged to "example.seq", "a" and "b", with
object type npiSeqFormalDecl.
The npiDirection property of both sequence formal declarations is npiNoDirection
because "a" and "b" are not local variables of "example.seq".
Applying npiTypespec relation on "a" or "b" returns the a typespec object whose npiType
is npiBitTypespec.
Applying the method npiExpr on "example.seq" returns the operation "@(posedge clk)
a 1 b 1 c".
The sequence expression "@(posedge clk) a 1 b 1 c" is evaluated to check if the
sequence is true or false.
Since the expression contain a clocking event "@(posedge clk)", the clocking event
expression can be retrieved by the 1-1 method npiClockingEvent from the sequence
declaration.
The sequence expression "a 1 b 1 c" is returned by applying the 1-1 method
npiExpr from the sequence declaration.
The sequence is instantiated under "example.prop". By using npiPropertyDecl relation
on a sequence instance (npiSequenceInst), the corresponding sequence declaration is

* For a sequence instance object, applying 1-1 method npiSequenceDecl returns the
corresponding sequence declaration.
* For a sequence declaration object, the npiSeqFormalDecl iterator returns the
sequence declaration arguments.
The npiVariables iterator returns all variables under the scope of a sequence
declaration. The 1-1 method npiExpr returns the sequence expression defined in the
sequence declaration.
* For a sequence formal declaration, the npiTypespec relation returns the object
directed to the typespec of the formal. If the formal is untyped, the returned typespec is
NULL.
If the formal has an initialization expression, the expression can be obtained using the
npiExpr relation.
The npiDirection returns npiNoDirection if the formal argument is not a local variable.
Otherwise, npiDirection returns npiInput, npiOutput, or npiInout.
