Vh Subprogram, Vh Subprogram Declaration
In the NPI Language model, the vh subprogram is a class that contains vh function and vh
procedure. The subprogram in the NPI VHDL model means the subprogram body, not the
declaration.
The subprogram declaration part is modeled as vh subp decl. Similarly, vh subp decl is
also a class that contains vh func decl and vh proc decl.

package PP is

shared variable WDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
constant WDC: WEEK_DAY := WED;
incr_proc(WDS, WDV, WDC);
process (WDS)
variable PWDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
variable PIV: integer := 0;
procA(WDS, WDS, PWDV, PWDV);
PIV := funcA(WDS) + funcB(WDS) + check_week_day(WDS, WDS, WDS);

A function declaration (npiVhFuncDecl) named "funcA" under package declaration "PP"
is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpDecl. However, the function
declaration "funcA" can also obtain its function (body) by applying one-to-one method
npiVhSubpBody.
In vh root "top", there are four subprogram declarations (two npiVhProcDecl objects and
two npiVhFuncDecl objects): procA, funcB, procDeclOnly and funcDeclOnly.
Two relative subprogram bodies ("top.procA" and "top.funcB") for procA and funcB is
obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpBody.
In vh root "top", there are four subprograms (two npiVhProcedure objects and two
npiVhFunction objects): incr_proc, procA, procB and check_week_day.
For npiVhProcedure "top.procA" and npiVhFunction "top.funcB", npiVhProcDecl and
npiVhFuncDecl is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpDecl.

npiVhPure returns 0 if the vh func decl contains the keyword impure, otherwise it returns 1.

Vh Use
npiVhUse is a group that contains npiVhStmt, npiVhBranch and npiVhMapElem. Only
object declaration, parameter, indexed, slice and select name can obtain use by applying
method npiVhUse.
Use contains the object that overlaps the reference handle.

generic (GNR0, GNR1: std_logic_vector(31 downto 0));
port(ea : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0));
architecture circus of add32 is
signal SI1: std_logic_vector(31 downto 0) := GNR0;
SI1 <= GNR0; -- use GNR0, SI1
SI1(5) <= ea(0); -- use SI1(5)
end architecture circus;

In example.vhd above, generic "GNR0" gets signal assignment "SI1 <= GNR0;" by
applying method npiVhUse. Indexed name "SI1(5)" gets signal assignment "SI1 <=
GNR0;" and signal assignment "SI1(5) <= ea(0);" Port "ea" gets signal assignment "SI1(5)
<= ea(0);".

* For array, the npiVhUse relationship accesses any use of the array, the overlapped
part, the indexed select or slice select of the array. If any variable is in the index or
slice, it is treated as a free index.
For the following example, if npiVhUse is applied for "V1(5)", the results is "V1(i) :=
A1(i);", "V1(5) := V1(0);" and "V1(6 downto 5) := A1(0 to 1);"; if it is applied for "V1(0)",
the result is "V1(i) := A1(i);" and "V1(4 downto i) := A1(4 downto i);".
for i in 2 to 3 loop
V1(i) := A1(i);
V1(4 downto i) := A1(4 downto i);
V1(5) := V1(0);
V1(6 downto 5) := A1(0 to 1);

VHDL port under VHDL scope: The npiVhStmt which use this port and the

Vh Variable Assignment
A variable assignment is a type of sequential statement, and left-hand-side object
and right-hand-side objects is obtained by applying method npiVhLhs and npiVhRhs,

prcs: process (a, b)

-- var assignment stmt

N/A

Vh Wait
The vh wait is a type of sequential statement. Conditional expression, time expression,
and signals in the sensitivity list is obtained by applying relative method (see object
diagram).

process begin
-- npiVhWait
ws: wait on a(0), b(1 downto 0), cin until a(0)='0' for 1 ns;

For vh wait "ws", signals "a(0)", "b(1 downto 0)" and "cin" is returned when applying oneto-many method npiVhSensitivities. When applying one-to-one method npiVhCondExpr,
operation "a(0)='0'" is returned.
When applying one-to-one method npiVhTimeExpr, time expression (npiVhPhysLiteral) "1
ns" is returned.

N/A

npiVhWait

Vh Waveform
A waveform element is the basic waveform that contains the value expression and time
expression. A conditional waveform is a vh waveform element with conditional expression.
A selected waveform is a waveform element with choice expressions.

-- => obtain 1 waveform element with value expr: "a or b" and time
expr: "1 ns"
ssa0: sum <= a or b after 1 ns;
-- => obtain 3 conditional waveforms
csa0: sum <= a after 3 ns when cin = '0' else

-- => obtain 4 selected waveforms
sesa0: with NEXT_STATE select

The simple signal assignment "ssa0" obtains a waveform element "a or b after 1 ns" by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
The value expression "a or b" and the time expression "1 ns" is obtained by applying oneto-one method npiVhValExpr and npiVhTimeExpr, respectively.
The conditional signal assignment "csa0" obtains three conditional waveforms by applying
one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
These three waveforms are "a after 3 ns when cin = `0'", "b after 3 ns when cin = `1'" and
"a and b after 3 ns", and they can obtain their own waveform elements by applying one-toone method npiVhWaveformElem.
The former two conditional waveforms can obtain the conditional expressions "cin = `0'"
and "cin = `1'" by applying one-to-one method npiVhCondExpr.
The selected signal assignment "sesa0" obtains four selected waveforms by applying
one-to-many method npiVhWaveform. These four waveforms are "x"00000001" after 1
ns when APPLY | RECEIVE | KEEP", "x"00000010" after 2 ns when WAITS | SLEEP",
"x"00000100" after 3 ns when RESET" and "unaffected when others", and they can obtain
their own waveform elements by applying one-to-one method npiVhWaveformElem.
For the first conditional waveform, three choice expressions "APPLY", "RECEIVE" and
"KEEP" is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices.

* For vh cond waveform, applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices returns nothing
when the choice condition is the reserved word others.
* For vh waveform elem, the reserved word unaffected is returned if its property
npiVhUnaffected returns 1.

Library
A library object in the NPI Netlist model serves as a container for cell objects. If you can
import design with symbol libraries, the NPI Netlist model can create corresponding cells
and shapes based on the cell definitions.

* Libraries is accessed using npi_nl_iterate with a NULL reference object.
* The npiNlLibPath property returns a string that represents the path of the library.
* The handles to library objects returned by npi_nl_iterate is not sorted since the
order of symbol libraries depends on the user configuration.

Cell
A cell object in the NPI Netlist model is a cell view which contains the information of cell
pins and cell functions.

1. The npiNlCellType property returns cell functions of instance objects, for example,,
npiNlEQCell, npiNlAndCell, and npiNlBufCell (refer to npi_nl.h).
2. The npiNlPowerCellType property returns power cell functions of instance objects
inferred from liberty.
For example,, npiNlPowerISOCell, npiNlPowerRETCell and npiNlPowerLVSCell
(refer to npi_nl.h).
3. The Boolean property npiNlIsMemoryCell returns TRUE if it has memory() definition in
liberty.
4. The Boolean property npiNlIsPadCell returns TRUE if it has the attribute "pad_cell"
being "true" in liberty.

Cell Pin
A cell pin object in the NPI Netlist model represents the pin of a library cell.

Following is an example of library definition:
library(test) {
cell(level_shifter) {
is_level_shifter : true;
level_shifter_type : HL;
pad_cell : "true";
std_cell_main_rail : true;
pg_function : "VSS";
switch_function : "VDD + VSS";
}
}
area:1;
pin (A) {
input_voltage_range ( 0.7 , 0.9);
}
pin (B) {

function : "A";
power_down_function : "!VDD + VSS";
is_pad : "true" ;
output_voltage_range (1.1 , 1.3)
}
}
cell(ret_cell) {
retention_cell : my_ret_cell;
}
}
pin (RETN) {
related_ground_pin: VSS;
always_on : true;
retention_pin (save_restore, "1");
}
}
}

* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.VDD", the npiNlIsStdCellMainRailPin
returns TRUE.
* The npiNlVoltageName returns "VDD", the npiNlPGFunc returns "VSS" and the
npiNlSwitchFunc returns "VDD + VSS".
* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.A", the npiNlRelatedPower and
npiNLRelatedGround returns "VDD" and "VSS". The npiNlInputVoltageRngMax and
npiNlInputVoltageRngMin returns "0.9" and "0.7" respectively.
* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.B", the npiNlIsPad returns TRUE; the
npiNlRelatedPower and npiNLRelatedGround returns "VDD" and "VSS".
The npiNlOutputVoltageRngMax and npiNlOutputVoltageRngMin returns "1.3"
and "1.1" respectively, and the npiNlPowerDownFunc returns "!VDD + VSS".
* For cell pin handle "test.ret_cell.RETN", the npiNlIsAlwaysOn returns TRUE, the
npiNlRetPinClassName returns "save_restore".

* For a pg_pin,
npiNlIsStdCellMainRailPin property returns TRUE when std_cell_main_rail
attribute is set true, return FALSE when set false or not set.
npiNlVoltageName property returns the string that represents the voltage_name
attribute defined in the pg_pin.
npiNlPGFunc, npiNlSwitchFunc returns the string that represents the
pg_function, and switch_function attribute specified in the pg_pin, respectively.
* For a non-pg_pin,
npiNlRelatedPower and npiNLRelatedGround property returns the string of its
specified related_power_pin and related_ground_pin.
If it is not specified, it returns npiNlUndefined. That means, it does not return the
default first primary_power nor the first primary_ground.
npiNlIsAlwaysOn property returns TRUE when always_on attribute is set true;
return FALSE when set false or not set.
For a cell pin in a pad_cell(with pad_cell set "true"), npiNlIsPad property

For an output pin, npiNlPowerDownFunc property returns the string of its specified
power_down_function.

For a cell pin in a level-shifter cell (with is_level_shifter set

An instance object in the NPI Netlist model could be a module instance or a primitive
instance. A module instance denotes a module reference in the design that serves as a
container for sub instance, port, instance port, and net objects.
A primitive instance denotes the minimum design unit. It is used to represent low-level
logic gates and switches with specific cell functions.
For example, npiNlAndCell, npiNlFSMCell, and npiNlBufCell.

* Top-level instances are accessed using npi_nl_iterate with a NULL reference object.
* The npiNlInstType property denotes the instance type used in the NPI Netlist model.
Available values include npiNlHierInst, npiNlRTLInst, npiNlSymbolLibInst,
npiNlFSMInst, and npiNlUDPInst.
The npiNlFSMInst is returned for npiNlInstType only when the value of
option "RecogFSM" is TRUE (see Schematic Configurations).
* The npiNlDefName property denotes the instance definition name. For any instance
objects with npiNlInstType of npiNlRTLInst or npiNlFSMInst, the npiNlDefName
property returns NULL.
* The npiNlCellType property returns cell functions of instance objects. for example,
npiNlModuleCell, npiNlAndCell, and npiNlBufCell (refer to npi_nl.h).
* The Boolean property npiNlIsInterface returns TRUE for an instance object if it is
inferred from a SystemVerilog interface.
* The Boolean property npiNlIsModport returns TRUE for an instance object if it is
inferred from a SystemVerilog modport.
* The Boolean property npiNlIsIntfConnector returns TRUE for an instance object if it
is inferred to connect the modport net and the whole interface port.
* The Boolean property npiNlIsIntfNet returns TRUE for an instance object if it is
inferred from the net of interface.
* The location properties npiNlFile, npiNlBeginLineNo, and npiNlEndLineNo returns
the file and line information of an instance object.
An instance object could be inferred from multiple sources. However, the
properties npiNlFile, npiNlBeginLineNo, and npiNlEndLineNo can only
obtain the information of the first source.
* The npiNlSrcInfo property returns a string that represents multiple source
information. The format of a returned string is as follows:
{ File1, BeginLineNo1, EndLineNo1} {File2, BeginLineNo2,
EndLineNo2}

To obtain more precise source information of an instance object, it is highly
recommended to use npiNlSrcInfo instead ofnpiNlFile, npiNlBeginLineNo, and
npiNlEndLineNo.

* An instance object with npiNlCellType of npiNlModuleCell, indicates that the
object is a module instance. For such instances,npiNlDriver, npiNlLoad, and
npiNlConnectivity relations returns NULL.
* An instance object with npiNlCellType that is not npiNlModuleCell, indicates that the
object is a primitive instance in the NPI Netlist model. Several specific rules for such
instance objects are described as follows:
* npiNlInst, npiNlPort, and npiNlNet relations always return NULL.
* npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations return the drivers and the loads of the instance,
respectively. Input and inout instance port objects are drivers of the instance; output
and inout instance port objects are loads of the instance.
* npiNlConnectivity relation returns all input, output, and inout instance port objects.
* The npiNlPowerCellType property returns power cell functions of instance objects
inferred from liberty, for example,npiNlPowerISOCell, npiNlPowerRETCell and
npiNlPowerLVSCell (refer to npi_nl.h).
* The Boolean property npiNlIsMemoryCell returns TRUE if it has memory() definition in
liberty.
* The Boolean property npiNlIsPadCell returns TRUE if it has the attribute "pad_cell"
being "true" in liberty.
* The npiNlPnRInfo property returns a string that represents place and route
information. The format of a returned string is as follows:
{"PnR_info": [{"x":LowerLeftX, "y":LowerLeftY}, {"x":UpperRightX,
"y":UpperRightY}]}

The LowerLeftX and LowerLeftY represent the lower-left corner of the rectangle. The
UpperRightX and UpperRightY represent the upper right corner of the rectangle.

Ports
A port object represents the port of a module instance. It is used to communicate between
instance port and net objects belonging to the module instance.

* The npiNlDirection property returns npiNlInput, npiNlOutput, or npiNlInout.
* For a pseudo port object, the npiNlParent relation returns the actual port object from
which the pseudo object is created.
* The npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations return net and instance port objects that
are drivers or loads of the given port.

For an input port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected instance port object,
while npiNlLoad relation returns the connected net object.
For an output port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected net object, while
npiNlLoad relation returns the connected instance port object.
For an inout port, both npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations return the connected
net and instance port objects.
* The npiNlConnectivity relation always returns the connected net and instance port
objects regardless of the port directions.
* Objects returned from npiNlInstPort, npiNlNet, and npiNlInst relations are
always actual objects.
* For the port with npiNlLangType of npiNlSPICE, the npiNlDirection property returns
npiNlInout.

Instance Ports
An instance port object represents the port instance along with the instance object. In
the NPI Netlist model, each instance port object has a specific property to indicate its
functional type.
For example, npiNlDataPort, npiNlClockPort, and npiNlLatchedPort.

* The npiNlDirection property returns npiNlInput, npiNlOutput, or npiNlInout.
* For a pseudo instance port object, the npiNlParent relation returns the actual instance
port object from which the pseudo object is created.
* The npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations returns net and port objects that are drivers
or loads of the given instance port.
* The npiNlConnectivity relation always returns the connected net and port objects
regardless of the port directions.
For an input instance port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected net object,
while npiNlLoad relation returns the connected port object.
For an output instance port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected port
object, while npiNlLoadrelation returns the connected net object.
For an inout instance port, both npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations return the
connected net and port objects.
* The npiNlPortType property returns functional types of instance port objects.
For example, npiNlDataPort, npiNlClockPort, and npiNlSyncSetPort (refer to
npi_nl.h).
* The npiNlPortState property returns the state of instance port objects. Available
values include: npiNlHighActive, npiNlLowActive, npiNlRisingActive, and
npiNlFallingActive.
For instance, port belonging to the instance with npiNlInstType of npiNlRTLInst,
npiNlSymbolLibInst, and npiNlFSMInst, the npiNlPortState property returns one
of the available values.

Nets
A net object represents physical connections between structural entities, such as instance
port and port.

* An npiNlDeclNet is an object that represents the full bus of an inferred net in the NPI
Netlist model.
In most cases, an npiNlDeclNet has a corresponding variable (for example, wire, reg,
logic, and so on). declaration in the design. However, additional npiNlDeclNet objects
could be created in the NPI Netlist model.
For example, in Figure 48, there are five npiNlDeclNet objects, "a", "b", "c", "d"
and "GEN0 d".
The first four objects have corresponding variable declarations in the HDL code. The
last npiNlDeclNet "GEN0 d", is an intermediate net object generated by the NPI
inference engine.

assign d = (a || b) && c;

An npiNlSliceNet in the NPI Netlist model is an object that represents a variable slice
in the source code, for example, part-select or bit-select.
npiNlSliceNet is different from npiNlPseudoNet; it is an actual object and
is always connected to one npiNlDeclNet object.

An npiNlConcatNet is an object concatenated with npiNlDeclNet and
npiNlSliceNet objects.
The following example illustrates the npiNlDeclNet, npiNlSlicelNet, and
npiNlConcatNet objects in the NPI Netlist model.

wire [5:0] c = {a[2:0],b[1:0]}; // a[2:0] and b[1:0] are slices of
wires a and b, separately

Object Type: npiTextFile

There is a one-to-many relationship from a NULL object to objects of type file.
There is a one-to-many relationship from an object of type file to objects of type line and a
many-to-one relationship from objects of type line to an object of type file.
Objects of type file have properties with their data type npiTextHandleType (string),
npiTextFileFullName (string), npiTextFileName (string), npiTextFileElabName (string),
npiTextFileContent (string), and npiTextLineCount (integer).

The property npiTextFileElabName means the file name used during the design
elaboration time of Verdi. Take the following case as an example:
The design file "example_inc.vh":

The design file "example.v":

After importing the design, the same source file "example_inc.vh" might becomes three
different text file handles, because of the define-undef sequence used in the example.v.

Therefore, in the design, there are four text file handles:
* npiTextFileName = example.v, npiTextFileElabName = example.v
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh#$#1
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh#$#2
The name of npiTextFileElabName is determined by Verdi system.
To map the type of object shown in the object diagram to the real type name
used in the C++/Tcl program, you need to add the prefix "npiText" in front of
the object name enclosed in the circle cape rectangle and change the first
character of the object name to uppercase.

Assign Statement, Deassign, Force, Release
Object Types: Assign Statement (npiDMAssignStmt), Deassign (npiDmDeassign),
Force (npiDmForce), Release (npiDmRelease)

Assign statement and force are procedural continues assignments (using keywords assign
and force) that allow expressions to be driven continuously onto variables or nets.
De-assign and release are procedure statements ends a procedure continues assignment
to a variable or a net.
Assign statement, de-assign, force, and release belong to the class of the atomic

reg ra;

assign ra = 1'bx; /* assign stmt */
deassign ra; /* deassign */
force w2 = 1'bz; /* force */
release w2; /* release */

* Apply method "npiDmLeft" to the handle "assign ra = 1'bx", and the npiDmVar handle
"ra" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRight" to the handle "assign ra = 1'bx", and the npiDmConstant
handle "1'bx" is returned.

Assignment
Object Type: npiDmAssignment

Assignment means a procedural assignment within a process and belongs to the class
atomic statement.
Property "npiDmOperator" returns npiDmAssignmentOp_e.

reg LHS, RHS, clk;
LHS = RHS; /* assignment_1 */

LHS = 10 RHS; /* assignment_2 */
LHS <= @(posedge clk) RHS; /* assignment_3 */
LHS <= repeat (5) @(posedge clk) RHS; /* assignment_4 */
LHS += 1; /* assignment_5 */
LHS++; /* assignment_6 */
end

* Apply method "npiDmLeft" to the handle "assignment_#1", and the npiDmVar handle
"LHS" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRight" to the handle "assignment_#1", and the npiDmVar handle
"RHS" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmDelayControl" to the handle "assignment_#2", and the
npiDmConstant handle "10" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmEventControl" to the handle "assignment_#3", and the
npiDmEventControl handle "@(posedge clk)" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRepeatControl" to the handle "assignment_#4", and the
npiDmRepeatControl handle "repeat(5) @(posedge clk)" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmBlocking" to handle "assignment_#1", and "1" is returned since it
is a blocking assignment.
* Apply property "npiDmBlocking" to handle "assignment_#3", and "0" is returned since it
is a non-blocking assignment.
* Apply property "npiDmOperator" to handle "assignment_#5", and
"npiDmPlusAssignOp" is returned.

Case, Case Item
Object Type: Case (npiDmCase), Case Item (npiDmCaseItem)

Case is a statement that is a multi way decision statement and tests whether an
expression matches one of a number of other expressions and branches accordingly.
Case item is a handle that consists of a condition expression and a statement. The
statement within case item represents a scenario of the case branches.
Case belongs to the class of the atomic statement. However, case item doesn't belong to
statement class.
Property "npiDmCaseType" returns npiDmCaseType_e.

module TOP(a, b, c);
input a, b, c;
reg [15:0] result;
reg [3:0] select;
always @ (a or b or c) begin
case(select) /* case statement */
4'd1, 4'd2, 4'd3: result = 16'h1111; /*case item 1*/
4'd4, 4'd5: result = 16'h2222; /*case item 2*/
default : result = 16'h0000; /*case item 3*/
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "case", and the npiDmVar handle
"select" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmCaseItem" to the handle "case", and three npiDmCaseItem
handles is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 1", and the npiDmConstant handle
"4'd1", "4'd2", and "4'd3" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "case item 1", and three npiDmAssignment
handle "result = 16'h1111" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 3", no handle is returned since it is
a default case item.
* Apply property "npiDmCaseType" to handle "case", and "npiDmCaseExact" is returned.

Assign Statement, Deassign, Force, Release
Object Types: Assign Statement (npiDMAssignStmt), Deassign (npiDmDeassign),
Force (npiDmForce), Release (npiDmRelease)

Assign statement and force are procedural continues assignments (using keywords assign
and force) that allow expressions to be driven continuously onto variables or nets.
De-assign and release are procedure statements ends a procedure continues assignment
to a variable or a net.
Assign statement, de-assign, force, and release belong to the class of the atomic

reg ra;

assign ra = 1'bx; /* assign stmt */
deassign ra; /* deassign */
force w2 = 1'bz; /* force */
release w2; /* release */

* Apply method "npiDmLeft" to the handle "assign ra = 1'bx", and the npiDmVar handle
"ra" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRight" to the handle "assign ra = 1'bx", and the npiDmConstant
handle "1'bx" is returned.

Assignment
Object Type: npiDmAssignment

Assignment means a procedural assignment within a process and belongs to the class
atomic statement.
Property "npiDmOperator" returns npiDmAssignmentOp_e.

reg LHS, RHS, clk;
LHS = RHS; /* assignment_1 */

LHS = 10 RHS; /* assignment_2 */
LHS <= @(posedge clk) RHS; /* assignment_3 */
LHS <= repeat (5) @(posedge clk) RHS; /* assignment_4 */
LHS += 1; /* assignment_5 */
LHS++; /* assignment_6 */
end

* Apply method "npiDmLeft" to the handle "assignment_#1", and the npiDmVar handle
"LHS" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRight" to the handle "assignment_#1", and the npiDmVar handle
"RHS" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmDelayControl" to the handle "assignment_#2", and the
npiDmConstant handle "10" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmEventControl" to the handle "assignment_#3", and the
npiDmEventControl handle "@(posedge clk)" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRepeatControl" to the handle "assignment_#4", and the
npiDmRepeatControl handle "repeat(5) @(posedge clk)" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmBlocking" to handle "assignment_#1", and "1" is returned since it
is a blocking assignment.
* Apply property "npiDmBlocking" to handle "assignment_#3", and "0" is returned since it
is a non-blocking assignment.
* Apply property "npiDmOperator" to handle "assignment_#5", and
"npiDmPlusAssignOp" is returned.

Atomic Statement
Atomic statement is a class composed of if, if-else, while, repeat, wait, case, for, delay
control, event control, event statement, assignment, assign statement, deassign, disable,
task call, function call, forever, force, release, do-while, return statement, break, continue,
and null statement.

; /*npiDmNullStmt*/
end

Case, Case Item
Object Type: Case (npiDmCase), Case Item (npiDmCaseItem)

Case is a statement that is a multi way decision statement and tests whether an
expression matches one of a number of other expressions and branches accordingly.
Case item is a handle that consists of a condition expression and a statement. The
statement within case item represents a scenario of the case branches.
Case belongs to the class of the atomic statement. However, case item doesn't belong to
statement class.
Property "npiDmCaseType" returns npiDmCaseType_e.

module TOP(a, b, c);
input a, b, c;
reg [15:0] result;
reg [3:0] select;
always @ (a or b or c) begin
case(select) /* case statement */
4'd1, 4'd2, 4'd3: result = 16'h1111; /*case item 1*/
4'd4, 4'd5: result = 16'h2222; /*case item 2*/
default : result = 16'h0000; /*case item 3*/
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "case", and the npiDmVar handle
"select" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmCaseItem" to the handle "case", and three npiDmCaseItem
handles is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 1", and the npiDmConstant handle
"4'd1", "4'd2", and "4'd3" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "case item 1", and three npiDmAssignment
handle "result = 16'h1111" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 3", no handle is returned since it is
a default case item.
* Apply property "npiDmCaseType" to handle "case", and "npiDmCaseExact" is returned.

Delay Control
Object Type: npiDmDelayControl

Delay control means that if a procedural assignment following the delay control is delayed
in its execution with respect to the procedural statement preceding the delay control by the
specified delay.
Delay control belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

reg reset, r1;
always /* process always */
100 /* delay control statement*/
begin: BLK /* named begin-end */
if(reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

* Apply method "npiDmDelay" to the handle "#100 begin: BLK end", and the
npiDmConstant handle "100" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "#100 begin: BLK end", and the
npiDmNamedBegin handle "begin: BLK" is returned.

Disable
Object Type: npiDmDisable

Disable provides the ability to terminate the activity associated with concurrently active
processes, while maintaining the structured nature of procedural descriptions.
Disable belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

disable blk_n; /* npiDmDisable */
end

Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "disable blk_n", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "blk_n" is returned.

Do-while
Object Type: npiDmDoWhile

Do-while is a kind of loop statement. It executes a statement first and tests its control
expression at the end of the loop.

The loop stops until do-while's control expression becomes false. Do-while belongs to the
class of the atomic statement.

do
// do while statement
begin : fff
x = x - 1;
if (x > 5) begin
end
end
while (x > 0);
return x + 10;
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "do-while", and the npiDmOperation
handle "x > 0" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "do-while", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "begin: fff" is returned.

Object Type: npiDmEvent

Event means the SystemVerilog event construct.

event ev; /*npiDmEvent*/
event evAry1 [3:0]; /*npiDmEvent*/
event evAry2 [1:0][2:0]; /*npiDmEvent*/
task too( ref event task_e /*npiDmEvent*/ );

Apply property "npiDmTaskFuncArgument" to the handle "task_e", and "1" is returned.

Event Control
Object Type: npiDmEventControl

Event control means that the execution of a procedural statement is synchronized with a
value change on a net or variable or the occurrence of a declared event.
Event control belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

reg clk, reset, r1;
always @(posedge clk or negedge reset) /* event control */
begin: BLK
if(!reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "event control", and the npiDmOperation
handle "posedge clk or negedge reset" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "event control", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "begin: BLK" is returned.

Event Statement
Object Type: npiDmEventStmt

Event statement means an event triggering statement. The blocking event is triggered
using the -> operator, and the non-blocking event is triggered using the ->> operator.
Event statement belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

event e2;
->e1; /* npiDmEventStmt_1 */
->>e2; /* npiDmEventStmt_2 */
end

* Apply method "npiDmEvent" to the handle "->e1", and the npiDmEvent handle "e1" is
* Apply property "npiDmBlocking" to handle "->>e2", and "0" is returned.

Expression, Constant, Operation
Object Type: Constant (npiDmConstant), Operation (npiDmOperation)

Simple expression is a class composed of net, variable, parameter, and interface
reference.
Constant means SystemVerilog constant literals or values such as "3'b001".
Operation is a construct that combines operands with operators such as "a[0]" or "{a, b}".
Property "npiDmConstType" returns npiDmConstType_e.
Property "npiDmOpType" returns npiDmOpType_e.
Property "npiDmDataType" returns npiDmDataType_e.
The "npiDmTypespec" method and the property "npiDmDataType" for operation are only
for the npiDmOpTypeCasting, npiDmOpTypeKeyAsgPtn, npiDmOpTypeStreamRL and
npiDmOpTypeStreamLR operations.

logic [$bits(w1):0] v1;
typedef integer usr_def_type;
usr_def_type u1;
assign {w1, w2} /*npiDmOperation*/ = 2'b01 /*npiDmConstant*/;
assign u1 = usr_def_type'(2'b11) /*npiDmOperation*/;
endmodul

* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "{w1, w2}", and the npiDmNet handles "w1"
and "w2" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmTypespec" to the handle "usr_def_type'(2'b11)", and a
npiDmTypespec handle "usr_def_type" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmUse" to the handle "w1", and the npiDmContAssign handle
"assign {w1, w2} = 2'b01" and the npiDmRange handle "[$bits(w1):0]" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmConstType" to handle "2'b01", and "npiDmConstBin" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmOpType" to handle "{w1, w2}", and "npiDmOpConcat" is
* Apply property "npiDmDataType" to handle "usr_def_type'(2'b11)", and
"npiDmDtTypespec" is returned.

For
Object Type: npiDmFor

For is a kind of loop statement. It consists of one or more initial statements, a control
expression, one or more step statements, and a statement which is executed every time
the control expression return true.
For belongs to the class of the scope and the atomic statement.
Only for statements containing variable declarations as part of the for-initialization
assignment create implicit begin-end block around the for-loop.
The block creates a new hierarchy scope, making the variables local to the loop scope.
Therefore, the proerty npiDmLocalVarDecls is used to decide whether a for statement is a

parameter int SIZE = 256;
integer index=0;
function myfunc;
for(index=0; index<SIZE; index=index+1) /* for statement */
begin: ggg
$display("aaa");
end
myfunc = 1;

* Apply method "npiDmForInitStmt" to the handle "for", and the npiDmAssignment handle
"index=0" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "for", and the npiDmOperation handle
"index<SIZE" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmForIncStmt" to the handle "for", and the npiDmAssignment handle
"index=index+1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "for", and the npiDmNamedBegin handle
"begin: ggg" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmLocalVarDecls" to handle "for", and "0" is returned.

Forever
Object Type: npiDmForever

Forever is a kind of loop statement. It continuously executes a statement. It belongs to the
class of the atomic statement.

forever CYCLE clk = ~clk; /* forever */
end

Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "forever", and the npiDmDelayControl handle
"#CYCLE clk = ~clk is returned.

Generate Block
Object Type: npiDmGenBlock

Generate block is a collection of one or more module items. It is either conditionally or
multiply instantiated in generate constructs.

A generate block might not contain port declarations, parameter declarations, specify
blocks or specparam declarations. All other modules items, including other generate
constructs, are allowed in a generate block.
* A generate construct must contain a generate block in DM model.
* A generate block is not a scope only if (1) it is within a conditionally generate
construct, (2) it has no begin-end keyword, and (3) it only contains another
conditionally generate construct.
* If a generate block's name is explicitly named, the property
"npiDmImplicitDecl" returns 0. Otherwise, this property returns 1.

module mm(input log);
module mm0(input a, b);

module mm1(input a, b);
parameter p = 1;
parameter q = 3;
wire w_ext1, w_ext2;
mm0 inst0(w_ext1, w_ext2);
if (p==1)
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
typedef bit T1;
mm inst1(v1);
xor g1 ( w1, w2, w3 );
function func1 ( input x );
task task1();
assign v1 = func1( w1 );
itf itf1();
initial /* npiDmInitial_1 */
end
genvar gvar1;
if(1) /* npiDmGenIf_1 */
begin : u2
end : u2
bind top.inst2 mm1 (1) b1 ( a, b ); /* npiDmBind_1 */
end
if (p==2) /* npiDmGenIf_2, npiDmGenBlock_2 */ ([Note]1)
;
if (p==3) /* npiDmGenIf_3, npiDmGenBlock_3 */
if (q==3) /* npiDmGenIf_4 */
begin /* npiDmGenBlock_4 */
end

* Apply property "npiDmName" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", "u1" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmImplicitDecl" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", "0" is returned.
([Note] 3)
* Apply property "npiDmImplicitDecl" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#2", "1" is returned.
([Note] 3)
* Apply method "npiDmNet" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the npiDmNet
handles "w1", "w2" and "w3" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmVar" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the npiDmVar
handle "v1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmEvent" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the npiDmEvent
handle "e1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmInstance" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmInstance handles "inst1" and "itf1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmPrimitive" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmPrimitive handle "g1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmTypespec" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmTypespec handle "T1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmTaskFunc" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmFunction handle "func1" and the npiDmTask handle "task1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmContAssign" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmContAssign handle "assign v1 = func1( w1 );" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmProcess" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmInitial handle "npiDmInitial_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmGenConstruct" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmGenIf handle "npiDmGenIf_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmBind" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the npiDmBind
handle "bind top.inst2 mm1 #(1) b1 ( a, b );" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmGenVar" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmGenVar handle "gvar1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handles "npiDmGenBlock_#1", and the
npiDmModule handle "top" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handles "npiDmGenIf_#1", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handles "npiDmGenBlock_#4", and the
npiDmModule handle "top" is returned (see NOTE #2).

Generate-case Construct, Generate-case Item
Object Types: Generate-case Construct (npiDmGenCase), Generate-case Item
(npiDmGenCaseItem)

Generate-case construct belongs to the conditional generate construct, which instantiates
at most one generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks.
Generate-case item is a handle that consists of a condition expression and a generate
block. The generate block within generate-case item represents a scenario of the
generate-case branches.
When generate-case item has no expression after applying method npiDmExpr,
it is a "default" generate-case item.

case(p) /* npiDmGenCase_1 */
1'b0: /* npiDmGenCaseItem_1 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
end
1'b1: /* npiDmGenCaseItem_2 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */
end
2,3: /*
begin :
end
default
begin :
end

npiDmGenCaseItem_3 */
u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_3 */
: /* npiDmGenCaseItem_4 */
u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_4 */

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "npiDmGenCase_#1", and the
npiDmParameter handle "p" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmGenCaseItem" to the handle "npiDmGenCase_#1", and the
npiDmGenCaseItem handles "npiDmGenCaseItem_#1" and "npiDmGenCaseItem_#2"
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "npiDmGenCaseItem_#1", and the
npiDmConstant handle "1'b0" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmGenBlock" to the handle "npiDmGenCaseItem_#1", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "npiDmGenCaseItem_#3", and the
npiDmConstant handle "2" and "3" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "npiDmGenCaseItem_#4", and no handle is
returned (see NOTE).

Generate Construct
Object Types: npiDmGenConstruct

Generate constructs are used to either conditionally or multiply instantiate generate blocks
into a model. They are if-generate, if-else-generate, case-generate and for-generate
constructs.
The if-generate, if-else-generate and case-generate constructs instantiate at most one
generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks. They belong to conditionally
generate constructs.
The for-generate construct allow a single generate block to be instantiated into a model
multiple times. It belongs to loop generate construct.

for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /* npiDmGenFor_1 */
begin : u1
end
if (p == 1) /* npiDmGenIf_1 */
end
if (p == 0) /* npiDmGenIfElse_1 */
end

end
case(p) /* npiDmGenCase_1 */
1'b0:
end
1'b1:
end

* Apply method "npiDmGenConstruct" to the handle "top", and the npiDmGenFor,
npiDmGenIf, npiDmGenIfElse, npiDmGenCase handles "npiDmGenFor_#1",
"npiDmGenIf_#1", "npiDmGenIfElse_#1", and "npiDmGenCase_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the npiDmModule
handle "top" is returned.

Generate-for Construct
Object Types: npiDmGenFor

Generate-for construct belongs to the loop generate construct, which instantiates a single
generate block into a model multiple times.
It consists of one initial statement, a control expression, one step statement, and a
generate block which is instantiated every time the control expression return true.

module top; /* npiDmModule_1 */
genvar i; /* npiDmGenVar_1 */
for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /* npiDmGenFor_1 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
end
for(genvar j = 0; j < 2; j++ ) /*npiDmGenFor_2, npiDmGenVar_2*/
begin : u2 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */
end

* Apply method "npiDmForInitStmt" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the
npiDmAssignment handle "i = 0" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the
npiDmOperation handle "i < 2" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmForIncStmt" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the
npiDmAssignment handle "i++" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmGenBlock" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmGenVar" to the handle "npiDmModule_#1", and the npiDmGenVar
handle "npiDmGenVar_#1" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmGenVar" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#2", and the
npiDmGenVar handle "npiDmGenVar_#2" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handle "npiDmGenVar_#2", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#2" is returned.

Generate-if Construct, Generate-if-else Item
Object Types: Generate-if Construct (npiDmGenIf), Generate-if-else Item
(npiDmGenIfElse)

Generate-if and generate-if-else constructs belong to the conditional generate construct,
which instantiates at most one generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks.

if (p == 1) /* npiDmGenIf_1 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
end
if (p == 0) /* npiDmGenIfElse_1 */
begin : v1 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */
end
begin : v1 /* npiDmGenBlock_3 */
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "npiDmGenIf_#1", and the
npiDmOperation handle "p==1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmGenBlock" to the handle "npiDmGenIf_#1", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmElseGenBlock" to the handle "npiDmGenIfElse_#1", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#3" is returned.

Genvar
Object Types: npiDmGenVar

Genvar is an integer during elaboration to evaluate the generate loop but it does not exist
at simulation time. It is not referenced anywhere other than in a loop generate scheme.
If a genvar has already been used as an index variable in an outer loop, it cannot be used
as an index variable in an inner loop.

module top; /* npiDmModule_1 */
genvar i; /* npiDmGenVar_1 */
for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /*npiDmGenFor_1, npiDmGenBlock_1*/
for (genvar j = 0; j < 4; j++) /* npiDmGenFor_2, npiDmGenVar_2 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */
end

* Apply method "npiDmGenVar" to the handle "npiDmModule_#1", and the npiDmGenVar
handles "npiDmGenVar_#1" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handle "npiDmGenVar_#1", and the npiDmModule
handle "npiDmModule_#1" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmGenVar" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#2", and the
npiDmGenVar handles "npiDmGenVar_#2" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handle "npiDmGenVar_#2", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#2" is returned.

Hierarchical Reference, Reference
Object Type: Hierarchical Reference (npiDmHierRef), Reference (npiDmRef)

There are several meaning for Hierarchical Reference in the DM model as follows:
* SystemVerilog hierarchial reference which accesses external scope object.
* SystemVerilog struct or union member access.
* SystemVerilog interface member access by interface port reference.
* SystemVerilog built-in method call of object.
The Reference is the segment of Hierarachical Reference. It contains the information of bit
select of part select and the actual object.

package pkg;
bit pa;
package pkg2;
bit pa2;

bit i1;
typedef struct { bit s1; bit s2; } T1;
import pkg2::pa2;
T1 s;
m1 i0();
// 1. hierarchical reference
assign pkg::pa = 1;
assign pa2 = 1;
// 1. hierarchical reference
assign top.i0.a[0][1:0] = 1;
// 2. struct member access
assign s.s1 = 1;
// 4. build-in method call
bit total;
byte b[] = { 1, 2, 3, 4 };
assign total = b.sum;
module m1( itf i );
bit [1:0][2:0] a;
// 3. interface member access by interface port reference
assign i.i1 = 1;

* Apply method "npiDmRef" to the the handle "top.i0.a[0][1:0]", and the npiDmRef
handles "top", "i0" and "a[0][1:0]" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmSelect" to the reference handle "a[0][1:0]", and the
npiDmOperation handles "[0]" and "[1:0]" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmActual" to the reference handle "a[0][1:0]", and the npiDmVar
handle "a" in the module m1 is returned.

If, If-else
Object Type: If (npiDmIf), If-else (npiDmIfElse)

If and if-else are conditional statements. They are used to make a decision about whether
a statement is executed.
If and if-else belong to the class of the atomic statement.

reg a, b, x, y, z;
if ( a & b ) /*npiDmIf*/
x = y;
if ( a | b ) /*npiDmIfElse*/
x = ~y;
x = z;
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "if", and the npiDmOperation handle "a &
b" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "if", and the npiDmAssignment handle "x = y"
* Apply method "npiDmElseStmt" to the handle "if-else", and the npiDmAssignment
handle "x = z" is returned.

Instance, Port Instance, Parameter Instance
Object Type: Instance (npiDmInstance), Port Instance (npiDmPortInst), Parameter
Instance (npiDmParamInst)

Instance means the SystemVerilog instance construct of a module or an interface.
Port Instance is the connection to the port. Parameter Instance is the connection to the
parameter.
The left index of the instance array is accessed by the method "npiDmLeft".
The right index of the instance array is accessed by the method "npiDmRight".
If the instance array has only one index such as "m i0 [1] ();", the index is accessed by the
method "npiDmLeft".
The instance in the bind construct which is not a real instance. The instance has no
real parameter and port connections. Apply the property "npiDmBindInst" to check if the
instance is in the bind. Any manipulation on the bind instance is not allowed.

bind top mm ( 3/*npiDmParamInst*/, 4 /*npiDmParamInst*/ )
b1 /*npiDmInstance*/
( w5/*npiDmPortInst*/, w6/*npiDmPortInst*/ );
module m();

parameter P1, P2;
wire cc;
wire w1, w2, w3, w4, w5, w6;
m inst_ary [1:0] (); /*npiDmInstance*/
mm ( 1 /*npiDmParamInst*/, 2 /*npiDmParamInst*/ )
u1 /*npiDmInstance*/
( w1/*npiDmPortInst*/, w2/*npiDmPortInst*/ );
mm ( .P2( 1 ) /*npiDmParamInst*/, .P1( 2 ) /*npiDmParamInst*/ )
u2 /*npiDmInstance*/
( .bb( w3 ) /*npiDmPortInst*/, .aa( w4 ) /*npiDmPortInst*/ );
assign top.u1.cc = 1'b1;

* Apply method "npiDmDefine" to the handle "u1", and the npiDmModule handle "mm" is
* Apply method "npiDmLeft" to the handle "inst_ary", and the npiDmConstant handle "1"
* Apply method "npiDmRight" to the handle "inst_ary", and the npiDmConstant handle "0"
* Apply method "npiDmParameter" to the handle ".P2( 1 )", and the npiDmParameter
handle "P2" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmPort" to the handle ".bb( w3 )", and the npiDmPort handle "bb" is
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle ".bb( w3 )", and the npiDmNet handle "w3" is
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the npiDmPortInst "w5" in the "b1", and the
npiDmHierRef handle "w5" without actual object is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmUse" to the handle "u1", and the npiDmContAssign handle
"assign top.u1.cc = 1'b1;" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmArray" to the handle "inst_ary", and "1" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmBindInst" to the handle "b1", and "1" is returned.

Interface
Object Type: npiDmInterface

Interface means the construct between SystemVerilog keywords interface and
endinterface. It belongs to the class Scope.
Limitation: Currently, no method exists to access all instantiations of an
interface.

interface itf; /*npiDmInterface*/
modport MASTER ( input a, output b );
modport SLAVE ( output a, input b );
interface eitf; /*npiDmInterface*/
bi b; /*typo*/

* Apply method "npiDmModport" to the handle "itf", and the npiDmModport handles
"MASTER" and "SLAVE" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmError" to handle "eitf", and "1" is returned because "eitf" has the
compile error.
* Apply property "npiDmFile" to the handles "itf" and "eitf", and the absolute path of the
source file is returned.

Interface Reference
Object Type: npiDmItfRef

Interface reference means the internal connection of SystemVerilog interface port.
Limitation: No method to access the unpacked dimension of the interface
reference exists.

modport MP( input a );
module top( itf.MP i1 /*npiDmItfRef*/, interface i2 /*npiDmItfRef*/ );

* Apply method "npiDmInterface" to the handle "i1", and the npiDmInterface handle "itf" is
* Apply method "npiDmModport" to the handle "i1", and the npiDmModport handle "MP"
* Apply property "npiDmGeneric" to the handle "i2", and "1" is returned.

Modport, Port in Modport, Task/Function in Modport, Clocking in
Modport
Object Type: Modport (npiDmModport), Port in Modport (npiDmMpport), Task/
Function in Modport (npiDmMptf), Clocking in Modport (npiDmMpclocking)

Modport means the SystemVerilog construct modport in interface.
Property "npiDmMptfType" returns npiDmMptfType_e.

interface simple_bus;
logic i1;
clocking sb @(posedge clk);
endclocking
modport master /*npiDmModport*/ (

input i1 /*npiDmMpport*/,
import read /*npiDmMptf*/,
clocking sb /*npiDmMpclocking*/ );

);

Vh Loop
Object Type: npiDmVhWhile, npiDmVhFor

Vh Loop is a class composed of Loop(npiDmVhWhile) and For Loop(npiDmVhFor). A loop
statement includes a sequence of statements that is to be executed repeatedly, zero or
more times.

variable cnt: integer := 2;
-- npiDmVhWhile
loop1: loop
if_stmt1: if(cnt = 0) then -- npiDmVhIf
exit;
cnt := 0;
end loop loop1;
-- npiDmVhWhile
loop2: while (cnt > 0) loop
if_stmt2: if(cnt > 0) then -- npiDmVhIf

cnt := cnt - 1;
cnt := cnt + 1;
end loop loop2;
-- npiDmVhFor
loop3: for ii in 3 downto 0 loop
va: cnt := cnt + ii; -- npiDmVhVarAssign
end loop loop3;

Assert Coverage
Object Types: Assert Metric (npiCovAssertMetric), Assert (npiCovAssert), Cover
Property (npiCovCoverProperty), Cover Sequence (npiCovCoverSequence),
Success Bin (npiCovSuccessBin), Attempt Bin (npiCovAttemptBin), Failure
Bin (npiCovFailureBin), Vacuous Bin (npiCovVacuousBin), Incomplete Bin
(npiCovIncompleteBin) and Firstmatch Bin (npiCovFirstmatchBin).

Assert Metric collects all the assert, cover property and cover sequence handles.
Success bin means the hit count for assert, match count for cover property and all
matches count for cover sequence.

Attempt bin means the attempt count. Failure bin means the failure count for assert.
Vacuous bin means the vacuous success count for cover property. Incomplete bin means
the incomplete count.
Firstmatch bin means the first match count for cover sequence.

* Assert generates child bins: Success, attempt, failure and incomplete.
Cover property generates child bins: Success, attempt, vacuous and incomplete.
Cover sequence generates child bins: Success, attempt, firstmatch and incomplete.
* Cover information only shows in assert, cover property and cover sequence. The
property npiCoverable of them is 1.
The property npiCovCount of success bin determines its scope handle (assert, cover
property or cover sequence) covered or not. (the value of npiCovCovered).
* The property npiCovCount can be set for success bin, attempt bin, failure bin,
incomplete bin and firstmatch bin. Similarly, the count of success bin could affect the
property npiCovered and npiCovStatus of its scope handle.

N.A

Branch Coverage
Object Types: Branch Metric (npiCovBranchMetric), Branch (npiCovBranch), Branch
Bin (npiCovBranchBin), Branch Term (npiCovBranchTerm)

Branch Metric tracks the execution of conditional statements in the design code. Branch is
a section of block which contains the combination of conditional statements.
Branch Bin is a vector value taken on the branch term of the branch. Branch Term is the
composition of the branch.

Condition Coverage
Object Types: Condition Metric (npiCovConditionMetric), Condition
(npiCovCondition), Condition Bin (npiCovConditionBin), Condition Term
(npiCovConditionTerm)

Condition Metric monitors whether certain expressions and sub expressions in the design
code evaluate to true or false. Condition is a logical or bitwise expression.

Condition Bin is a vector value taken on the condition term of the expression. Condition
Term is the composition of the expression.

Coverage Database
Object Type: Database (npiCovDatabase), Test (npiCovTest), Test Info
(npiCovTestInfo)

Database represents the object loaded from a coverage database. It contains the
available tests and the top-level instances of the design.
Test represents the result of a single execution of a tool or the merged results of two or
more executions. It contains the coverage data which determine a coverage object is
covered or not.
Test Info represents the test information got from merged test.
To get the top-level instance, apply the method "npiCovInstance" to the database handle.
Only one database could be opened in a single process. If the application wants
to open another database, the original database should be closed first.

Covered Test
Object Type: Covered Test (npiCovCoveredTest)

Covered Test represents the test that covers the bin handle.

There are three tests: "t0", "t1", and "t2". The merged test of these three tests is "tm".
Cover bin "cbA" named "auto[0]" is covered by "t0" twice and "t2" three times. The pseudo
code for getting the covered tests would be like:
printf("Cover bin: %s is covered by\n", npi_cov_get_str(npiCovName,
cbA));
npiCovHandle ctItr = npi_cov_iter_start(npiCovCoveredTest, cbA, tm/*test
must be given*/);
npiCovHandle ct = NULL;
while ((ct = npi_cov_iter_next(ctItr))) {
printf(" %s (%d times)\n", npi_cov_get_str(npiCovName, ct),
npi_cov_get(npiCovCount, ct, tm));
}
npi_cov_iter_stop(ctItr);

Cover bin: auto[0] is covered by
t0 (2 times)
t1 (3 times)

1. One-to-many method npiCovCoveredTest must be applied to test handle when getting
iterator.
2. npiCovCount for covered test means the covered times for the associated bin handle.

Finite State Machine Coverage
Object Types: Fsm Metric (npiCovFsmMetric), Fsm (npiCovFsm), States
(npiCovStates), Transitions (npiCovTransitions), Sequences (npiCovSequences),
State Bin (npiCovStateBin), Transition Bin (npiCovTransBin), Sequence Bin
(npiCovSeqBin)

Fsm Metric tracks the states and transitions of the finite state machines recognized by
verification tools. Fsm represents a finite state machine logic.
States represents the possible states of the FSM. Transitions represents the possible
transitions of the FSM.
Sequences represents the possible sequence of the FSM. State Bin represents the
coverage object of a state.
Transition Bin represents the coverage object of a transition. Sequence Bin represents the
coverage object of a sequence.

Object Type: npiCovInstance

Instance represents the hierarchical structure of the design. Instance contains a variety of
metrics. The metric defines the method of the measurement.
To get the parent instance, apply the method "npiCovScope" to the instance handle. To get
the child instances, apply the method "npiCovInstance" to the instance handle.

npiCovDefInfo shows the instance's definition name plus the information of assigned

parameter value.

Line Coverage
Object Types: Line Metric (npiCovLineMetric), Block (npiCovBlock), Statement Bin
(npiCovStmtBin)

Line Metric tracks which statements in the design source code were executed during
simulation.
Block represents the section of code, contains statements. Statement Bin represents the
coverage object of a statement.

Power Coverage
Object Types: Power Domain (npiCovPowerDomain), Power Measure
(npiCovPowerMeasure), Power Metric (npiCovPowerMetric) and Covergroup
(npiCovCovergroup)

Power Domain is the power network defined by upf or cpf.

Power Measure is the measure unit under power domain to connect the covergroups for
power coverage estimation. Power Metric collects all the covergroups for power coverage
estimation.
Covergroup here mentions the covergroup whose purpose is to estimate power coverage.
These covergroups only appears under power metrics.

1. If coverage database generated by simulator contains low-power hierarchical
verification plan, power domains is generated from test. Otherwise, power metric is
generated from test directly.
2. For VCS, the option -power=coverage+dump_hvp needs to be applied to generate lowpower hierarchical verification plan.

N.A.

Toggle Coverage
Object Types: Toggle Metric (npiCovToggleMetric), Signal (npiCovSignal), Signal Bit
(npiCovSignalBit), Toggle Bin (npiCovToggleBin)

Toggle Metric monitors value changes on signal bits in the design. Signal represents a
multiple bit signal. The npiCovSize property is great than 1.
Signal Bit represents a bit signal. The npiCovSize property is great 1. Toggle Bin
represents a value change state of a signal bit. The npiCovToggleType property can be
"0a1" or "1a0".

generated from covergroup.
* The property npiCovCount can be set for cover bin, and it also affects the cover bin's

* Cover bin's property npiCovBinName and npiCovBinType are supported for the cover

* The property npiCovBinType returns npiCovAutoBin for auto-bin, npiCovUserBin for

event clk;
class A;
bit[1:0] a,b,c,d,e;
covergroup cg @(clk);
cpa : coverpoint a; /* coverpoint "cpa" will get 4 cover-bins due
to the bit size */
cpb : coverpoint b;
cpc : coverpoint c;
cr1 : cross cpa,cpb; /* cr1 can get coverpoints "cpa" and "cpb" by
1-to-many method "npiCovComponent" */
CR1 : cross cr1,cpc;
crossdXe : cross d, e {
bins bsub = binsof(d) intersect {0}; /* user defined bin whose
property npiCovBinName is "bsub" */
ignore_bins bignore = binsof(e) intersect {0}; /* ignore bin
whose property npiCovBinName is "bignore" */
}
endgroup
cg = new();
A a = new();
-> clk;
a.a = 2;
a.b = 0;
a.c = 1;
a.d = 1;
a.e = 1;
-> clk;
a.a = 1;
a.b = 2;
a.c = 0;
-> clk;
a.a = 3;
a.b = 1;
a.c = 2;
-> clk;
end
endprogram

VCS Database
Database represents the object loaded from the simulator database generated by VCS.
It contains compilation information, design statistics, simulation information and test
A simulation test means running simulation once.
The number of simv runs without cleaning the database equals the number of simulation
tests.

* The database handle is obtained by the npi_vcs_open API.
* npiVcsToolName is always "VCS".

Compilation
The compilation handle shows the compilation information from the database generated
by the VCS simulator.

* npiVcsResult returns 1 if the compilation result is successful; otherwise, returns 0.

Design Statistics
The Design statistics handle shows the basic design information like the module number
and all the module information.

* Module signifies the module definition in the design.

Simulation
The simulation handle contains the simulation information like simulation begin-time and
end-time. Combined with simulation test handle, the information in every simulation test
can also be obtained.

* Waveform signifies the waveform dumped by a specific system task.

Test
Test signifies the simulation test by simv. The execution times of simv is equal to the test
number. This information (test number) can be obtained by the npiVcsTestNo property
from design statistics (npiVcsDesignStats) handle.

N/A

Time is the handle to represent the time information from compilation or simulation. The
time format could be time_t or double.

* npiVcsFormat indicates what kind of value format npi_vcs_get_value should use.
Start time, finish time, and gen time use the npiVcsTimeVal format.
Elapsed time and cpu time use the npiVcsDoubleVal format.

Module represents the module definition in the design.

* npiVcsLength signifies the number of code lines for the module definition.

Waveform
Waveform represents the waveform dumping system task. The number of waveforms is
equal to the number of dumping system tasks.

* npiVcsSize signifies the size of the waveform file and the unit is KB.

Iterator is the container to save the handles obtained by one-to-many method.

* npiVcsSize signifies the number of handles that is iterated by this iterator.

HVP Plan
Plan represents the object loaded from hierarchical verification plan. The hierarchy
is composed of features. Plan defines some attributes, annotations and metrics for
estimating the coverage status.

Plan handle is obtained by API npi_hvp_load_plan.

Spec
Spec file for the hierarchical verification plan.

NA.

Attribute Declaration
Attribute declaration is declared under plan and used by features. Attribute declaration
contains four data type: integer, real, string and enum. The difference between attribute
and annotation is that attribute propagates the assigned value down to the child hierarchy
unless it is explicitly overridden at the plan or feature level.

attribute real fraction = 1.0; // attribute decl; npi_hvp_get_value
gets 1.0
annotationreal fractionAnn = 2.0;

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute decl gets the value assigned in its right-hand-side.

Annotation Declaration
Annotation declaration is declared under plan and used by features. Annotation
declaration contains four data type: integer, real, string and enum. The difference between
attribute and annotation is that attribute propagates the assigned value down to the child
hierarchy unless it is explicitly overridden at the plan or feature level.

annotation real fractionAnn = 2.0; //annotation decl;
npi_hvp_get_value gets 2.0

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute decl gets the value assigned in its right-hand-side.

Attribute assign represents the attribute value assign statement under plan.

fraction = 3.0; // attribute assign
fractionAnn= 5.0;

NA

fractionAnn = 5.0; //annotation assign

NPI Libraries is a set of libraries that extend the functionality of NPI Models. The goal is to
improve the NPI programmers' productivity by reducing reinvention-of-the-wheel.
The libraries are aimed at a wide range of NPI users and application domains. They
range from common design traversal applications like hierarchy tree dumping, module
annotation, signal driver/load tracing, to specific design flow enhancements like design
rule validation, design manipulation, and so on. Some special NPI Models programming
tricks are also included.
NPI Libraries covers both C/C++ APIs and Tcl commands. All of them are written using
NPI Models. They are open source. Users can download NPI Libraries and make
modifications as desired.

In SystemVerilog, the design hierarchy includes the following scopes:
* Instance (module instance, interface, or package).
* Task and function declaration.
* Named begin block.
* (unnamed) begin block.
* Named fork block.
* (unnamed) fork block.
* Generate scope for block.
In VHDL, the design hierarchy includes the following scopes:
* Instance (root, component, or package).
* Subprogram (procedure and function).
* Block.
* Generate (if-generate, for-generate, or case-generate).
The APIs "npi_hier_tree_dump_txt" and "npi_hier_tree_dump_csv" dumps the design
hierarchy.
The APIs in the prefix "npi_hier_tree_trv_" collects the handles (npiHandle) of the scopes
during the traversal of the design hierarchy.
The APIs "npi_hier_tree_trv", "npi_hier_trv_trv_register_cb", and "npi_hier_trv_reset_cb"
traverses the design hierarchy and execute the callback functions registered by the user.
The APIs "npi_nl_hier_tree_trv", "npi_nl_hier_trv_trv_register_cb", and
"npi_nl_hier_trv_reset_cb" traverses the design hierarchy and execute the callback
functions registered by the user.
All the APIs in this category are written based on the NPI Language Model and NPI Netlist

The Signal Library provides the APIs that are related to the design information of a signal
(variable or net). In general, the APIs can be classified into the following groups:
1. Trace the driver or load of a signal based on the NPI Language Model and NPI Netlist
2. Get the equivalent signals of a target signal.
3. Get the signal definition typespec of a target signal.
Driver/Load Tracing
The APIs with the prefix "npi_sv_trace" mean they function as tracing the driver or load of
a signal based on the NPI Language (SystemVerilog) Model.
The APIs with the prefix "npi_nl_trace" mean they function as tracing the driver or load of a
signal based on the NPI Netlist Model.
Equivalent Signals
The API "npi_get_equivalent_signal" obtains the net handles that are equivalent to the
target signal.
The two signals are defined as "equivalent" if they are only connected by the port/instport
of the module instances (for example, an instance whose cell type is npiNlModuleCell).
Signal Definition Typespec
The API "npi_get_signal_define_typespec" obtains the typespec handle that represents
the definition of the signal.
The API is written based on the NPI Language Model.

Limitations
1. All the APIs for tracing the drivers or loads of a signal based on NPI Language Model
does not work when the specified signal is located at the index or slice of a reference
module mm(ref bit ma);
bit [1:0] a;
mm m0(a[p]); // m0 port ma's higher connection a[p] that is a
ref-obj,
endmodule // if tracing p's load, a[p] is not shown in the results.

Description of Network Trace
Trace Network APIs are based on Netlist models. It contains three parts:
1. Trace network and generate network graph under user-specified criteria.
2. Report path according to current graph.
3. Clear network, delete whole graph. The first part is flexible. You can start tracing from a
port or a signal.
The endpoint can also be an instance or a signal. Some options support wildcard
patterns. In addition, you can set different properties.
Complexity of the graph by detail mode.
Stop condition when tracing.
Ports that you particularly want to observe( = link ports).
It also reports floating signals, constant-tied signals, and ports of top boundary
module.
Detail Mode Setting
By default, 0, the network graph contains the start ports and end ports, both sides of ports
of mapping module, link ports that you want to observe, the stop ports or instports and
literal net that meet the stop conditions.
1. Adding all past ports of module into the graph.
2. Adding all instports of instance from symbol library.

3. Adding all past ports of module, and the past instports from the passCellFile into the
graph.
Figure 52

Detail Mode Setting

There are a bunch of stop conditions for this system. You can specify the cell type of
instance that can be passed through, either with positive listing or negative listing. You can
also specify the module names that you want to stop tracing.
To prevent loop and complexity of the graph, it does not pass through flip-flops, and a
maximum tracing depth is also specified.
Further, a module ports mapping can be given to prevent tracing too deep into modules. It
simply jumps from input port to the corresponding output port while tracing.
The following section covers the map file mapping rules:
Basic Mapping Rules
Map file:
modName portA portB
1. If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
2. If trace to a bit portA[idx], it maps to portB[idx].
3. If trace to slice portA[lidx,ridx], it maps to slice portB[lidx:ridx]. (For example, portA [1:0]
maps to portB[1:0]).
4. If output port not existed, it stops tracing at input port and the port is listed in the result
5. If portB has size = 1, then any part of portA maps to portB. (for example, both portA[1]
and portA[1:0] maps to portB).

Extended Mapping Rules
Map file:
modName portA portB
modName portA[0] portB[2]
If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
If trace to portA[0], it maps to portB[2]. Since the map relation is specified.
If trace to portA[1], maps to portB[1] according to basic mapping rules.
Map file:
modName portA portB
modName portA[0] portB
If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
If trace to port portA[0], maps to portB. Since the map relation is specified.
If trace to port portA[1], maps to portB[1] according to basic mapping rules.
Map file:
modName portA portB[1]
If trace to portA, it maps to portB[1].
If trace to portA[idx], maps to portB[1].
If trace to portA[lidx:ridx], maps to portB[1].
The map is bidirectional. portB maps to portA, and the spec is also applicable.

setenv NPI_NL_TRACE_DUMP_STATUS 1 - Dump tracing status information.
setenv NPI_NL_TRACE_REG_PASS_DQ 1

Pass register from D to Q and reverse. You must be careful with this option because this
might increase the graph complexity significantly.

Since the NPI Netlist Model regards the design as a netlist after inference, the objects
in the Netlist model might have its specific name, which might not be their names in the
design source code.
In the Netlist model, the object name "nl_name" is called. The "nl_name" can be obtained
from the property npiNlName for that handle.
However, if you dump the nl_name into a file, it is difficult to recover the handle directly
from the nl_name.

APIs to get the handles from the nl_name:

instance port name of library cell.

more detailed information, refer to npi_nl_sig_handle_by_name.

Rules for Active Trace
When tracing an active driver/load from output/input pins of instances, different rules are
applied for different npiNlInstType
This section introduces the rules for Active Trace of every supported instance.

NPI VANL provides "Active Trace" functionality, which is a way to trace driver or load with
value. Active trace only happens when tracing driver from an instance output or tracing
load from an instance input.
It considers its npiNlCellType and the values of its inputs and outputs. You can trace
active drivers and then conveniently find the possible signals which are the root cause to
the value change of the target signal.
On the contrary, you can trace active loads whose values are mainly or partially affected
by the target signal.
The relationship between active driver and active load is mutual. If A and B are the active
drivers of O, then O must be the active load of A and B.
Rules for User Set Signals
Since VANL Library is based on NPI Netlist Model, user can set or define values on
npiNlNet, npiNlInstPort, and npiNlPort.
The user-defined or user-set signals are "value-tied" and they do not change their values
until user cleans or resets them. More importantly, they do NOT have any active driver.
For example, as shown in the figure below, if you set the value on npiNlNet top.a and
npiNlPort top.b (marked as blue words) and you try to recursively get the active drivers
from npiNlNet top.o after evaluation, you have npiNlInstport before npiNlNet top.a
(pointed out by the black arrow) and npiNlPort top.b, if their values formed the value of
npiNlNet top.o.

Rules for npiNlSymbolLibInst
For npiNlSymbolLibInst, extract its npiNlFunc, npiNlXFunc, and npiNlThreeStateFunc.
According to these function-strings, the active drivers can be evaluated.
FN04D2 oai2 (ZN, A1, A2, B1, B2)

npiNlFunc:
!((A1&A2)|(B1&B2))

When A1=1, A2=0, B1=0, and B2=1, the active drivers of ZN are A2 and B1 because
the value of output ZN is caused by its input (A1&A2) = 0 and (B1&B2) = 0, which are
caused by A2 and B1 respectively.

This program recursively traces the driver with value and the value of each signal after
propagation is shown in the preceding Schematic.
At first stage, you want to trace active driver recursively from top.w1. The active driver of
top.w1 would be top.w2 and top.w3 is dropped because the value of top.w1 is X, and
the possible driver to cause this is only top.w2 with value X.
Due to similar reason, the active driver of top.w2 would be top.w7 and top.w9, since the
value X of top.w2 is caused by mux input top.w7 and the control pin top.w9, which are X
and 1, respectively.
Since the value on net is set in this example, on tracing you get
npiNlInstport top.top:Always0SigOp0:2:2:Mux.CH_w9 and
top.top:Always0SigOp0:2:2:Mux.IH_w7 before those net.
Secondly, user traces the active driver of top.w3, the output of an npiNlOrCell, with value
1.
The possible drivers that caused this 1 are signals whose value is also 1, thus get top.w5
and top.w6.
Since the value on net is set in this example, thus when tracing you
get npiNlInstPort top.top:Always1SigOp1:3:3:Or.IH_w5 and
top.top:Always1SigOp1:3:3:Or.IH_w6 before those net.

User Interface and Use Flow
The following figure shows the flow of using NPI Transaction Writer APIs:

Firstly, the new instance of the npi_tr_writer class needs to be created with the provided
instance path. The instance path specifies the scope to which all the objects created
through this instance belong.
Secondly, you can create any objects by the APIs of writer instance.
It is allowed to have multiple writer instances to dump the objects into the
same FSDB file, so the objects under different paths appear in one FSDB file
accordingly.
The relationship with another object can be set through the related relationship APIs. In
this model, there are two main relationships:
* Parent and child (children).
* Predecessor and successor (successors).

The two objects belonging to two different writer instances can be set as predecessor and
successor (successors) by calling the corresponding APIs and specifying the successor's
writer instance.
The attributes with different values and data types can be added. The allowed data types
are bit, bit vector, integer, real (double), time (64 bits unsigned integer), and string.
You can also set the expected attribute and if the attribute is not equal to the expected
attribute, it is highlighted in Protocol Analyzer.
To end an object creation, theend_object() method can be used for a specified object.
The ended object cannot be modified after it ends using this API.
To end all of the not ended objects, the flush_writer() API can be used, which ends all the
objects and dumps them into the FSDB file.

Illegal Cases for Object ID
The object ID is defined as const char*.
The following are some illegal cases for the provided object ID:
* The NULL pointer is provided.
* The object ID is not created by the create_object() API.
An error message is issued if these conditions are violated and the API that calls these
illegal cases becomes invalid.

Using npiSocketClient in C/C++ Programming
Include "npi_util.h" in your C/C++ program when using npiSocketClient.
The following is an example showing how to use npiSocketClient to connect to a server
process, Novas executable, and call Novas Tcl commands with the program.
In the program, a process is forked to invoke the Novas executable. Then a
npiSocketClient handle is created and connected to Novas.
Finally, several Novas Tcl commands are called to load an FSDB and display signals in
nWave.

<unistd.h>

void abortCB(void* cbData)
{
printf("Socket connection is broken\n");
}
{

// 1. get free port
int port = npi_socket_client_get_free_port();
if( !npi_socket_client_is_port_free(port) ) {
printf("Error. Fail to get a free port.\n");
}
// 2. invoke novas executable
pid_t pid = fork();
if( pid<0 ) {
printf("Error. Fail to fork a process to invoke Novas.\n");
}
if(pid == 0) { //child process
// the argument argc and argv is the options of Novas executable
// to invoke Novas with a port, we need to run Novas by the commands
below:
//
// novas -serverPort <free_port> <original_novas_load_design_options>
int new_argc = argc + 3;
char** new_argv = (char**) malloc(sizeof(char*)*new_argc);
// set the argument : novas -serverPort <free_port>
new_argv[0] = "novas";
new_argv[1] = "-serverPort";
static char buf[256];
sprintf(buf, "%d", port);
new_argv[2] = buf;
// keep original novas load design options except argv[0], which is
the executable name
for(int i=1; i<argc; i++) {
new_argv[2+i] = argv[i];
}
// final argument must be NULL
new_argv[new_argc-1] = 0;

}

// invoke novas with server port
if( !execvp(new_argv[0], new_argv) ) {
printf("Error. Fail to invoke Novas.\n");
}

// 3. connect novas by npiSocketClient handle
npiSocketClient socket_client_hdl = npi_socket_client_construct();
if( !npi_socket_client_connect(socket_client_hdl, port, NULL/*Local
host*/, 60/*timeout*/) ) {
npi_socket_client_destroy(socket_client_hdl);

}

printf("Error. Fail to connect Novas.\n");

char* err_msg;
int is_conn = npi_socket_client_check_connect(socket_client_hdl,
&err_msg);

The npiArg APIs are used to facilitate processing the arguments passed into a C program
(argv). In npiArg, argv arguments are defined as a set of attributes with their associated
values.
An attribute is a string beginning with a minus (-) or plus (+). Anything that follows an
attribute before another attribute begins are the values associated with the preceding
npiArg APIs provide routines to get, add, or remove attributes as well their associated

Parse User-Defined Arguments in NPI C/C++ Programming
In the introduction to Use NPI Libraries in C/C++, the use of an NPI program is similar to
the following:
%> my_NPI_program.exe <novas import design options> <NPI options> <user
options>

To parse <user options> in the NPI program, npiArg can be a very convenient utility. For
example, assume an NPI program needs the user options "-input_signal signal_name".
%> my_npi_program.exe -f run.f -path ./Design -input_signal
"system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.carry_mode"

The following code snippet shows how to use npiArg to parse such a user option:

include "npi_util.h" // for npiArg
{
// parse the user options by npiUSN
int new_argc = 0;
char** new_argv = NULL;
string input_signal;
npiArg arg = npi_arg_construct(argc, argv);
if( npi_arg_has_attr(arg, "-input_signal") ) { // parse the attribute
"-input_signal"
// record the signal name specified in the "-input_signal" attribute
input_signal = npi_arg_attr_get_value(arg, "-input_signal",
1/*position*/);
// remove the "-input_signal" attribute and output new_argc and new_argv
for npi_init()
npi_arg_remove_attr(arg, "-input_signal");
new_argc = npi_arg_get_argc(arg);
new_argv = npi_arg_get_argv(arg);
}
printf("ERROR. Fail to find the argument \"-input_signal\"\n");
}
// now you can pass new_argc and new_argv to npi_init()
if( !npi_init(new_argc, new_argv) )

// close the npiArg
npi_arg_destroy(arg);
}

As shown in the above code snippets, npiArg can be used to retrieve the values of userdefined arguments while leaving the other arguments for npi_init() and npi_load_design()
alone.

Universal Scope Name
npiUSN is used to create a Universal Scope Name representation for hierarchical scopes
in SystemVerilog and VHDL.
As different tools have their own convention for SystemVerilog and VHDL scope names,
the npiUSN APIs convert different scope representations into a unified format thus making
it easier to use the scopes in NPI.
SystemVerilog and VHDL escape names are handled automatically.

The npiUSN handle. (used in C/C++).

Construct a npiUSN handle with a hierarchical string and a
delimiter.

npi_usn_destroy

Destroy a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_push_back

Append a scope to the end of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_pop_back

Remove the last scope from a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_back

Get the last scope name of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_set_delimiter

Change the delimiter of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_delimiter

Get the current delimiter of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_is_empty

Check whether any scopes exist for a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_number

Get the total number of scopes of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_scope_name
_at

Get the scope name at the specified position of a npiUSN

ame
